### Smoky Mountain and early career (1994–1997)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Smoky Mountain and early career (1994–1997)")]

See also: [The Gangstas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Gangstas "The Gangstas")

Connor began his wrestling career in [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey") as "Ace the Animal". He then wrestled [Earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthquake_(wrestler) "Earthquake (wrestler)") in the [World Wrestling Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wrestling_Federation "World Wrestling Federation") (WWF) in 1994 under his given name as a [jobber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Job_(professional_wrestling)#Jobbers "Job (professional wrestling)").

Connor debuted in [Smoky Mountain Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoky_Mountain_Wrestling "Smoky Mountain Wrestling") in September 1994 as "A.C. Conner". In October 1994, he was renamed "'Downtown' D'Lo Brown" and introduced as the head of security for [the Gangstas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Gangstas "The Gangstas") ([Mustapha Saed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mustapha_Saed "Mustapha Saed") and [New Jack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jack "New Jack")). Brown was the [worker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worker_(professional_wrestling) "Worker (professional wrestling)") of the [stable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_(professional_wrestling) "Stable (professional wrestling)"), complementing Saed's size and Jack's animated personality. He regularly wrestled on [Smoky Mountain Wrestling's television show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoky_Mountain_Wrestling "Smoky Mountain Wrestling"), unsuccessfully challenged for the [SMW Beat the Champ Television Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SMW_Beat_the_Champ_Television_Championship "SMW Beat the Champ Television Championship") on several occasions. At Sunday Bloody Sunday II in February 1995, the Gangstas lost to the [Heavenly Bodies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavenly_Bodies_(1990s_tag_team) "Heavenly Bodies (1990s tag team)") and [Jim Cornette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Cornette "Jim Cornette"). At Bluegrass Brawl III in April 1995, the Gangstas lost to [Tracy Smothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracy_Smothers "Tracy Smothers") and [The Undertaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Undertaker "The Undertaker") in a [handicap match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handicap_match "Handicap match"). Brown wrestled his final match for Smoky Mountain Wrestling in October 1995.

After leaving Smoky Mountain Wrestling, Brown signed a deal with the WWF and was sent to the [Heartland Wrestling Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland_Wrestling_Association "Heartland Wrestling Association") for more training while also making appearances as a jobber on WWF television. Brown also spent most of 1996 wrestling in [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico") for the [World Wrestling Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wrestling_Council "World Wrestling Council").

### World Wrestling Federation / World Wrestling Entertainment (1997–2003)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: World Wrestling Federation / World Wrestling Entertainment (1997–2003)")]

#### Nation of Domination (1997–1998)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Nation of Domination (1997–1998)")]

Main article: [Nation of Domination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nation_of_Domination "Nation of Domination")

In April 1997, Brown was reintroduced to the World Wrestling Federation (WWF) as a member of [Faarooq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Simmons "Ron Simmons")'s [heel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heel_(professional_wrestling) "Heel (professional wrestling)")[Nation of Domination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nation_of_Domination "Nation of Domination")[stable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Stable "Glossary of professional wrestling terms"), debuting as one of several non-descript people in suits that accompanied the group to the ring. During this time, his most notable moment was when [Ahmed Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Johnson "Ahmed Johnson") slammed him onto the roof of a car during _[Shotgun Saturday Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shotgun\_Saturday\_Night "Shotgun Saturday Night")_. His first televised match as a member of the Nation was on the April 26, 1997, episode of _Shotgun Saturday Night_, as he, [Crush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crush_(wrestler) "Crush (wrestler)"), and [Savio Vega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savio_Vega "Savio Vega") defeated [Aldo Montoya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldo_Montoya "Aldo Montoya"), [Steve Corino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Corino "Steve Corino"), and [Freddie Joe Floyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Joe_Floyd "Freddie Joe Floyd"). On May 26, 1997, he had his first match on _[Raw is War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raw\_is\_War "Raw is War")_, defeating [Bob "Spark Plugg" Holly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_%22Spark_Plugg%22_Holly "Bob \"Spark Plugg\" Holly"). After the [King of the Ring 1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_the_Ring_1997 "King of the Ring 1997"), Faarooq fired the rest of the Nation's members, except for D-Lo, who was later joined by [Ahmed Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Johnson "Ahmed Johnson") (later replaced by [Rocky Maivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Maivia "Rocky Maivia")), [Kama Mustafa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kama_Mustafa "Kama Mustafa"), and [Mark Henry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Henry "Mark Henry").

In early 1998, the Nation of Domination [turned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Turn "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") on Faarooq, allowing Maivia, now going by the name "The Rock", to assume leadership. During this period Kama also changed his name to "The Godfather" and began portraying a pimp character. Brown and Henry eventually turned on both Rock and Godfather separately, moving into a feud with the Rock before finally branching out as a moderately successful [tag team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tag_team "Tag team"), later turning [face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face_(professional_wrestling) "Face (professional wrestling)") along the way. Prior to the face turn, Brown had started wrestling with a chest protector, supposedly for a torn [pectoral muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pectoral_muscle "Pectoral muscle") sustained in a match against [Dan "The Beast" Severn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_%22The_Beast%22_Severn "Dan \"The Beast\" Severn"). Instead, he used the chest protector to his advantage, making his finishing move, the [Lo Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lo_Down "Lo Down"), more effective.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-7)

#### Title pursuit (1998–2000)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Title pursuit (1998–2000)")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/D%27Lo_Brown_in_Birmingham.jpg/250px-D%27Lo_Brown_in_Birmingham.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:D'Lo_Brown_in_Birmingham.jpg)

Brown in the late 1990s

In 1998, he feuded with [X-Pac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Pac "X-Pac") over the [WWF European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWF_European_Championship "WWF European Championship"). His career peaked when he held the [European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE_European_Championship "WWE European Championship") and [Intercontinental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE_Intercontinental_Championship "WWE Intercontinental Championship") Championships simultaneously during a feud with [Jeff Jarrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Jarrett "Jeff Jarrett") and Mark Henry. This feat has only been duplicated by [Jeff Jarrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Jarrett "Jeff Jarrett"), [Kurt Angle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Angle "Kurt Angle"), and [Rob Van Dam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Van_Dam "Rob Van Dam"), all of whom became [world champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling_championship#World_championships "Professional wrestling championship") in some form, later in their careers.

Brown was involved in inadvertently ending the career of [Droz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Droz_(wrestler) "Droz (wrestler)") on October 5, 1999, when a [running powerbomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Powerbomb#Sit-Out_Powerbomb "Powerbomb") was [botched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botch_(professional_wrestling) "Botch (professional wrestling)") due to Droz's baggy shirt. The match was filmed for the October 7 edition of _[SmackDown!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Friday\_Night\_SmackDown "WWE Friday Night SmackDown")_, but was never aired. Droz suffered a severe neck injury, rendering him a [quadriplegic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadriplegia "Quadriplegia").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-PowerSlam109-6) During an interview with Title Match Wrestling, Brown dispelled a popular rumor that a fan had thrown an object into the ring which caused him to slip and badly injure Darren Drozdov. Brown took responsibility for botching the move, stating that the accident could have happened to "any" wrestler he had been in the ring with that night. He also said the accident caused him to "wrestle differently" and to second guess every move he performed in the ring from that day forward.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-8) Drozdov maintained that he did not blame Brown for his injuries and believed the incident was an accident.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-9)

During the rest of the year and into some of the next, Brown became an ally of former fellow Nation member The Godfather, emulating his dress and walking motions. The teaming ended when Brown turned heel on the Godfather.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-PowerSlam109-6)

#### Lo Down (2000–2001)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Lo Down (2000–2001)")]

Brown then formed a tag team in July 2000 with [Chaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosh_(wrestler) "Mosh (wrestler)") named _Lo Down_. The team mostly wrestled on _[Sunday Night Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Heat "WWE Heat")_ and _[WWE Jakked / Metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Jakked\_/\_Metal "WWE Jakked / Metal")_. Shortly after the team formed, [Tiger Ali Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiger_Ali_Singh "Tiger Ali Singh") joined the team to become their [manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manager_(professional_wrestling) "Manager (professional wrestling)"). The tag team then came dressed towards the ring in [Sikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh "Sikh") attire and took on a [gimmick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Gimmick "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") very similar to Tiger's.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-PowerSlam109-6) The team was removed from WWF [television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television "Television") in January 2001 after Singh was injured.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-swervepodcast-10) According to Brown, it was the lowest point in his career. Brown also spent six months in Puerto Rico wrestling for the [International Wrestling Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Wrestling_Association_(Puerto_Rico) "International Wrestling Association (Puerto Rico)") teaming with Chaz. He later teamed with Glamour Boy Shane holding the IWA tag team titles.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-swervepodcast-10)

#### OVW and Heartland (2001–2002)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: OVW and Heartland (2001–2002)")]

Chaz and Singh were later released by WWF that year, Brown stayed in WWE's [developmental territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling#Farm_team "Professional wrestling"), OVW. Notably, Brown wrestled future World champion [Batista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Batista "Dave Batista") in a losing effort. He also worked for [Heartland Wrestling Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland_Wrestling_Association "Heartland Wrestling Association") going into 2002.

#### Alliance with Theodore Long (2002–2003)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Alliance with Theodore Long (2002–2003)")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/D%27lo_Brown%2C_2002.jpg/250px-D%27lo_Brown%2C_2002.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:D'lo_Brown,_2002.jpg)

Brown in September 2002

Brown returned to television on the April 28, 2002, episode of _Heat_, losing to [Eddie Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Guerrero "Eddie Guerrero"). For the rest of the year, Brown mostly wrestled on _Heat_, did a little bit of commentary on the show, and even started a brief feud with [Raven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raven_(wrestler) "Raven (wrestler)"). In late 2002, [Theodore Long](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Long "Theodore Long") retired as a WWE [referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referee_(professional_wrestling) "Referee (professional wrestling)") and managed D'Lo, who had complained about acts of [racism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racism "Racism") during his matches. D'Lo started Long's group Thuggin' and Buggin' Enterprises which eventually turned into a group of African Americans who worked an angle in which they felt they were victims of racism and were being held down by the "white man". With Long's managerial services, D'Lo Brown went undefeated for several weeks.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-PowerSlam109-6)

Brown faced [Booker T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Booker_T_(wrestler) "Booker T (wrestler)") in a losing effort on the February 10, 2003, episode of _[Raw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Raw "WWE Raw")_. His involvement with Thuggin' and Buggin' Enterprises was brought to a close when footage was shown on the February 16 episode (taped February 10) of _Heat_ of Theodore Long kicking D'Lo Brown to the curb and introducing his replacement [Rodney Mack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodney_Begnaud "Rodney Begnaud").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-PowerSlam109-6) He was then released from his WWE contract on February 14, 2003.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-PowerSlam109-6)

### NWA Total Nonstop Action (2003–2004)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: NWA Total Nonstop Action (2003–2004)")]

Connor, still under the D'Lo Brown name, Joined [NWA Total Nonstop Action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NWA_Total_Nonstop_Action "NWA Total Nonstop Action") in March 2003. During his time in TNA, he teamed with [AJ Styles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AJ_Styles "AJ Styles") on many occasions together even challenging for the NWA World Tag Team Championships but were unsuccessful. After the team split up Brown challenged Styles for the [NWA World Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NWA_World_Heavyweight_Championship "NWA World Heavyweight Championship") but came up short on every occasion doing a best of 3 series.

On the March 19, 2003, edition of NWA-TNA, Brown teamed with [Dusty Rhodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dusty_Rhodes "Dusty Rhodes") and [Jeff Jarrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Jarrett "Jeff Jarrett") defeating [Erik Watts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erik_Watts "Erik Watts"), [Brian Lawler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Lawler "Brian Lawler") and [David Flair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Flair "David Flair").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-11) On April 2, 2003, edition of NWA-TNA weekly pay-per view D'Lo Brown unsuccessfully challenged Jeff Jarrett for the [NWA World Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NWA_World_Heavyweight_Championship "NWA World Heavyweight Championship").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-12) On April 14, 2004, Brown and [Gran Apolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran_Apolo "Gran Apolo") won the [NWA World Tag Team Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NWA_World_Tag_Team_Championship "NWA World Tag Team Championship") defeating [Kid Kash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kid_Kash "Kid Kash") and [Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lance_Archer "Lance Archer"), They lost the titles just seven days after winning them.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-13) D'Lo later left TNA in the summer of 2004.

On a September 2014 interview, Brown said there was a time in TNA during this time where the creative team wanted to radically change his character; on top of not feeling like he was a good fit with TNA, Brown felt that by wrestling in Japan, he could still wrestle there while being D'Lo Brown.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-swervepodcast-10)

### All Japan Pro Wrestling and overseas (2004–2009)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: All Japan Pro Wrestling and overseas (2004–2009)")]

Brown Joined [All Japan Pro Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Japan_Pro_Wrestling "All Japan Pro Wrestling"), competing in regular tours with the Japanese company as a member of [Roughly Obsess and Destroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roughly_Obsess_and_Destroy "Roughly Obsess and Destroy") (RO&D).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-PowerSlam109-6) During one of these tours on September 17, 2006, Brown betrayed RO&D to join the rival [Voodoo Murders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voodoo_Murders "Voodoo Murders") faction. Brown left All Japan in 2007 and rejoined [RO&D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roughly_Obsess_and_Destroy "Roughly Obsess and Destroy") in [Pro Wrestling Noah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Wrestling_Noah "Pro Wrestling Noah").

When not in Japan, Brown was regularly found touring the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), as well as working for [Irish Whip Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Whip_Wrestling "Irish Whip Wrestling") in [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland "Ireland"). In April 2005, Brown became one of the lead trainers of the ill-fated _[Celebrity Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity\_Wrestling "Celebrity Wrestling")_ on [ITV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_(TV_network) "ITV (TV network)"). This Saturday evening [reality show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reality_television "Reality television") saw [celebrities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity "Celebrity") learn wrestling and compete in challenge matches. After a few weeks the programme was to be canceled, but was instead moved to Sunday mornings to finish its final episodes. During his time wrestling in [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England "England"), he would face off in a series of matches against his _Celebrity Wrestling_ opposition's trainer, [Joe Legend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Hitchen "Joe Hitchen").

### Return to WWE (2008–2009)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Return to WWE (2008–2009)")]

In 2008, Brown began wrestling in a number of [dark matches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Dark_match "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") for WWE. On June 5, WWE announced that Brown had been signed to a contract, and he began working more dark matches for the company.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-14) He made his television return on the July 21, 2008, edition of _[Raw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Raw "WWE Raw")_, defeating [Santino Marella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santino_Marella "Santino Marella"). Following this, Brown's appearances on television became more sporadic, and on January 9, 2009, it was announced on WWE's website that he had been released from his WWE contract due to cost-cutting measures.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-15)

### Independent circuit (2009–2010)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Independent circuit (2009–2010)")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/D_Lo_Brown_in_2009_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-D_Lo_Brown_in_2009_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:D_Lo_Brown_in_2009_(cropped).jpg)

Brown in 2009

Brown debuted for [Ring of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_Honor "Ring of Honor") during Proving Ground 09 weekend in February. He was defeated by [Nigel McGuinness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_McGuinness "Nigel McGuinness") in an [ROH World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ROH_World_Championship "ROH World Championship") match. He also wrestled at the [ROH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_Honor "Ring of Honor") 7th Anniversary Show on March 21, 2009, in Manhattan, defeating [Jay Briscoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Briscoe "Jay Briscoe"). Brown also appeared on _[Ring of Honor Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring\_of\_Honor\_Wrestling "Ring of Honor Wrestling")_ on [HDNet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HDNet "HDNet"). Varsity Pro Wrestling also announced that Brown would be making his third appearance for the promotion on their February tour. Brown also made a surprise appearance in [Chikara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chikara_(professional_wrestling) "Chikara (professional wrestling)"), where he filled in as a substitute for Iceberg of The Cold Front at the [2009 King of Trios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Trios#2009 "King of Trios") tournament. Brown came up short in an [ROH World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ROH_World_Championship "ROH World Championship") match at [Take No Prisoners (2009)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take_No_Prisoners_(2009) "Take No Prisoners (2009)"). At ROH's Manhattan Mayhem III on June 13, Brown tapped out to [Colt Cabana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colt_Cabana "Colt Cabana") in a four-way match also involving [Bryan Danielson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Danielson "Bryan Danielson") and [Claudio Castagnoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cesaro_(wrestler) "Cesaro (wrestler)"). On June 27 on an [ROH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_Honor "Ring of Honor") show he was defeated by Cabana.

Throughout April and May 2009, Brown flew to [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan") to take part in the 13-night [Pro Wrestling Noah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Wrestling_Noah "Pro Wrestling Noah") Global Tag League with his partner [Buchanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Buchanan "Barry Buchanan"). During the course of the event they won and lost three matches with one contest went to a draw giving them seven points placing them sixth of the eight teams.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-noahtourn09-16) Outside of the tournament Brown was undefeated in six-man tag team competition, adding [Keith Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Walker_(wrestler) "Keith Walker (wrestler)") to the team, including a victory over Noah founder [Mitsuharu Misawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitsuharu_Misawa "Mitsuharu Misawa") in one of his last matches.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-noah09-17)

On the September 15, 2009, edition of _Between The Ropes_, Brown announced that after his current tour with [Ring of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_Honor "Ring of Honor"), he would retire from in-ring action. Also, on this edition of Between The Ropes, Brown announced he would become a semi-regular co-host when his [TNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_Nonstop_Action_Wrestling "Total Nonstop Action Wrestling") scheduling allowed him to be in studio.

He defeated [Mr. Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Anderson_(wrestler) "Ken Anderson (wrestler)") on June 12, 2010, TCW event in Pine Bluff, Arkansas. He did not wrestle again until 2013.

### Return to TNA (2009–2013)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Return to TNA (2009–2013)")]

Main article: [Aces & Eights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aces_&_Eights "Aces & Eights")

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/D_Lo_Brown_2013.jpg/250px-D_Lo_Brown_2013.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:D_Lo_Brown_2013.jpg)

D'Lo Brown as a member of Aces & Eights

In September 2009, Connor was re-signed by TNA as their lead [agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Agent "Glossary of professional wrestling terms"). Additionally, D'Lo was in charge of talent development and acquisitions heading up the [TNA Gut Check](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TNA_Gut_Check "TNA Gut Check") program.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-18)

On the March 7, 2013, episode of _Impact Wrestling_, Brown attacked Kurt Angle and revealed himself as the Vice President of [Aces & Eights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aces_&_Eights "Aces & Eights"), turning heel in the process.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-pwtorch.com-19) Three days later at [Lockdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockdown_(2013) "Lockdown (2013)"), Brown interfered in Angle's steel cage match against fellow Aces & Eights member [Wes Brisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Brisco "Wes Brisco"), costing Angle the match. Later that evening, the President of the Aces & Eights was revealed to be [Bully Ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bully_Ray "Bully Ray").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-pwtorch.com-19) Brown wrestled his first televised match in four years on the May 2 episode of _Impact Wrestling_, losing to Kurt Angle in an I Quit Match.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-20) As a result of his loss, Brown was demoted to a prospect the following week. On July 17, Brown announced he was released from his TNA contract.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-Waldmanrelease-1)

### Return to AJPW (2013)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Return to AJPW (2013)")]

On August 11, 2013, All Japan Pro Wrestling announced that Brown would be returning to the promotion the following month to take part in the [2013 Ōdō Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%8Cd%C5%8D_Tournament#2013 "Ōdō Tournament").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-21) Brown returned to the promotion on September 11 in a non-tournament tag team match, where he and [Bambi Killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Raaber "Chris Raaber") defeated [Burning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_(professional_wrestling) "Burning (professional wrestling)") ([Atsushi Aoki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atsushi_Aoki "Atsushi Aoki") and [Yoshinobu Kanemaru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoshinobu_Kanemaru "Yoshinobu Kanemaru")), with Brown pinning Kanemaru for the win.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-22) Three days later, Brown was eliminated by Kanemaru in his first round match in the Ōdō Tournament.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-23) For the rest of the tour, which lasted until September 23, Brown worked [midcard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Card "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") tag team matches, suffering pinfall losses in most of them.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-27) On October 3, Brown was announced also for All Japan's next tour, which started October 12.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-28) Brown continued teaming regularly with Bambi Killer, which eventually led to the two forming a heel stable named [DK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_Kingdom_(professional_wrestling) "Dark Kingdom (professional wrestling)") (Dark Kingdom) under the leadership of [Kenso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenzo_Suzuki "Kenzo Suzuki") on November 21.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-30)

### Return to Independent circuit (2013–2023)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Return to Independent circuit (2013–2023)")]

After working for TNA, Brown returned to the independent circuit where he appeared for Pro Wrestling Syndicate on May 18, 2013, with [D.O.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drew_Hankinson "Drew Hankinson") and [Knux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Knox "Mike Knox").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-31) On August 3, 2013, Brown and Hankinson lost to the [Rock N' Roll Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_N'_Roll_Express "Rock N' Roll Express") at Mid-Atlantic Wrestling Legends Fanfest. By the end of the year he worked in England and the Netherlands.

On November 22, 2014, Brown would team with former WWE wrestler [Bull Buchanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bull_Buchanan "Bull Buchanan") defeating AJ Steele and Brad Lynch at Buchanan's retirement show at UIW in Bowden, Georgia.

He lost to [Sabu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabu_(wrestler) "Sabu (wrestler)") at XICW Bodyslams Childhood Cancer event in Wyandotte, Michigan, on July 29, 2017. On October 27, 2018, he won the vacated HLW Legends Title defeating Dru Skillz in Fort Wayne, Indiana. He dropped the title to [Tracy Smothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracy_Smothers "Tracy Smothers") on April 20, 2019.

Brown's last match was on October 7, 2023, for Border City Wrestling in which he along with [Scott D'Amore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_D'Amore "Scott D'Amore") and [Tommy Dreamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Dreamer "Tommy Dreamer") defeated the team of [Johnny Swinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Swinger "Johnny Swinger"), N8 Mattson and Tyler Tirva.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-32)

### Future Stars of Wrestling (2014–2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Future Stars of Wrestling (2014–2015)")]

Brown formerly held a weekly class on Friday for "Future Stars of Wrestling" training center in Las Vegas.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-swervepodcast-10)

### Return to Impact / Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (2019–present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Return to Impact / Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (2019–present)")]

On July 3, 2019, Brown announced that he had returned to [Impact Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_Wrestling "Impact Wrestling") with a multi-year contract as a [producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_agent_(professional_wrestling) "Road agent (professional wrestling)").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-33) Brown and Mr Anderson were scheduled to represent the [Aces & Eights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aces_&_Eights "Aces & Eights") at [TNA: There's No Place Like Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TNA:_There's_No_Place_Like_Home "TNA: There's No Place Like Home") but the event was annulled due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-34)

In January 2021, it was announced that Brown would be one half of Impact's new announce team with Matt Striker from Hard to Kill onward. The role ended in early 2022 when [Honor No More](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honor_No_More "Honor No More") attacked him. His role was replaced by [Matt Rehwoldt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Rehwoldt "Matt Rehwoldt").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-36)

Brown returned as part of the reunited [Aces & Eights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aces_&_Eights "Aces & Eights"), managing [Garett Bischoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garett_Bischoff "Garett Bischoff") and [Wes Brisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Brisco "Wes Brisco"), in a losing effort against Honor No More's [Kenny King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_King_(wrestler) "Kenny King (wrestler)") and [Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinny_Marseglia "Vinny Marseglia"). The reunion would later be a one-off, as Brown continued to his Talent Relations role backstage and makes occasional appearances thereafter.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-40)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Connor holds an accounting degree from the [University of Maine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Maine "University of Maine"). He also played for the [football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Black_Bears_football "Maine Black Bears football") while attending university. He worked as a [Certified Public Accountant (CPA)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certified_Public_Accountant "Certified Public Accountant") before he began his wrestling career.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-OWW-2)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-41)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-IMDb-3) He and his wife Jennifer were married in 2001 and have two daughters. He has three half siblings on his dad's side. He is a fan of the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears") and [Liverpool F.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.")

**Accie Julius Connor** (born October 22, 1973), better known by his [ring name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_name "Ring name")**D'Lo Brown** (also formatted as **D-Lo Brown**), is an American [professional wrestler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestler "Professional wrestler"). He is signed to [Total Nonstop Action Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_Nonstop_Action_Wrestling "Total Nonstop Action Wrestling") (TNA), where he works as a [producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_agent_(professional_wrestling) "Road agent (professional wrestling)"). He is best known for his time with [WWE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE "WWE"). Brown is also known for his appearances in [Ring of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_Honor "Ring of Honor") (ROH), [All Japan Pro Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Japan_Pro_Wrestling "All Japan Pro Wrestling") (AJPW), [Irish Whip Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Whip_Wrestling "Irish Whip Wrestling") (IWW) and [Pro Wrestling Noah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Wrestling_Noah "Pro Wrestling Noah").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-PowerSlam109-6)

## Professional wrestling career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Professional wrestling career")]

### Smoky Mountain and early career (1994–1997)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Smoky Mountain and early career (1994–1997)")]

See also: [The Gangstas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Gangstas "The Gangstas")

Connor began his wrestling career in [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey") as "Ace the Animal". He then wrestled [Earthquake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthquake_(wrestler) "Earthquake (wrestler)") in the [World Wrestling Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wrestling_Federation "World Wrestling Federation") (WWF) in 1994 under his given name as a [jobber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Job_(professional_wrestling)#Jobbers "Job (professional wrestling)").

Connor debuted in [Smoky Mountain Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoky_Mountain_Wrestling "Smoky Mountain Wrestling") in September 1994 as "A.C. Conner". In October 1994, he was renamed "'Downtown' D'Lo Brown" and introduced as the head of security for [the Gangstas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Gangstas "The Gangstas") ([Mustapha Saed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mustapha_Saed "Mustapha Saed") and [New Jack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jack "New Jack")). Brown was the [worker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worker_(professional_wrestling) "Worker (professional wrestling)") of the [stable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_(professional_wrestling) "Stable (professional wrestling)"), complementing Saed's size and Jack's animated personality. He regularly wrestled on [Smoky Mountain Wrestling's television show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smoky_Mountain_Wrestling "Smoky Mountain Wrestling"), unsuccessfully challenged for the [SMW Beat the Champ Television Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SMW_Beat_the_Champ_Television_Championship "SMW Beat the Champ Television Championship") on several occasions. At Sunday Bloody Sunday II in February 1995, the Gangstas lost to the [Heavenly Bodies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavenly_Bodies_(1990s_tag_team) "Heavenly Bodies (1990s tag team)") and [Jim Cornette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Cornette "Jim Cornette"). At Bluegrass Brawl III in April 1995, the Gangstas lost to [Tracy Smothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracy_Smothers "Tracy Smothers") and [The Undertaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Undertaker "The Undertaker") in a [handicap match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handicap_match "Handicap match"). Brown wrestled his final match for Smoky Mountain Wrestling in October 1995.

After leaving Smoky Mountain Wrestling, Brown signed a deal with the WWF and was sent to the [Heartland Wrestling Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland_Wrestling_Association "Heartland Wrestling Association") for more training while also making appearances as a jobber on WWF television. Brown also spent most of 1996 wrestling in [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico") for the [World Wrestling Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wrestling_Council "World Wrestling Council").

### World Wrestling Federation / World Wrestling Entertainment (1997–2003)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: World Wrestling Federation / World Wrestling Entertainment (1997–2003)")]

#### Nation of Domination (1997–1998)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Nation of Domination (1997–1998)")]

Main article: [Nation of Domination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nation_of_Domination "Nation of Domination")

In April 1997, Brown was reintroduced to the World Wrestling Federation (WWF) as a member of [Faarooq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Simmons "Ron Simmons")'s [heel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heel_(professional_wrestling) "Heel (professional wrestling)")[Nation of Domination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nation_of_Domination "Nation of Domination")[stable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Stable "Glossary of professional wrestling terms"), debuting as one of several non-descript people in suits that accompanied the group to the ring. During this time, his most notable moment was when [Ahmed Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Johnson "Ahmed Johnson") slammed him onto the roof of a car during _[Shotgun Saturday Night](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shotgun\_Saturday\_Night "Shotgun Saturday Night")_. His first televised match as a member of the Nation was on the April 26, 1997, episode of _Shotgun Saturday Night_, as he, [Crush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crush_(wrestler) "Crush (wrestler)"), and [Savio Vega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savio_Vega "Savio Vega") defeated [Aldo Montoya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldo_Montoya "Aldo Montoya"), [Steve Corino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Corino "Steve Corino"), and [Freddie Joe Floyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Joe_Floyd "Freddie Joe Floyd"). On May 26, 1997, he had his first match on _[Raw is War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raw\_is\_War "Raw is War")_, defeating [Bob "Spark Plugg" Holly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_%22Spark_Plugg%22_Holly "Bob \"Spark Plugg\" Holly"). After the [King of the Ring 1997](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_the_Ring_1997 "King of the Ring 1997"), Faarooq fired the rest of the Nation's members, except for D-Lo, who was later joined by [Ahmed Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ahmed_Johnson "Ahmed Johnson") (later replaced by [Rocky Maivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rocky_Maivia "Rocky Maivia")), [Kama Mustafa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kama_Mustafa "Kama Mustafa"), and [Mark Henry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Henry "Mark Henry").

In early 1998, the Nation of Domination [turned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Turn "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") on Faarooq, allowing Maivia, now going by the name "The Rock", to assume leadership. During this period Kama also changed his name to "The Godfather" and began portraying a pimp character. Brown and Henry eventually turned on both Rock and Godfather separately, moving into a feud with the Rock before finally branching out as a moderately successful [tag team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tag_team "Tag team"), later turning [face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face_(professional_wrestling) "Face (professional wrestling)") along the way. Prior to the face turn, Brown had started wrestling with a chest protector, supposedly for a torn [pectoral muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pectoral_muscle "Pectoral muscle") sustained in a match against [Dan "The Beast" Severn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dan_%22The_Beast%22_Severn "Dan \"The Beast\" Severn"). Instead, he used the chest protector to his advantage, making his finishing move, the [Lo Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lo_Down "Lo Down"), more effective.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-7)

#### Title pursuit (1998–2000)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Title pursuit (1998–2000)")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/D%27Lo_Brown_in_Birmingham.jpg/250px-D%27Lo_Brown_in_Birmingham.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:D'Lo_Brown_in_Birmingham.jpg)

Brown in the late 1990s

In 1998, he feuded with [X-Pac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Pac "X-Pac") over the [WWF European Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWF_European_Championship "WWF European Championship"). His career peaked when he held the [European](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE_European_Championship "WWE European Championship") and [Intercontinental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE_Intercontinental_Championship "WWE Intercontinental Championship") Championships simultaneously during a feud with [Jeff Jarrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Jarrett "Jeff Jarrett") and Mark Henry. This feat has only been duplicated by [Jeff Jarrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Jarrett "Jeff Jarrett"), [Kurt Angle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurt_Angle "Kurt Angle"), and [Rob Van Dam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Van_Dam "Rob Van Dam"), all of whom became [world champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling_championship#World_championships "Professional wrestling championship") in some form, later in their careers.

Brown was involved in inadvertently ending the career of [Droz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Droz_(wrestler) "Droz (wrestler)") on October 5, 1999, when a [running powerbomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Powerbomb#Sit-Out_Powerbomb "Powerbomb") was [botched](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botch_(professional_wrestling) "Botch (professional wrestling)") due to Droz's baggy shirt. The match was filmed for the October 7 edition of _[SmackDown!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Friday\_Night\_SmackDown "WWE Friday Night SmackDown")_, but was never aired. Droz suffered a severe neck injury, rendering him a [quadriplegic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadriplegia "Quadriplegia").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-PowerSlam109-6) During an interview with Title Match Wrestling, Brown dispelled a popular rumor that a fan had thrown an object into the ring which caused him to slip and badly injure Darren Drozdov. Brown took responsibility for botching the move, stating that the accident could have happened to "any" wrestler he had been in the ring with that night. He also said the accident caused him to "wrestle differently" and to second guess every move he performed in the ring from that day forward.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-8) Drozdov maintained that he did not blame Brown for his injuries and believed the incident was an accident.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-9)

During the rest of the year and into some of the next, Brown became an ally of former fellow Nation member The Godfather, emulating his dress and walking motions. The teaming ended when Brown turned heel on the Godfather.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-PowerSlam109-6)

#### Lo Down (2000–2001)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Lo Down (2000–2001)")]

Brown then formed a tag team in July 2000 with [Chaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mosh_(wrestler) "Mosh (wrestler)") named _Lo Down_. The team mostly wrestled on _[Sunday Night Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Heat "WWE Heat")_ and _[WWE Jakked / Metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Jakked\_/\_Metal "WWE Jakked / Metal")_. Shortly after the team formed, [Tiger Ali Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiger_Ali_Singh "Tiger Ali Singh") joined the team to become their [manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manager_(professional_wrestling) "Manager (professional wrestling)"). The tag team then came dressed towards the ring in [Sikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikh "Sikh") attire and took on a [gimmick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Gimmick "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") very similar to Tiger's.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-PowerSlam109-6) The team was removed from WWF [television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television "Television") in January 2001 after Singh was injured.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-swervepodcast-10) According to Brown, it was the lowest point in his career. Brown also spent six months in Puerto Rico wrestling for the [International Wrestling Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Wrestling_Association_(Puerto_Rico) "International Wrestling Association (Puerto Rico)") teaming with Chaz. He later teamed with Glamour Boy Shane holding the IWA tag team titles.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-swervepodcast-10)

#### OVW and Heartland (2001–2002)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: OVW and Heartland (2001–2002)")]

Chaz and Singh were later released by WWF that year, Brown stayed in WWE's [developmental territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling#Farm_team "Professional wrestling"), OVW. Notably, Brown wrestled future World champion [Batista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Batista "Dave Batista") in a losing effort. He also worked for [Heartland Wrestling Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heartland_Wrestling_Association "Heartland Wrestling Association") going into 2002.

#### Alliance with Theodore Long (2002–2003)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Alliance with Theodore Long (2002–2003)")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/D%27lo_Brown%2C_2002.jpg/250px-D%27lo_Brown%2C_2002.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:D'lo_Brown,_2002.jpg)

Brown in September 2002

Brown returned to television on the April 28, 2002, episode of _Heat_, losing to [Eddie Guerrero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Guerrero "Eddie Guerrero"). For the rest of the year, Brown mostly wrestled on _Heat_, did a little bit of commentary on the show, and even started a brief feud with [Raven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raven_(wrestler) "Raven (wrestler)"). In late 2002, [Theodore Long](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Long "Theodore Long") retired as a WWE [referee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Referee_(professional_wrestling) "Referee (professional wrestling)") and managed D'Lo, who had complained about acts of [racism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racism "Racism") during his matches. D'Lo started Long's group Thuggin' and Buggin' Enterprises which eventually turned into a group of African Americans who worked an angle in which they felt they were victims of racism and were being held down by the "white man". With Long's managerial services, D'Lo Brown went undefeated for several weeks.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-PowerSlam109-6)

Brown faced [Booker T](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Booker_T_(wrestler) "Booker T (wrestler)") in a losing effort on the February 10, 2003, episode of _[Raw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Raw "WWE Raw")_. His involvement with Thuggin' and Buggin' Enterprises was brought to a close when footage was shown on the February 16 episode (taped February 10) of _Heat_ of Theodore Long kicking D'Lo Brown to the curb and introducing his replacement [Rodney Mack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodney_Begnaud "Rodney Begnaud").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-PowerSlam109-6) He was then released from his WWE contract on February 14, 2003.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-PowerSlam109-6)

### NWA Total Nonstop Action (2003–2004)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: NWA Total Nonstop Action (2003–2004)")]

Connor, still under the D'Lo Brown name, Joined [NWA Total Nonstop Action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NWA_Total_Nonstop_Action "NWA Total Nonstop Action") in March 2003. During his time in TNA, he teamed with [AJ Styles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AJ_Styles "AJ Styles") on many occasions together even challenging for the NWA World Tag Team Championships but were unsuccessful. After the team split up Brown challenged Styles for the [NWA World Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NWA_World_Heavyweight_Championship "NWA World Heavyweight Championship") but came up short on every occasion doing a best of 3 series.

On the March 19, 2003, edition of NWA-TNA, Brown teamed with [Dusty Rhodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dusty_Rhodes "Dusty Rhodes") and [Jeff Jarrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Jarrett "Jeff Jarrett") defeating [Erik Watts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erik_Watts "Erik Watts"), [Brian Lawler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brian_Lawler "Brian Lawler") and [David Flair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Flair "David Flair").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-11) On April 2, 2003, edition of NWA-TNA weekly pay-per view D'Lo Brown unsuccessfully challenged Jeff Jarrett for the [NWA World Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NWA_World_Heavyweight_Championship "NWA World Heavyweight Championship").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-12) On April 14, 2004, Brown and [Gran Apolo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gran_Apolo "Gran Apolo") won the [NWA World Tag Team Championships](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NWA_World_Tag_Team_Championship "NWA World Tag Team Championship") defeating [Kid Kash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kid_Kash "Kid Kash") and [Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lance_Archer "Lance Archer"), They lost the titles just seven days after winning them.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-13) D'Lo later left TNA in the summer of 2004.

On a September 2014 interview, Brown said there was a time in TNA during this time where the creative team wanted to radically change his character; on top of not feeling like he was a good fit with TNA, Brown felt that by wrestling in Japan, he could still wrestle there while being D'Lo Brown.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-swervepodcast-10)

### All Japan Pro Wrestling and overseas (2004–2009)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: All Japan Pro Wrestling and overseas (2004–2009)")]

Brown Joined [All Japan Pro Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_Japan_Pro_Wrestling "All Japan Pro Wrestling"), competing in regular tours with the Japanese company as a member of [Roughly Obsess and Destroy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roughly_Obsess_and_Destroy "Roughly Obsess and Destroy") (RO&D).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-PowerSlam109-6) During one of these tours on September 17, 2006, Brown betrayed RO&D to join the rival [Voodoo Murders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voodoo_Murders "Voodoo Murders") faction. Brown left All Japan in 2007 and rejoined [RO&D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roughly_Obsess_and_Destroy "Roughly Obsess and Destroy") in [Pro Wrestling Noah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Wrestling_Noah "Pro Wrestling Noah").

When not in Japan, Brown was regularly found touring the [United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Kingdom "United Kingdom"), as well as working for [Irish Whip Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Whip_Wrestling "Irish Whip Wrestling") in [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland "Ireland"). In April 2005, Brown became one of the lead trainers of the ill-fated _[Celebrity Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity\_Wrestling "Celebrity Wrestling")_ on [ITV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_(TV_network) "ITV (TV network)"). This Saturday evening [reality show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reality_television "Reality television") saw [celebrities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celebrity "Celebrity") learn wrestling and compete in challenge matches. After a few weeks the programme was to be canceled, but was instead moved to Sunday mornings to finish its final episodes. During his time wrestling in [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England "England"), he would face off in a series of matches against his _Celebrity Wrestling_ opposition's trainer, [Joe Legend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Hitchen "Joe Hitchen").

### Return to WWE (2008–2009)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Return to WWE (2008–2009)")]

In 2008, Brown began wrestling in a number of [dark matches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Dark_match "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") for WWE. On June 5, WWE announced that Brown had been signed to a contract, and he began working more dark matches for the company.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-14) He made his television return on the July 21, 2008, edition of _[Raw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Raw "WWE Raw")_, defeating [Santino Marella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santino_Marella "Santino Marella"). Following this, Brown's appearances on television became more sporadic, and on January 9, 2009, it was announced on WWE's website that he had been released from his WWE contract due to cost-cutting measures.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-15)

### Independent circuit (2009–2010)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Independent circuit (2009–2010)")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/D_Lo_Brown_in_2009_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-D_Lo_Brown_in_2009_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:D_Lo_Brown_in_2009_(cropped).jpg)

Brown in 2009

Brown debuted for [Ring of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_Honor "Ring of Honor") during Proving Ground 09 weekend in February. He was defeated by [Nigel McGuinness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nigel_McGuinness "Nigel McGuinness") in an [ROH World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ROH_World_Championship "ROH World Championship") match. He also wrestled at the [ROH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_Honor "Ring of Honor") 7th Anniversary Show on March 21, 2009, in Manhattan, defeating [Jay Briscoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jay_Briscoe "Jay Briscoe"). Brown also appeared on _[Ring of Honor Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring\_of\_Honor\_Wrestling "Ring of Honor Wrestling")_ on [HDNet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HDNet "HDNet"). Varsity Pro Wrestling also announced that Brown would be making his third appearance for the promotion on their February tour. Brown also made a surprise appearance in [Chikara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chikara_(professional_wrestling) "Chikara (professional wrestling)"), where he filled in as a substitute for Iceberg of The Cold Front at the [2009 King of Trios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Trios#2009 "King of Trios") tournament. Brown came up short in an [ROH World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ROH_World_Championship "ROH World Championship") match at [Take No Prisoners (2009)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Take_No_Prisoners_(2009) "Take No Prisoners (2009)"). At ROH's Manhattan Mayhem III on June 13, Brown tapped out to [Colt Cabana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colt_Cabana "Colt Cabana") in a four-way match also involving [Bryan Danielson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryan_Danielson "Bryan Danielson") and [Claudio Castagnoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cesaro_(wrestler) "Cesaro (wrestler)"). On June 27 on an [ROH](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_Honor "Ring of Honor") show he was defeated by Cabana.

Throughout April and May 2009, Brown flew to [Japan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japan "Japan") to take part in the 13-night [Pro Wrestling Noah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Wrestling_Noah "Pro Wrestling Noah") Global Tag League with his partner [Buchanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Buchanan "Barry Buchanan"). During the course of the event they won and lost three matches with one contest went to a draw giving them seven points placing them sixth of the eight teams.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-noahtourn09-16) Outside of the tournament Brown was undefeated in six-man tag team competition, adding [Keith Walker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Walker_(wrestler) "Keith Walker (wrestler)") to the team, including a victory over Noah founder [Mitsuharu Misawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitsuharu_Misawa "Mitsuharu Misawa") in one of his last matches.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-noah09-17)

On the September 15, 2009, edition of _Between The Ropes_, Brown announced that after his current tour with [Ring of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_Honor "Ring of Honor"), he would retire from in-ring action. Also, on this edition of Between The Ropes, Brown announced he would become a semi-regular co-host when his [TNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_Nonstop_Action_Wrestling "Total Nonstop Action Wrestling") scheduling allowed him to be in studio.

He defeated [Mr. Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ken_Anderson_(wrestler) "Ken Anderson (wrestler)") on June 12, 2010, TCW event in Pine Bluff, Arkansas. He did not wrestle again until 2013.

### Return to TNA (2009–2013)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Return to TNA (2009–2013)")]

Main article: [Aces & Eights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aces_&_Eights "Aces & Eights")

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f4/D_Lo_Brown_2013.jpg/250px-D_Lo_Brown_2013.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:D_Lo_Brown_2013.jpg)

D'Lo Brown as a member of Aces & Eights

In September 2009, Connor was re-signed by TNA as their lead [agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Agent "Glossary of professional wrestling terms"). Additionally, D'Lo was in charge of talent development and acquisitions heading up the [TNA Gut Check](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TNA_Gut_Check "TNA Gut Check") program.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-18)

On the March 7, 2013, episode of _Impact Wrestling_, Brown attacked Kurt Angle and revealed himself as the Vice President of [Aces & Eights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aces_&_Eights "Aces & Eights"), turning heel in the process.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-pwtorch.com-19) Three days later at [Lockdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lockdown_(2013) "Lockdown (2013)"), Brown interfered in Angle's steel cage match against fellow Aces & Eights member [Wes Brisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Brisco "Wes Brisco"), costing Angle the match. Later that evening, the President of the Aces & Eights was revealed to be [Bully Ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bully_Ray "Bully Ray").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-pwtorch.com-19) Brown wrestled his first televised match in four years on the May 2 episode of _Impact Wrestling_, losing to Kurt Angle in an I Quit Match.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-20) As a result of his loss, Brown was demoted to a prospect the following week. On July 17, Brown announced he was released from his TNA contract.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-Waldmanrelease-1)

### Return to AJPW (2013)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Return to AJPW (2013)")]

On August 11, 2013, All Japan Pro Wrestling announced that Brown would be returning to the promotion the following month to take part in the [2013 Ōdō Tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/%C5%8Cd%C5%8D_Tournament#2013 "Ōdō Tournament").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-21) Brown returned to the promotion on September 11 in a non-tournament tag team match, where he and [Bambi Killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Raaber "Chris Raaber") defeated [Burning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burning_(professional_wrestling) "Burning (professional wrestling)") ([Atsushi Aoki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atsushi_Aoki "Atsushi Aoki") and [Yoshinobu Kanemaru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoshinobu_Kanemaru "Yoshinobu Kanemaru")), with Brown pinning Kanemaru for the win.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-22) Three days later, Brown was eliminated by Kanemaru in his first round match in the Ōdō Tournament.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-23) For the rest of the tour, which lasted until September 23, Brown worked [midcard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Card "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") tag team matches, suffering pinfall losses in most of them.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-27) On October 3, Brown was announced also for All Japan's next tour, which started October 12.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-28) Brown continued teaming regularly with Bambi Killer, which eventually led to the two forming a heel stable named [DK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_Kingdom_(professional_wrestling) "Dark Kingdom (professional wrestling)") (Dark Kingdom) under the leadership of [Kenso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenzo_Suzuki "Kenzo Suzuki") on November 21.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-30)

### Return to Independent circuit (2013–2023)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Return to Independent circuit (2013–2023)")]

After working for TNA, Brown returned to the independent circuit where he appeared for Pro Wrestling Syndicate on May 18, 2013, with [D.O.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drew_Hankinson "Drew Hankinson") and [Knux](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Knox "Mike Knox").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-31) On August 3, 2013, Brown and Hankinson lost to the [Rock N' Roll Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_N'_Roll_Express "Rock N' Roll Express") at Mid-Atlantic Wrestling Legends Fanfest. By the end of the year he worked in England and the Netherlands.

On November 22, 2014, Brown would team with former WWE wrestler [Bull Buchanan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bull_Buchanan "Bull Buchanan") defeating AJ Steele and Brad Lynch at Buchanan's retirement show at UIW in Bowden, Georgia.

He lost to [Sabu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabu_(wrestler) "Sabu (wrestler)") at XICW Bodyslams Childhood Cancer event in Wyandotte, Michigan, on July 29, 2017. On October 27, 2018, he won the vacated HLW Legends Title defeating Dru Skillz in Fort Wayne, Indiana. He dropped the title to [Tracy Smothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracy_Smothers "Tracy Smothers") on April 20, 2019.

Brown's last match was on October 7, 2023, for Border City Wrestling in which he along with [Scott D'Amore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_D'Amore "Scott D'Amore") and [Tommy Dreamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Dreamer "Tommy Dreamer") defeated the team of [Johnny Swinger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Swinger "Johnny Swinger"), N8 Mattson and Tyler Tirva.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-32)

### Future Stars of Wrestling (2014–2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Future Stars of Wrestling (2014–2015)")]

Brown formerly held a weekly class on Friday for "Future Stars of Wrestling" training center in Las Vegas.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-swervepodcast-10)

### Return to Impact / Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (2019–present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Return to Impact / Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (2019–present)")]

On July 3, 2019, Brown announced that he had returned to [Impact Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_Wrestling "Impact Wrestling") with a multi-year contract as a [producer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_agent_(professional_wrestling) "Road agent (professional wrestling)").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-33) Brown and Mr Anderson were scheduled to represent the [Aces & Eights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aces_&_Eights "Aces & Eights") at [TNA: There's No Place Like Home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TNA:_There's_No_Place_Like_Home "TNA: There's No Place Like Home") but the event was annulled due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-34)

In January 2021, it was announced that Brown would be one half of Impact's new announce team with Matt Striker from Hard to Kill onward. The role ended in early 2022 when [Honor No More](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honor_No_More "Honor No More") attacked him. His role was replaced by [Matt Rehwoldt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Rehwoldt "Matt Rehwoldt").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-36)

Brown returned as part of the reunited [Aces & Eights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aces_&_Eights "Aces & Eights"), managing [Garett Bischoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garett_Bischoff "Garett Bischoff") and [Wes Brisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Brisco "Wes Brisco"), in a losing effort against Honor No More's [Kenny King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_King_(wrestler) "Kenny King (wrestler)") and [Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vinny_Marseglia "Vinny Marseglia"). The reunion would later be a one-off, as Brown continued to his Talent Relations role backstage and makes occasional appearances thereafter.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-40)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=D%27Lo_Brown&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Connor holds an accounting degree from the [University of Maine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Maine "University of Maine"). He also played for the [football team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maine_Black_Bears_football "Maine Black Bears football") while attending university. He worked as a [Certified Public Accountant (CPA)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Certified_Public_Accountant "Certified Public Accountant") before he began his wrestling career.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-OWW-2)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-41)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D'Lo_Brown#cite_note-IMDb-3) He and his wife Jennifer were married in 2001 and have two daughters. He has three half siblings on his dad's side. He is a fan of the [Chicago Bears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Bears "Chicago Bears") and [Liverpool F.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.")

The **International Boxing Hall of Fame** (**IBHOF**), located in [Canastota, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canastota,_New_York "Canastota, New York"), adjacent to exit 34 of the [New York State Thruway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Thruway "New York State Thruway"), honors [boxers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing "Boxing"), trainers and other contributors to the sport worldwide. Inductees are selected on ballots created through screened public nominations by members of the [Boxing Writers Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_Writers_Association_of_America "Boxing Writers Association of America").

The IBHOF started as a 1980s initiative by Ed Brophy to honor Canastota's world boxing champions, [Carmen Basilio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carmen_Basilio "Carmen Basilio") and Basilio's nephew, [Billy Backus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Backus "Billy Backus"); the village of Canastota inaugurated the new museum in 1989 which showcases boxing's rich history.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Boxing_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Boxing_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-2) With the opening of the Oneida Indian Nation's Turning Stone Casino in the nearby city of Verona in the early 90s, a relationship was developed whereas various IBHOF Hall of Fame Weekend events were hosted at the casino.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Boxing_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Boxing_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Boxing_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-5) Today, the IBHOF is visited by boxing fans from all over the world.

An earlier hall had been created in 1954, when _[The Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ring\_(magazine) "The Ring (magazine)")_ magazine's [Boxing Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ring_magazine_Hall_of_Fame "The Ring magazine Hall of Fame") was launched, located at [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden "Madison Square Garden") in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"). When that Boxing Hall of Fame was disbanded in 1987, it had a total of 155 inductees. As of November 2018[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=International_Boxing_Hall_of_Fame&action=edit), [all but 13](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ring_magazine_Hall_of_Fame "The Ring magazine Hall of Fame") of those 155 have also been inducted into the IBHOF. In 2002, boxing promoter [Aileen Eaton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aileen_Eaton "Aileen Eaton") became the first woman inducted into the IBHOF.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Boxing_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-auto-6) Beginning in 2020, the IBHOF began inducting female boxers for the first time since its inception.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Boxing_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-auto1-7)

Ceremonies have been held every second Sunday in June since 1990 to honor inductees but were postponed in 2020 and 2021 due to [COVID-19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Boxing_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-8) Events are attended by many former world boxing champions, as well as boxing and [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_(film_industry) "Hollywood (film industry)") celebrities. Artist [Richard T. Slone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_T._Slone "Richard T. Slone") has been the official artist of the IBHOF since 1997, creating portraits of inductees and other works for the Hall.

## Eligibility

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=International_Boxing_Hall_of_Fame&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Eligibility")]

All professional boxers become eligible for election into the International Boxing Hall of Fame three years after their retirement (previously used to be five years before 2019). Inductees are selected by members of the [Boxing Writers Association of America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_Writers_Association_of_America "Boxing Writers Association of America") and an international panel of boxing historians, based on criteria in five separate categories:

*   **Modern**: Retired boxers whose last bout was no earlier than 1989. Prior to a 2014 rule change, the category reflected boxers whose last bout was after 1943.
*   **Old Timers**: Until 2014, the rule was boxers whose last bout was no earlier than 1893 and no later than 1942. This category has since changed, similar to the [Veterans Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veterans_Committee "Veterans Committee") in baseball's Hall of Fame. It is now split into two categories. 
    *   **Early Era**: Boxers who fought from the beginning of Marquis of Queensbury Rules (1893) until 1942.
    *   **Late Era**: Boxers who fought their last bout from 1943 to 1988 [[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Boxing_Hall_of_Fame#cite_note-9)

*   **Pioneers**: Boxers whose last bout was in or prior to 1892. Generally, they are boxers who fought before the Marquis of Queensbury Rules.
*   **Observers**: Journalists, historians, writers and artists.
*   **Non-Participants**: People who made contributions to the sport of boxing apart from their roles as boxers or observers.
