## Infrastructure

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Waterbury,_Connecticut&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Infrastructure")]

### Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Waterbury,_Connecticut&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: Transportation")]

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Waterbury%2C_CT%2C_Metro-North_station.jpg/250px-Waterbury%2C_CT%2C_Metro-North_station.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Waterbury,_CT,_Metro-North_station.jpg)

[Waterbury Metro-North Railroad station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury_station_(Metro-North) "Waterbury station (Metro-North)"), located on the [Waterbury Branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury_Branch "Waterbury Branch") line

Commuting in the Greater Waterbury area consists of multiple public transportation options. [CT Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_Transit "Connecticut Transit") through [Northeast Transportation Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northeast_Transportation_Company "Northeast Transportation Company"), operates a significant number of city buses running from Waterbury's city center at Exchange Place to various neighborhoods in the city.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut#cite_note-78) In 2014, the [Hartford-New Britain Busway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hartford-New_Britain_Busway "Hartford-New Britain Busway") was opened, a local bus runs to Waterbury, [Cheshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheshire,_Connecticut "Cheshire, Connecticut"), [Southington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southington,_Connecticut "Southington, Connecticut") and [New Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Britain,_Connecticut "New Britain, Connecticut") an express bus to run between Waterbury and [Hartford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hartford,_Connecticut "Hartford, Connecticut").

[Metro-North Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro-North_Railroad "Metro-North Railroad") runs commuter trains multiple times a day between the [Waterbury station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury_station_(Metro-North) "Waterbury station (Metro-North)") and [Bridgeport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bridgeport_(Metro-North_station) "Bridgeport (Metro-North station)"), with connections to [Grand Central Terminal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Central_Terminal "Grand Central Terminal") in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"). Waterbury's [Union Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury_Union_Station "Waterbury Union Station"), built in 1909 for the [New York, New Haven and Hartford Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York,_New_Haven_and_Hartford_Railroad "New York, New Haven and Hartford Railroad"), is now closed for use as a railway station and part of the building is now the headquarters of the _Republican-American_ newspaper.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut#cite_note-79) Passengers traveling to and from Waterbury board and alight on a concrete platform adjacent to the old station. There are no ticket agents at Waterbury, which is currently the end of the line for the [Waterbury Branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury_Branch "Waterbury Branch").

The two main highways that run through the heart of the city are [I-84](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_84_in_Connecticut "Interstate 84 in Connecticut") (Yankee Expressway) and [Route 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_Route_8 "Connecticut Route 8"). In the downtown area, I-84 and Route 8 are located on the elevated William W. Deady Bridge,[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut#cite_note-80) known locally as the "MixMaster" with eastbound traffic on the upper deck and westbound traffic on the lower deck. The interchange is ranked as one of the most heavily congested traffic areas in the New York/Connecticut region.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut#cite_note-mixmasterfox61-81)[Waterbury–Oxford Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury%E2%80%93Oxford_Airport "Waterbury–Oxford Airport") is the primary airport serving the city. The smaller [Waterbury Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury_Airport_(Connecticut) "Waterbury Airport (Connecticut)") is about 4 miles (6.4 km) from the city's central business district. [Bradley International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradley_International_Airport "Bradley International Airport") ([BDL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bradley_International_Airport "Bradley International Airport")) in [Windsor Locks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Windsor_Locks,_Connecticut "Windsor Locks, Connecticut") and [Tweed New Haven Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tweed_New_Haven_Airport "Tweed New Haven Airport") ([HVN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tweed_New_Haven_Airport "Tweed New Haven Airport")) in [East Haven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Haven,_Connecticut "East Haven, Connecticut") are the closest commercial airports to Waterbury.

### Police department

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Waterbury,_Connecticut&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Police department")]

The Waterbury Police Department was founded in 1853. The department has a police academy.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut#cite_note-82)

### Fire department

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Waterbury,_Connecticut&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Fire department")]

Waterbury Fire Department is a full-time, paid fire department, which operates eight engine companies, three truck companies, one squad company, and one rescue company out of nine fire stations, divided into 2 battalions. One battalion is commanded by a Battalion Chief, and the other a Deputy Chief, who serves as the Tour Commander each shift.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut#cite_note-83)

**Bello** (Spanish pronunciation:[[ˈbeʎo]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish"), [[ˈbeʝo]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish")) is a city and municipality in [Antioquia Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antioquia_Department "Antioquia Department"), Colombia and a suburb of [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín"), the department capital. Bello is part of [the Metropolitan Area of the Aburrá Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Metropolitan_Area_of_the_Aburr%C3%A1_Valley "The Metropolitan Area of the Aburrá Valley") in the department of Antioquia. It is bordered on the north by the municipality of San Pedro de los Milagros, on the east by the municipality of [Copacabana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copacabana_(Colombia) "Copacabana (Colombia)"), on the south by the municipality of [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín") and on the west by the municipalities of Medellín and [San Jerónimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jer%C3%B3nimo,_Colombia "San Jerónimo, Colombia").

It is the center of the development in the north of the [Aburrá Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aburr%C3%A1_Valley "Aburrá Valley") ([Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"): _Valle de Aburrá_), and as a member of the [Metropolitan Area of Aburrá Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Metropolitan_Area_of_the_Aburr%C3%A1_Valley "The Metropolitan Area of the Aburrá Valley"), or AMVA (Spanish: _Área Metropolitana del Valle de Aburrá_), some public services are regulated for the [Metropolitan Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_area "Metropolitan area"). There are several nicknames for the municipality: Imperio del Cacique Niquia (Cacique Niquia's Empire), Cuna de Marco Fidel Suárez ("[Marco Fidel Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Fidel_Su%C3%A1rez "Marco Fidel Suárez")'s cradle"), "Ciudad de los artistas" ("Artist's city").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Meaning "Beautiful" in English, Bello was founded in 1676 as "Hato Viejo". [The department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antioquia_Department "Antioquia Department") later changed its name to Bello in honor of Latin American polymath [Andrés Bello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_Bello "Andrés Bello") (1781–1865). Bello was granted municipal status in 1913, officially making it one of the cities of Antioquia Department.

Bello is also known as the "City of Artists" in Colombia. Its current mayor is Lorena Gonzáles Ospina.

In July 1541, troops under the command of [Jerónimo Luis Tejelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jer%C3%B3nimo_Luis_Tejelo?action=edit&redlink=1 "Jerónimo Luis Tejelo (page does not exist)") (Deputy Marshal to [Jorge Robledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Robledo "Jorge Robledo")) found the wide valley of Los Aburrá inhabited by indigenous farmers who had "a habitat organized in groups with scattered houses, forming clusters of houses". This was especially true in the town of Niquías, which occupied the territory now called Bello.

In 1574, the Spanish subject [Gaspar de Rodas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaspar_de_Rodas "Gaspar de Rodas") requested a land grant for the Aburrá Valley from the town hall of Santa Fe de Antioquia in order to establish therein "herds of livestock and agricultural plots", in order to provide food for the conquest. He was awarded the territories from the hill or "Asientos viejos de Aburrá" – an area which is now occupied by the Medellín town center – down, including the Niquía territory. In 1576, the captain of Rodas came to exercise control over the area from the Spanish Crown, permitting the use of the territory for corrals, ranches and flocks. From 1613 onward, the area began to be called Hatoviejo instead of Hato de Rodas or Hato de Aburrá to distinguish it from later herds.

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Capilla_de_Hatoviejo-Bello.JPG/250px-Capilla_de_Hatoviejo-Bello.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Capilla_de_Hatoviejo-Bello.JPG)

Chapel of Nuestra Señora del Rosario in Hatoviejo, better known as the Hatoviejo Chapel.

In this context the colonizers exercised their chivalry, understood as "that noble philosophy that reacted against innovations." Thus they endowed their farms with chapels to signify prestige and noble origin and so it can be inferred that in Bello the colony was not given a foundation that "involve a regular pattern of squares and streets. Hatoviejo was not a village as it was in the beginning the town of Candelaria." The chapels that were constructed were [Our Lady of Chiquinquirá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Lady_of_Chiquinquir%C3%A1 "Our Lady of Chiquinquirá") (in 1653) [Our Lady of the Rosary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Lady_of_the_Rosary "Our Lady of the Rosary") (1720), Our Lady of Sopetrán (in Madera, 1775) and [Our Lady of Guadalupe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Lady_of_Guadalupe "Our Lady of Guadalupe") (in Fontidueño, 1761). Later these temples were moved or demolished, as happened with the Hatoviejo Parish Church of Our Lady of the Rosary, demolished in 1788 in order to build the Chapel of Hatoviejo in 1792, which still stands. At the end of the eighteenth century, in 1788, Hatoviejo was elevated to the status of party, assigned to the jurisdiction of the town of Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria in [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín").

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/Apartamentos_en_el_municipio_de_bello.JPG/250px-Apartamentos_en_el_municipio_de_bello.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apartamentos_en_el_municipio_de_bello.JPG)

Apartments at the Bello exit.

In Hatoviejo the land was organized according to the economic role of its people. The reference to "Calle arriba" (Up the road) and "Calle Abajo," (down the road) was common. The square and the Church of the Rosary were used as the central point. On 28 December 1883 the "Ciudadano Presidente " of the Antioquia State renamed the village from Hatoviejo to Bello, at the request of a group of people who felt that the name "Hato" made them despised and humiliated as _hato_ was a place for animals. Instead, the name Bello was "more cultured, more appropriate and more worthy of the great patriarch of American letters" ([Andrés Bello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_Bello "Andrés Bello")).

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/Amanecer_%28Bello%29.JPG/250px-Amanecer_%28Bello%29.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Amanecer_(Bello).JPG)

Dawn on 10 June 2012, in Bello

Bello forms part of the Aburrá Valley, a valley in the Andes mountain range. It is located next to Medellín at its northern border in the Valley of Aburrá. The climate is warm and is affected by gentle winds throughout the year.

The city has a total area of 142.36 km 2 of which 19.7 km 2 are urban land and 122.66 km 2 is rural land. This valley is fully urbanized in the plains, and very busy on its slopes. In the valley it is crossed by the Medellín River, which runs south–north, and its 57 streams throughout its 70 kilometers.

Topographically the urban part of the city is a tilted plane that descends from 1600 to 1400 meters above sea level. Bello is in the northern part of the valley and the mountains surrounding the city exceed 2,500 meters.

The main topographic feature is the Cerro Quitasol (pyramidal mountain, 2,880 meters above sea level), located north of the city and considered by its grandeur as the tutelary hill of Bello.

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Climate")]

The city, being located in the tropics, does not experience climatic changes. The average rainfall is 1347 mm., The temperature is determined by climatic zones ranging from desert, through cold up to medium where he is the highest, which has an average temperature of 25.7°C throughout the year, alternating between dry and wet periods and is cooled by winds that blow along the valley throughout the year.

Additionally the area receives trade winds that blow from the lower valleys of the [Cauca River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cauca_River "Cauca River") to the west and the [Magdalena River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magdalena_River "Magdalena River") to the east and middle, creating a dense layer of warm air, which causes the lower part of the town and some surrounding areas to increase in humidity and increase barometric temperature. As a result of the wind, northern municipalities such as Bello, [Copacabana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copacabana,_Antioquia "Copacabana, Antioquia"), [Girardota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girardota "Girardota") and [Barbosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbosa,_Antioquia "Barbosa, Antioquia") are warmer than the Antioquia capital of [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín"), despite its proximity.

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Bello_en_la_noche.jpg/250px-Bello_en_la_noche.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bello_en_la_noche.jpg)

Bello at night

According to figures from the 2005 DANE census,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bello,_Antioquia#cite_note-DANE_2005-6) Bello has 371,973 inhabitants. It is the second largest city in the metropolitan area of the Aburrá Valley, altogether totaling 3,312,165 people.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bello,_Antioquia#cite_note-DANE_2009-7) The municipality has a population density of about 2496 per square kilometer. 47.1% of the population are male and 52.9% are female. The literacy rate in the population over 5 years of age is 92.9%. Public services have high coverage, since 96.9% of households have electricity service, 96.4% have water service and 91.4% have telephone communication.

According to figures from the Government of Antioquia based on the 2004 Quality of Life Survey, the prevailing socioeconomic strata in the municipality is 2 (low) with 39.3%, followed by the strata 3 (medium-low) at 36.1% then strata 1 (low-high) with 20.2%. In a smaller proportion are also strata 4 (middle) and 5 (medium-high) with 4.3% and 0.1% respectively, which are mainly rustic houses located on the sidewalks of the municipality.

## Politico-administrative structures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Politico-administrative structures")]

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Bello-Diciembre2007.jpg/250px-Bello-Diciembre2007.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bello-Diciembre2007.jpg)

[Christmas lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_lights_in_Medell%C3%ADn "Christmas lights in Medellín") in the main park in 2007.

Bello is governed by a democratic system based on administrative decentralization processes generated by the Political Constitution of Colombia, 1991. The city is governed by a mayor (executive power) and a Municipal Council (legislative power).

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/Alcald%C3%ADa_de_Bello-Colombia.jpg/250px-Alcald%C3%ADa_de_Bello-Colombia.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Alcald%C3%ADa_de_Bello-Colombia.jpg)

Bello City Hall.

The Mayor of Bello is the head of government and of the municipal administration, representing the municipality legally, judicially and extrajudicially. It is a position elected by popular vote for a four-year period. The current mayor is Carlos Alirio Munoz Lopez.

The main functions of the Mayor are to administer the resources of the municipality, to provide for the welfare and interests of his fellow citizens and to represent them before the Federal Government. He should also promote local policies to improve the quality of life, such as health programs, housing, education and road infrastructure; equally, he maintains public order.

The Municipal Council of Bello is a popularly elected public corporation, composed of 19 democratically elected councillors, for a term of four years. The council is the legislative body and makes binding agreements within its territorial jurisdiction. Its functions include approving projects from the mayor, issuing the organic standards of the budget and issuing the annual revenues and expenditures budget. To manage the municipality, the Mayor has 14 ministries:

*   Administrative Services Secretariat
*   Secretariat of Government
*   Secretariat of Sport and Recreation
*   Education and Culture Secretariat
*   Internal Control Secretariat
*   Secretariat of Health
*   Planning Secretariat
*   Secretariat of Infrastructure
*   The Environment Secretariat
*   General Secretariat
*   Secretariat of Finance
*   Secretariat of Welfare and Social Integration
*   Secretariat of Transport and Traffic
*   Secretariat of Entrepreneurship

### Metropolitan area

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Metropolitan area")]

The Metropolitan Area of the Aburrá Valley is an administrative political entity which is based throughout the [Aburrá Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aburr%C3%A1_Valley "Aburrá Valley") at an average altitude of about 1,538 meters.

The area consists of 10 municipalities, and is crossed from south to north by the [Medellín River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn_River "Medellín River") which, being born to its south in the town of Caldas, it takes on the name of Rio Porce in the north, in the municipality of Barbosa.

It was the first metropolitan area to be established in Colombia in 1980 and is the second largest metropolitan area in the country in population after the Capital District of Bogotá. The total population, which includes the urban and rural population of the ten cities is 3,312,165 inhabitants.

The main urban area of the Metropolitan Area of the Aburrá Valley is located in the center of the valley and consists of the four largest cities by population: [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín"), Bello, [Itagüí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itag%C3%BC%C3%AD "Itagüí") and [Envigado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Envigado "Envigado").

## Economy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Economy")]

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Camara_de_Comercio_de_Medellin-Sede_Bello.JPG/250px-Camara_de_Comercio_de_Medellin-Sede_Bello.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Camara_de_Comercio_de_Medellin-Sede_Bello.JPG)

Medellín Chamber of Commerce, Bello headquarters

In the urban area the main economic activities are related to textiles, concentrates, organized trade, informal trade, and the exploitation of sand pits and quarries. The rural areas are devoted to agriculture and livestock on a small scale.

Both industry and trade have been contributing to economic activities in the town as a result of their contribution to and participation in economic growth.

The economic activity of the municipality of Bello is represented in the following sectors according to their levels of participation:

**Industrial activity**[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bello,_Antioquia#cite_note-semiosfera.org.co-9)

*   Textiles 18.30%
*   Wood, paper and publishing, chemicals, coal, rubber, mineral and nonmetallic products 16.92%
*   Other nonspecific industries 14.85%
*   Basic machinery and equipment metal industries 12.60%

**Commercial activity**[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bello,_Antioquia#cite_note-semiosfera.org.co-9)

*   Retail (Includes agricultural production) 61.51%
*   Hotels and accommodation 26.14%
*   Transport, storage and communication 9.60%
*   Wholesale 2.19%
*   Construction 0.78%

## Communication

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Communication")]

In the town of Bello virtually all possible telecommunications services are available, from payphones, to mobile phone networks, broadband wireless networks, browsing centers or cybercafés, IP communication, and others.

The leading company in this sector is EPM Telecommunications (under its brand UNE), recently separated from its parent company Public Enterprises of Medellín ([EPM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EPM_(company) "EPM (company)")). Also present are Bello Cable Bello Television Telecommunications Company, the Bogotá Telecommunications Enterprise ([ETB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ETB_(company) "ETB (company)")), [Telmex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telmex "Telmex") and [Telecom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telecom_(Colombia)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Telecom (Colombia) (page does not exist)") (from Telefónica).

There are three mobile operators all with nationwide coverage and GSM technology, Claro, Movistar (Telefónica) and Tigo of ETB, EPM and Luxembourg's Millicom International Telecommunications.

The Avantel company also operates in the municipality, offering [trunking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trunking "Trunking") service, which is done by means of a hybrid cellular and radio.

The city has several channels of broadcast television, the three local channels – Telemedellín, Channel U and Televida, (which cover the Valle de Aburrá), a regional channel Teleantioquia, and five national channels: two private – Caracol and RCN, and three public – Canal Uno, [Señal Institucional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Se%C3%B1al_Institucional "Señal Institucional") and [Señal Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Se%C3%B1al_Colombia "Señal Colombia"). In addition the TVN Channel of the Cable Bello Television Cable System, reaches approximately 80,000 thousand homes. Subscription TV companies offer their own channels.

The city has a variety of AM and FM stations, with both local and national coverage, most of which are managed by [Caracol Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caracol_Radio "Caracol Radio") or [RCN Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCN_Radio "RCN Radio"), although there are other independent stations such as Todelar and Super.

In Bello and the rest of Antioquia there are two major newspapers in circulation: [El Colombiano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Colombiano "El Colombiano") and [El Mundo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Mundo_(Colombia) "El Mundo (Colombia)"), both with a long history at the regional level. Also circulating are the [El Tiempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Tiempo_(Colombia) "El Tiempo (Colombia)") and [El Espectador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Espectador "El Espectador") newspapers, both with national circulation.

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Education")]

Bello has 111 educational institutions, of which 41 are public and 70 are private. Over 84,002 students are educated in these institutions, of which 48,086 are within the public sector and 35,916 within the private sector. Throughout the metropolitan area there is a wide number of higher education institutions. There are four such institutions located within Bello's territory: the University of San Buenaventura, Bello branch of Uniminuto, a sub-site of the Jaime Isaza Cadavid Colombian Polytechnic and the Marco Fidel Suárez Polytechnic.

## Sports

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Sports")]

Until 2010, the town had a football (soccer) team, [Atlético Bello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Bello "Atlético Bello"), in the Colombian Professional Second Division ("Primera B"). That team was later acquired by [Atlético Juventud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Juventud "Atlético Juventud") and is now defunct.

**Bello** (Spanish pronunciation:[[ˈbeʎo]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish"), [[ˈbeʝo]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish")) is a city and municipality in [Antioquia Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antioquia_Department "Antioquia Department"), Colombia and a suburb of [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín"), the department capital. Bello is part of [the Metropolitan Area of the Aburrá Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Metropolitan_Area_of_the_Aburr%C3%A1_Valley "The Metropolitan Area of the Aburrá Valley") in the department of Antioquia. It is bordered on the north by the municipality of San Pedro de los Milagros, on the east by the municipality of [Copacabana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copacabana_(Colombia) "Copacabana (Colombia)"), on the south by the municipality of [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín") and on the west by the municipalities of Medellín and [San Jerónimo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Jer%C3%B3nimo,_Colombia "San Jerónimo, Colombia").

It is the center of the development in the north of the [Aburrá Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aburr%C3%A1_Valley "Aburrá Valley") ([Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language"): _Valle de Aburrá_), and as a member of the [Metropolitan Area of Aburrá Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Metropolitan_Area_of_the_Aburr%C3%A1_Valley "The Metropolitan Area of the Aburrá Valley"), or AMVA (Spanish: _Área Metropolitana del Valle de Aburrá_), some public services are regulated for the [Metropolitan Area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metropolitan_area "Metropolitan area"). There are several nicknames for the municipality: Imperio del Cacique Niquia (Cacique Niquia's Empire), Cuna de Marco Fidel Suárez ("[Marco Fidel Suárez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marco_Fidel_Su%C3%A1rez "Marco Fidel Suárez")'s cradle"), "Ciudad de los artistas" ("Artist's city").

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Meaning "Beautiful" in English, Bello was founded in 1676 as "Hato Viejo". [The department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antioquia_Department "Antioquia Department") later changed its name to Bello in honor of Latin American polymath [Andrés Bello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_Bello "Andrés Bello") (1781–1865). Bello was granted municipal status in 1913, officially making it one of the cities of Antioquia Department.

Bello is also known as the "City of Artists" in Colombia. Its current mayor is Lorena Gonzáles Ospina.

In July 1541, troops under the command of [Jerónimo Luis Tejelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jer%C3%B3nimo_Luis_Tejelo?action=edit&redlink=1 "Jerónimo Luis Tejelo (page does not exist)") (Deputy Marshal to [Jorge Robledo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Robledo "Jorge Robledo")) found the wide valley of Los Aburrá inhabited by indigenous farmers who had "a habitat organized in groups with scattered houses, forming clusters of houses". This was especially true in the town of Niquías, which occupied the territory now called Bello.

In 1574, the Spanish subject [Gaspar de Rodas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaspar_de_Rodas "Gaspar de Rodas") requested a land grant for the Aburrá Valley from the town hall of Santa Fe de Antioquia in order to establish therein "herds of livestock and agricultural plots", in order to provide food for the conquest. He was awarded the territories from the hill or "Asientos viejos de Aburrá" – an area which is now occupied by the Medellín town center – down, including the Niquía territory. In 1576, the captain of Rodas came to exercise control over the area from the Spanish Crown, permitting the use of the territory for corrals, ranches and flocks. From 1613 onward, the area began to be called Hatoviejo instead of Hato de Rodas or Hato de Aburrá to distinguish it from later herds.

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/51/Capilla_de_Hatoviejo-Bello.JPG/250px-Capilla_de_Hatoviejo-Bello.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Capilla_de_Hatoviejo-Bello.JPG)

Chapel of Nuestra Señora del Rosario in Hatoviejo, better known as the Hatoviejo Chapel.

In this context the colonizers exercised their chivalry, understood as "that noble philosophy that reacted against innovations." Thus they endowed their farms with chapels to signify prestige and noble origin and so it can be inferred that in Bello the colony was not given a foundation that "involve a regular pattern of squares and streets. Hatoviejo was not a village as it was in the beginning the town of Candelaria." The chapels that were constructed were [Our Lady of Chiquinquirá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Lady_of_Chiquinquir%C3%A1 "Our Lady of Chiquinquirá") (in 1653) [Our Lady of the Rosary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Lady_of_the_Rosary "Our Lady of the Rosary") (1720), Our Lady of Sopetrán (in Madera, 1775) and [Our Lady of Guadalupe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Lady_of_Guadalupe "Our Lady of Guadalupe") (in Fontidueño, 1761). Later these temples were moved or demolished, as happened with the Hatoviejo Parish Church of Our Lady of the Rosary, demolished in 1788 in order to build the Chapel of Hatoviejo in 1792, which still stands. At the end of the eighteenth century, in 1788, Hatoviejo was elevated to the status of party, assigned to the jurisdiction of the town of Nuestra Señora de la Candelaria in [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín").

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8c/Apartamentos_en_el_municipio_de_bello.JPG/250px-Apartamentos_en_el_municipio_de_bello.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Apartamentos_en_el_municipio_de_bello.JPG)

Apartments at the Bello exit.

In Hatoviejo the land was organized according to the economic role of its people. The reference to "Calle arriba" (Up the road) and "Calle Abajo," (down the road) was common. The square and the Church of the Rosary were used as the central point. On 28 December 1883 the "Ciudadano Presidente " of the Antioquia State renamed the village from Hatoviejo to Bello, at the request of a group of people who felt that the name "Hato" made them despised and humiliated as _hato_ was a place for animals. Instead, the name Bello was "more cultured, more appropriate and more worthy of the great patriarch of American letters" ([Andrés Bello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andr%C3%A9s_Bello "Andrés Bello")).

## Geography

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Geography")]

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/ac/Amanecer_%28Bello%29.JPG/250px-Amanecer_%28Bello%29.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Amanecer_(Bello).JPG)

Dawn on 10 June 2012, in Bello

Bello forms part of the Aburrá Valley, a valley in the Andes mountain range. It is located next to Medellín at its northern border in the Valley of Aburrá. The climate is warm and is affected by gentle winds throughout the year.

The city has a total area of 142.36 km 2 of which 19.7 km 2 are urban land and 122.66 km 2 is rural land. This valley is fully urbanized in the plains, and very busy on its slopes. In the valley it is crossed by the Medellín River, which runs south–north, and its 57 streams throughout its 70 kilometers.

Topographically the urban part of the city is a tilted plane that descends from 1600 to 1400 meters above sea level. Bello is in the northern part of the valley and the mountains surrounding the city exceed 2,500 meters.

The main topographic feature is the Cerro Quitasol (pyramidal mountain, 2,880 meters above sea level), located north of the city and considered by its grandeur as the tutelary hill of Bello.

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Climate")]

The city, being located in the tropics, does not experience climatic changes. The average rainfall is 1347 mm., The temperature is determined by climatic zones ranging from desert, through cold up to medium where he is the highest, which has an average temperature of 25.7°C throughout the year, alternating between dry and wet periods and is cooled by winds that blow along the valley throughout the year.

Additionally the area receives trade winds that blow from the lower valleys of the [Cauca River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cauca_River "Cauca River") to the west and the [Magdalena River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Magdalena_River "Magdalena River") to the east and middle, creating a dense layer of warm air, which causes the lower part of the town and some surrounding areas to increase in humidity and increase barometric temperature. As a result of the wind, northern municipalities such as Bello, [Copacabana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copacabana,_Antioquia "Copacabana, Antioquia"), [Girardota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girardota "Girardota") and [Barbosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbosa,_Antioquia "Barbosa, Antioquia") are warmer than the Antioquia capital of [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín"), despite its proximity.

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/66/Bello_en_la_noche.jpg/250px-Bello_en_la_noche.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bello_en_la_noche.jpg)

Bello at night

According to figures from the 2005 DANE census,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bello,_Antioquia#cite_note-DANE_2005-6) Bello has 371,973 inhabitants. It is the second largest city in the metropolitan area of the Aburrá Valley, altogether totaling 3,312,165 people.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bello,_Antioquia#cite_note-DANE_2009-7) The municipality has a population density of about 2496 per square kilometer. 47.1% of the population are male and 52.9% are female. The literacy rate in the population over 5 years of age is 92.9%. Public services have high coverage, since 96.9% of households have electricity service, 96.4% have water service and 91.4% have telephone communication.

According to figures from the Government of Antioquia based on the 2004 Quality of Life Survey, the prevailing socioeconomic strata in the municipality is 2 (low) with 39.3%, followed by the strata 3 (medium-low) at 36.1% then strata 1 (low-high) with 20.2%. In a smaller proportion are also strata 4 (middle) and 5 (medium-high) with 4.3% and 0.1% respectively, which are mainly rustic houses located on the sidewalks of the municipality.

## Politico-administrative structures

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Politico-administrative structures")]

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b7/Bello-Diciembre2007.jpg/250px-Bello-Diciembre2007.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Bello-Diciembre2007.jpg)

[Christmas lights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christmas_lights_in_Medell%C3%ADn "Christmas lights in Medellín") in the main park in 2007.

Bello is governed by a democratic system based on administrative decentralization processes generated by the Political Constitution of Colombia, 1991. The city is governed by a mayor (executive power) and a Municipal Council (legislative power).

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/97/Alcald%C3%ADa_de_Bello-Colombia.jpg/250px-Alcald%C3%ADa_de_Bello-Colombia.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Alcald%C3%ADa_de_Bello-Colombia.jpg)

Bello City Hall.

The Mayor of Bello is the head of government and of the municipal administration, representing the municipality legally, judicially and extrajudicially. It is a position elected by popular vote for a four-year period. The current mayor is Carlos Alirio Munoz Lopez.

The main functions of the Mayor are to administer the resources of the municipality, to provide for the welfare and interests of his fellow citizens and to represent them before the Federal Government. He should also promote local policies to improve the quality of life, such as health programs, housing, education and road infrastructure; equally, he maintains public order.

The Municipal Council of Bello is a popularly elected public corporation, composed of 19 democratically elected councillors, for a term of four years. The council is the legislative body and makes binding agreements within its territorial jurisdiction. Its functions include approving projects from the mayor, issuing the organic standards of the budget and issuing the annual revenues and expenditures budget. To manage the municipality, the Mayor has 14 ministries:

*   Administrative Services Secretariat
*   Secretariat of Government
*   Secretariat of Sport and Recreation
*   Education and Culture Secretariat
*   Internal Control Secretariat
*   Secretariat of Health
*   Planning Secretariat
*   Secretariat of Infrastructure
*   The Environment Secretariat
*   General Secretariat
*   Secretariat of Finance
*   Secretariat of Welfare and Social Integration
*   Secretariat of Transport and Traffic
*   Secretariat of Entrepreneurship

### Metropolitan area

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Metropolitan area")]

The Metropolitan Area of the Aburrá Valley is an administrative political entity which is based throughout the [Aburrá Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aburr%C3%A1_Valley "Aburrá Valley") at an average altitude of about 1,538 meters.

The area consists of 10 municipalities, and is crossed from south to north by the [Medellín River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn_River "Medellín River") which, being born to its south in the town of Caldas, it takes on the name of Rio Porce in the north, in the municipality of Barbosa.

It was the first metropolitan area to be established in Colombia in 1980 and is the second largest metropolitan area in the country in population after the Capital District of Bogotá. The total population, which includes the urban and rural population of the ten cities is 3,312,165 inhabitants.

The main urban area of the Metropolitan Area of the Aburrá Valley is located in the center of the valley and consists of the four largest cities by population: [Medellín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medell%C3%ADn "Medellín"), Bello, [Itagüí](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itag%C3%BC%C3%AD "Itagüí") and [Envigado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Envigado "Envigado").

## Economy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Economy")]

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a2/Camara_de_Comercio_de_Medellin-Sede_Bello.JPG/250px-Camara_de_Comercio_de_Medellin-Sede_Bello.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Camara_de_Comercio_de_Medellin-Sede_Bello.JPG)

Medellín Chamber of Commerce, Bello headquarters

In the urban area the main economic activities are related to textiles, concentrates, organized trade, informal trade, and the exploitation of sand pits and quarries. The rural areas are devoted to agriculture and livestock on a small scale.

Both industry and trade have been contributing to economic activities in the town as a result of their contribution to and participation in economic growth.

The economic activity of the municipality of Bello is represented in the following sectors according to their levels of participation:

**Industrial activity**[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bello,_Antioquia#cite_note-semiosfera.org.co-9)

*   Textiles 18.30%
*   Wood, paper and publishing, chemicals, coal, rubber, mineral and nonmetallic products 16.92%
*   Other nonspecific industries 14.85%
*   Basic machinery and equipment metal industries 12.60%

**Commercial activity**[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bello,_Antioquia#cite_note-semiosfera.org.co-9)

*   Retail (Includes agricultural production) 61.51%
*   Hotels and accommodation 26.14%

*   Construction 0.78%

## Communication

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Communication")]

In the town of Bello virtually all possible telecommunications services are available, from payphones, to mobile phone networks, broadband wireless networks, browsing centers or cybercafés, IP communication, and others.

The leading company in this sector is EPM Telecommunications (under its brand UNE), recently separated from its parent company Public Enterprises of Medellín ([EPM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EPM_(company) "EPM (company)")). Also present are Bello Cable Bello Television Telecommunications Company, the Bogotá Telecommunications Enterprise ([ETB](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ETB_(company) "ETB (company)")), [Telmex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telmex "Telmex") and [Telecom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telecom_(Colombia)?action=edit&redlink=1 "Telecom (Colombia) (page does not exist)") (from Telefónica).

There are three mobile operators all with nationwide coverage and GSM technology, Claro, Movistar (Telefónica) and Tigo of ETB, EPM and Luxembourg's Millicom International Telecommunications.

The Avantel company also operates in the municipality, offering [trunking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trunking "Trunking") service, which is done by means of a hybrid cellular and radio.

The city has several channels of broadcast television, the three local channels – Telemedellín, Channel U and Televida, (which cover the Valle de Aburrá), a regional channel Teleantioquia, and five national channels: two private – Caracol and RCN, and three public – Canal Uno, [Señal Institucional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Se%C3%B1al_Institucional "Señal Institucional") and [Señal Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Se%C3%B1al_Colombia "Señal Colombia"). In addition the TVN Channel of the Cable Bello Television Cable System, reaches approximately 80,000 thousand homes. Subscription TV companies offer their own channels.

The city has a variety of AM and FM stations, with both local and national coverage, most of which are managed by [Caracol Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caracol_Radio "Caracol Radio") or [RCN Radio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RCN_Radio "RCN Radio"), although there are other independent stations such as Todelar and Super.

In Bello and the rest of Antioquia there are two major newspapers in circulation: [El Colombiano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Colombiano "El Colombiano") and [El Mundo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Mundo_(Colombia) "El Mundo (Colombia)"), both with a long history at the regional level. Also circulating are the [El Tiempo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Tiempo_(Colombia) "El Tiempo (Colombia)") and [El Espectador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Espectador "El Espectador") newspapers, both with national circulation.

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Education")]

Bello has 111 educational institutions, of which 41 are public and 70 are private. Over 84,002 students are educated in these institutions, of which 48,086 are within the public sector and 35,916 within the private sector. Throughout the metropolitan area there is a wide number of higher education institutions. There are four such institutions located within Bello's territory: the University of San Buenaventura, Bello branch of Uniminuto, a sub-site of the Jaime Isaza Cadavid Colombian Polytechnic and the Marco Fidel Suárez Polytechnic.

## Sports

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Bello,_Antioquia&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Sports")]

Until 2010, the town had a football (soccer) team, [Atlético Bello](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Bello "Atlético Bello"), in the Colombian Professional Second Division ("Primera B"). That team was later acquired by [Atlético Juventud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atl%C3%A9tico_Juventud "Atlético Juventud") and is now defunct.

Where your donation goes

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://wikimediafoundation.org/annualreports/current/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

32% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

11% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

**Marlton** is a [census-designated place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census-designated_place "Census-designated place")[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-10) (CDP) located within [Evesham Township](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evesham_Township,_New_Jersey "Evesham Township, New Jersey") in [Burlington County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burlington_County,_New_Jersey "Burlington County, New Jersey"), in the [U.S. state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-CPH232-13) As of the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the CDP had a population of 10,594 residents,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2020-3) reflecting a 4.5% increase from the 10,133 enumerated at the [2010 U.S. census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_U.S._census "2010 U.S. census"),[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2010-14) in turn a 1.2% decrease from the 10,260 counted in the [2000 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_census "2000 United States census").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2000-15)

While Marlton comprises only a small part of Evesham Township, many people colloquially refer to the entire township as Marlton.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-16)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marlton,_New_Jersey&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Marlton was founded by [Welsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welsh_people "Welsh people") and [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_people "English people") farmers beginning in 1676. The name Marlton first appeared in the early 19th century. The name is derived from [marl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marl "Marl") clay, which is commonly found in the local soil. The discovery of the marl content helped local business and farmers, and caused the first "building boom", occurring in the 1830s and 1840s. Marl continued to be excavated in Marlton until 1930, when the pits were shut down.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-17) The marl was sold locally, and shipped directly, by rail to Burlington City, [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia"), [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania"), and [Atlantic City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_City,_New_Jersey "Atlantic City, New Jersey"), for reshipping as an alternate for [green manure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_manure "Green manure"), [water treatment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_treatment "Water treatment") amendment, and semi-flowable fill.

## Landmarks

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marlton,_New_Jersey&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Landmarks")]

[PH-32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PH-32 "PH-32"), a [Project Nike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Nike "Project Nike") missile base from the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"), was completed in 1955 on a 38-acre (15 ha) site located near Marlton Middle School.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-18)

### 2020 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marlton,_New_Jersey&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2020 census")]

As of the [2020 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), Marlton had a population of 10,594. The median age was 41.9 years. 18.6% of residents were under the age of 18 and 17.8% were 65 years of age or older. For every 100 females, there were 94.1 males, and for every 100 females age 18 and older there were 91.2 males.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2020DP-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2020PL-32)

100.0% of residents lived in urban areas, while 0.0% lived in rural areas.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2020DHC-33)

There were 4,525 households in Marlton, of which 25.5% had children under the age of 18 living in them. Of all households, 45.3% were married-couple households, 17.8% were households with a male householder and no spouse or partner present, and 30.5% were households with a female householder and no spouse or partner present. About 32.9% of all households were made up of individuals and 14.8% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2020DP-31)

There were 4,725 housing units, of which 4.2% were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.9% and the rental vacancy rate was 6.7%.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2020DP-31)

### 2010 census

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marlton,_New_Jersey&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: 2010 census")]

The [2010 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_United_States_census "2010 United States census") counted 10,133 people, 4,126 households, and 2,653 families in the CDP. The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 3,140.3 per square mile (1,212.5/km 2). There were 4,343 housing units at an average density of 1,345.9 per square mile (519.7/km 2). [Hispanic or Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._census) "Hispanic (U.S. census)") of any race were 4.41% (447) of the population.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2010-14)

Of the 4,126 households, 28.2% had children under the age of 18; 50.7% were married couples living together; 10.2% had a female householder with no husband present and 35.7% were non-families. Of all households, 29.9% were made up of individuals and 9.2% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.45 and the average family size was 3.12.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2010-14)

21.4% of the population were under the age of 18, 7.5% from 18 to 24, 28.7% from 25 to 44, 28.7% from 45 to 64, and 13.6% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 40.3 years. For every 100 females, the population had 92.2 males. For every 100 females ages 18 and older there were 90.3 males.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2010-14)

The [population density](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Population_density "Population density") was 3,171.0 inhabitants per square mile (1,224.3/km 2). There were 4,203 housing units at an average density of 1,299 per square mile (502/km 2). The racial makeup of Marlton was 91.32% [White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_(U.S._Census) "White (U.S. Census)"), 2.88% [Black](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/African_American_(U.S._Census) "African American (U.S. Census)") or [African American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), 0.14% [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_American_(U.S._Census) "Native American (U.S. Census)"), 4.18% [Asian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asian_(U.S._Census) "Asian (U.S. Census)"), 0.01% [Pacific Islander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Islander_(U.S._Census) "Pacific Islander (U.S. Census)"), 0.59% from [other races](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(United_States_Census) "Race (United States Census)"), and 0.89% from two or more races. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") of any race were 2.34% of the population.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2000-15)

There were 4,097 households, out of which 30.7% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 54.3% were [married couples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage "Marriage") living together, 9.3% had a female householder with no husband present, and 33.4% were non-families. 28.4% of all households were made up of individuals, and 7.8% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.49 and the average family size was 3.12.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2000-15)

In Marlton, the population was spread out, with 23.5% under the age of 18, 6.6% from 18 to 24, 34.8% from 25 to 44, 23.2% from 45 to 64, and 12.0% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 37 years. For every 100 females, there were 93.8 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 91.2 males.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2000-15)

The median income for a household in Marlton was $52,271, and the median income for a family was $61,217. Males had a median income of $46,905 versus $31,798 for females. The [per capita income](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Per_capita_income "Per capita income") for Marlton was $25,145. About 2.1% of families and 3.5% of the population were below the [poverty line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_line "Poverty line"), including 3.6% of those under age 18 and 2.9% of those age 65 or over.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2000-15)

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marlton,_New_Jersey&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Transportation")]

[NJ Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NJ_Transit "NJ Transit") provides bus service on the [406](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/406_(New_Jersey_bus) "406 (New Jersey bus)") route to and from [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-34)

The [Marlton Circle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton_Circle "Marlton Circle") was a traffic circle at the intersection of [Route 70](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey_Route_70 "New Jersey Route 70") and [Route 73](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey_Route_73 "New Jersey Route 73"). In 2010, the circle was completely eliminated and replaced with a grade-separated interchange where Route 73 crosses over Route 70. The new traffic pattern was completed in late 2011.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-35)

The [Philadelphia Marlton and Medford Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Marlton_and_Medford_Railroad "Philadelphia Marlton and Medford Railroad") made multiple stops in Marlton from July 1881 to September 24, 1927.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-36)

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marlton,_New_Jersey&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Education")]

The CDP is in the [Evesham Township School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evesham_Township_School_District "Evesham Township School District") (elementary and middle school) and the [Lenape Regional School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenape_Regional_School_District "Lenape Regional School District") (for high school).[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-37) All residents of Evesham Township are zoned to [Cherokee High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherokee_High_School_(New_Jersey) "Cherokee High School (New Jersey)"). Additionally, the small school program at [Seneca High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seneca_High_School_(New_Jersey) "Seneca High School (New Jersey)") accepts Evesham Township residents.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-38)

**Marlton** is a [census-designated place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Census-designated_place "Census-designated place")[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-10) (CDP) located within [Evesham Township](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evesham_Township,_New_Jersey "Evesham Township, New Jersey") in [Burlington County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burlington_County,_New_Jersey "Burlington County, New Jersey"), in the [U.S. state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") of [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-CPH232-13) As of the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the CDP had a population of 10,594 residents,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2020-3) reflecting a 4.5% increase from the 10,133 enumerated at the [2010 U.S. census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2010_U.S._census "2010 U.S. census"),[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2010-14) in turn a 1.2% decrease from the 10,260 counted in the [2000 census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_census "2000 United States census").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-Census2000-15)

While Marlton comprises only a small part of Evesham Township, many people colloquially refer to the entire township as Marlton.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-16)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marlton,_New_Jersey&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

Marlton was founded by [Welsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welsh_people "Welsh people") and [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_people "English people") farmers beginning in 1676. The name Marlton first appeared in the early 19th century. The name is derived from [marl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marl "Marl") clay, which is commonly found in the local soil. The discovery of the marl content helped local business and farmers, and caused the first "building boom", occurring in the 1830s and 1840s. Marl continued to be excavated in Marlton until 1930, when the pits were shut down.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-17) The marl was sold locally, and shipped directly, by rail to Burlington City, [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia"), [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania "Pennsylvania"), and [Atlantic City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_City,_New_Jersey "Atlantic City, New Jersey"), for reshipping as an alternate for [green manure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_manure "Green manure"), [water treatment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_treatment "Water treatment") amendment, and semi-flowable fill.

## Landmarks

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marlton,_New_Jersey&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Landmarks")]

[PH-32](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PH-32 "PH-32"), a [Project Nike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Project_Nike "Project Nike") missile base from the [Cold War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cold_War "Cold War"), was completed in 1955 on a 38-acre (15 ha) site located near Marlton Middle School.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-18)

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marlton,_New_Jersey&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Transportation")]

[NJ Transit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NJ_Transit "NJ Transit") provides bus service on the [406](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/406_(New_Jersey_bus) "406 (New Jersey bus)") route to and from [Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia "Philadelphia").[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-34)

The [Marlton Circle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton_Circle "Marlton Circle") was a traffic circle at the intersection of [Route 70](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey_Route_70 "New Jersey Route 70") and [Route 73](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey_Route_73 "New Jersey Route 73"). In 2010, the circle was completely eliminated and replaced with a grade-separated interchange where Route 73 crosses over Route 70. The new traffic pattern was completed in late 2011.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-35)

The [Philadelphia Marlton and Medford Railroad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philadelphia_Marlton_and_Medford_Railroad "Philadelphia Marlton and Medford Railroad") made multiple stops in Marlton from July 1881 to September 24, 1927.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-36)

## Education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Marlton,_New_Jersey&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Education")]

The CDP is in the [Evesham Township School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evesham_Township_School_District "Evesham Township School District") (elementary and middle school) and the [Lenape Regional School District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenape_Regional_School_District "Lenape Regional School District") (for high school).[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-37) All residents of Evesham Township are zoned to [Cherokee High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cherokee_High_School_(New_Jersey) "Cherokee High School (New Jersey)"). Additionally, the small school program at [Seneca High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seneca_High_School_(New_Jersey) "Seneca High School (New Jersey)") accepts Evesham Township residents.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marlton,_New_Jersey#cite_note-38)

**Mazatlán** (Spanish pronunciation:[[masaˈtlan]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Spanish "Help:IPA/Spanish")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/8/8b/Mazatl%C3%A1n.ogg/Mazatl%C3%A1n.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mazatl%C3%A1n.ogg "File:Mazatlán.ogg")) is a city in the Mexican [state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_states_of_Mexico "List of states of Mexico") of [Sinaloa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinaloa "Sinaloa"). The city serves as the municipal seat for the surrounding _[municipio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Municipio "Municipio")_, known as the [Mazatlán Municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n_Municipality "Mazatlán Municipality"). It is located on the [Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean") coast across from the southernmost tip of the [Baja California peninsula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baja_California_peninsula "Baja California peninsula").

_Mazatlán_ is a [Nahuatl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nahuatl "Nahuatl") word for 'place of deer'. The city was colonized in 1531 by the [Conquistadors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquistadors "Conquistadors") where many [indigenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas "Indigenous peoples of the Americas") people lived. By the mid-19th century, a large group of immigrants arrived from Germany. Over time, Mazatlán developed into [a commercial seaport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_of_Mazatl%C3%A1n "Port of Mazatlán"), importing equipment for the nearby gold and silver mines. It served as the capital of Sinaloa from 1859 to 1873. The [German settlers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Mexicans "German Mexicans") also influenced the local music, [banda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banda_music "Banda music"), with some genres being an alteration of [Bavarian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bavaria "Bavaria") folk music. The settlers established the [Pacifico Brewery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pac%C3%ADfico_(beer) "Pacífico (beer)") on 14 March 1900. Mazatlán has a rich culture and art community; in addition to the [Angela Peralta Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teatro_%C3%81ngela_Peralta,_Mazatl%C3%A1n "Teatro Ángela Peralta, Mazatlán"), the city has many galleries, museums and buildings of historic value.

With a population of 438,434 (city) and 489,987 (municipality) as of the 2010 census, Mazatlán is the second-largest city in the state. It is also a tourist destination, with its beaches lined with resort hotels. A car ferry crosses the [Gulf of California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_of_California "Gulf of California"), from Mazatlán to [La Paz, Baja California Sur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Paz,_Baja_California_Sur "La Paz, Baja California Sur"). The municipality has a land area of 3,068.48 km 2 (1,184.75 sq mi) and includes smaller outlying communities such as [Villa Unión](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villa_Uni%C3%B3n,_Sinaloa "Villa Unión, Sinaloa"), La Noria, [El Quelite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Quelite,_Sinaloa "El Quelite, Sinaloa"), and El Habal. Mazatlán is served by [Mazatlán International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n_International_Airport "Mazatlán International Airport").

## Etymology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Etymology")]

Mazatlán [etymologically](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etymology "Etymology") comes from the [Nahuatl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nahuatl "Nahuatl") language and means "Land of deer" (mazatl "deer" and tlan referring to a place abundant with something).[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-3)

Originally, the name Presidio of Mazatlán was used for what is now called Villa Unión. The port of Mazatlán served as a reference to arrive to Presidio by sea, and was called the Islands of Mazatlán. By decree of the [Estado de Occidente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estado_de_Occidente "Estado de Occidente"), on September 11, 1828, Presidio of Mazatlán was renamed Villa of the Union. This freed the name Mazatlán (land of deer), and since the port was known as Islas de Mazatlán, the name was adopted.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: History")]

### Early settlers

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Early settlers")]

[Indigenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_Mexico "Indigenous peoples of Mexico") groups were in the region of Mazatlán prior to the arrival of the Spanish. These groups included the Totorames, who lived from the south bank of the River Piaxtla to the Río de las Cañas, as well as the [Xiximes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xiximes "Xiximes"), who lived in the mountains in the bordering state of Durango.

### Colonial period

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Colonial period")]

During the early years of the Spanish conquest in Sinaloa, the region currently occupied by the municipality of Mazatlán remained uninhabited. The nearest town was [Chametla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chametla,_Baja_California_Sur?action=edit&redlink=1 "Chametla, Baja California Sur (page does not exist)"), which was occupied by the Spanish in 1531, and lent its name to the province, despite being abandoned shortly afterward.

The city was colonized in 1531 by an [army of Spaniards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conquistador "Conquistador").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-4)

In 1534, the Valley of Mazatlán was divided into 25 Castellanos by an unknown person who did not stay there for long. In 1576, Don Hernando de Bazán, Governor and Captain General of Nueva Vizcaya, sent Captain Martín Hernández with his father, brothers, and soldiers to occupy the site of Mazatlán, granting them land and titles in return. The Captain's claims were ratified in the City of Durango in 1639, and endorsed in the same city in 1650.

[Nuño de Guzmán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nu%C3%B1o_de_Guzm%C3%A1n "Nuño de Guzmán")'s entry to Sinaloa in 1531, and the appointment of the conquered lands as provinces, prompted the internal territorial division of the State. Chametla was occupied by the Spanish, and listed the province extending from the Rio Cañas Elota to the boundary with the province of Culiacán. Both provinces belonged to the kingdom of New Galicia.

In 1565, the town of Chametla was gradually diminished by ongoing Indian raids. That year, Captain Francisco de Ibarra recovered the territory south of the state, rebuilt Chametla, and founded the Villa de San Sebastián (known today as Concordia), and awarded the region to [Nueva Vizcaya, New Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nueva_Vizcaya,_New_Spain "Nueva Vizcaya, New Spain"). The provinces under his jurisdiction included the villages of San Sebastián, Charcas, [Copala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copala,_Sinaloa "Copala, Sinaloa") and Pánuco.

During the last years of the seventeenth century and early eighteenth century, the territory within Sinaloa remained unchanged, until 1732, when the provinces of Sonora and Ostimuri were united, as were the provinces of Sinaloa, Culiacán, and Rosario, with San Felipe and Santiago being the principal cities.

In 1749, Sinaloa was divided into five provinces with their mayors and lieutenancy: Maloya, with jurisdiction over Chametla, Rosario, and San José; Copala, with jurisdiction over San Ignacio, Piaxtla, and Mazatlán; Culiacán, with jurisdiction over Badiraguato, and Sinaloa, which bordered the [Mayo River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayo_River_(Mexico) "Mayo River (Mexico)").

In 1786, the intendant system was implemented due to the need to establish a provincial government. [Arizpe Municipality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizpe_Municipality "Arizpe Municipality") was formed out of the territories of Sonora and Sinaloa. That year, the first mayor, Garrido Durán, established eleven subdelegations, eight of them in Sinaloa, with Mazatlán being within the subdelegation of Copala, which was later called San Sebastián.

### Independent Mexico

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Independent Mexico")]
