Mazatlán's [lighthouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faro_Mazatl%C3%A1n "Faro Mazatlán") (El Faro) began operating in mid-1879. The maritime signals were manufactured in Paris, France, containing a large oil lamp with mirrors, and a [Fresnel lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresnel_lens "Fresnel lens") to focus the light. Since the light was static, from a distance it was often mistaken for a star. By 1905, this lamp was converted to a revolving lamp. During that period, the Mazatlán lighthouse was considered to be the naturally highest in the world. Today, the 1000 watt bulb can be seen for 30 nautical miles (60 km). Near the lighthouse shore, famous "divers" (called this even by the Spanish-speaking inhabitants of Mazatlán) perform daring jumps off high rocks into the Pacific Ocean, for tips from onlooking tourists.

On June 26, 1880, Jesus Ramirez, former general in command of 400 men, stormed the garrison of the square and appropriated Mazatlán. The city was subsequently bombed again by the Mexican warship the _Democratic_, which, during its attack, killed and wounded a high number of women and children. Of the 24 cannon shots fired, only three hit the army headquarters, and the rest landed on neighboring houses.

[Angela Peralta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angela_Peralta "Angela Peralta") (1845–1883), a Mexican opera diva famed throughout the world, died of [yellow fever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yellow_fever "Yellow fever") in Mazatlán shortly after her arrival in the port. Legend has it that she sang one last aria from her [hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centro_Municipal_de_las_Artes,_Mazatl%C3%A1n "Centro Municipal de las Artes, Mazatlán") balcony overlooking the [Plazuela Machado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plazuela_Machado "Plazuela Machado"). Her memory is held dear by Mazatlecos to this day, and the restored Angela Peralta Theater by the Plazuela keeps her memory alive.

The [Cerveceria del Pacífico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerveceria_del_Pac%C3%ADfico "Cerveceria del Pacífico") was founded in the city in 1900 by [German immigrants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Mexican "German Mexican").

### Mexican Revolution

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Mexican Revolution")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f0/Mazatlan_Viejo_285_%2813089852394%29.jpg/250px-Mazatlan_Viejo_285_%2813089852394%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mazatlan_Viejo_285_(13089852394).jpg)

Rebel Infantry near Mazatlán, 1914

In 1912, the municipalities enacted law No.21 as a form of internal division of the State. However, it wasn't until 1915 that the law was abolished by the political directorate, when it erected the first free communes.

With the publication of the decree creating the municipality of Mazatlán in the official newspaper on April 8, 1915, independent life began in the region. The Constitution of 1917, culminating in the first constitutional governor, General Ramón F. Iturbe, born in Mazatlán, confirmed the sixteen municipalities into which the state was divided, which would then be subdivided into receiverships and police precincts.

The City of Mazatlán has the dubious distinction of being the second city in the world after [Tripoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tripoli,_Libya "Tripoli, Libya"), Libya, to suffer aerial bombardment (although the local historical display at the _plazuela_ claims that Mazatlán was the first). During the Mexican Revolution, General [Venustiano Carranza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venustiano_Carranza "Venustiano Carranza") (later president), intent on taking the city of Mazatlán, ordered a biplane to drop a crude bomb of nails and dynamite wrapped in leather on the target of Neveria Hill adjacent to the downtown area of Mazatlán. The crude bomb landed off target on the city streets of Mazatlán, killing two citizens and wounding several others.

### Modern

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Modern")]

Beachgoers

Mazatlán is also the hometown of [Pedro Infante](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pedro_Infante "Pedro Infante"), one of the most popular actors and singers of the [Cinema of Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_Mexico "Cinema of Mexico")'s golden years.

Mazatlán was well regarded by film stars such as [John Wayne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wayne "John Wayne"), [Gary Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Cooper "Gary Cooper"), [John Huston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Huston "John Huston"), and others of their generation as a sportfishing mecca. The hotels along Olas Altas flourished during the 1940s, 1950s and 1960s, supporting this vibrant trade.

In the 1970s, tourism in Old Mazatlán declined as newer venues catering to Western tourists opened on the expanses of beach to the north of the city ("Zona Dorada"). As an example of Mazatlán's tourism expansion, one of the largest [timeshare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timeshare "Timeshare") providers in Mexico, [Grupo Vidanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grupo_Vidanta "Grupo Vidanta"), was founded in 1975 with the inauguration of _Paraíso Mazatlán_ (Mazatlán Paradise). This time also saw the expansion of the Hotel Playa Mazatlán, and the construction of many others, a trend that continues to this day.

Next to Infante, [Lorena Herrera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorena_Herrera "Lorena Herrera"), one of the most famous actresses and singers in Mexico and Latin America during the final decades of the 20th century and the first decades of the 21st century, is Mazatlán's most famous native.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-8) German-born [telenovela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telenovela "Telenovela") star [Sabine Moussier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabine_Moussier "Sabine Moussier"), a stablemate of Herrera's—both have been under [Televisa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Televisa "Televisa") contract since the 1990s—also grew up in Mazatlán. [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_(film_industry) "Hollywood (film industry)") and [Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadway_theatre "Broadway theatre") actress [Sara Ramirez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Ramirez "Sara Ramirez") is also a Mazatlán native.

As the 21st century began, the Centro Histórico was rediscovered by newcomers and locals alike, spurring a renaissance of restoration and entrepreneurial endeavors. Once-fine homes that had fallen into literal ruin were restored to their former glory as family homes and boutique businesses. The city has assisted by upgrading infrastructure such as better water, sewer, and electrical services.

Mazatlán experienced two total solar eclipses in relatively rapid succession on [July 11, 1991](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_eclipse_of_July_11,_1991 "Solar eclipse of July 11, 1991") and [April 8, 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solar_eclipse_of_April_8,_2024 "Solar eclipse of April 8, 2024"), and it was the first city in North America to experience the latter eclipse.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-9)

## Neighboring communities

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Neighboring communities")]

The town of Mazatlán is organized territorially into nine syndicates:

**Mazatlán:** Municipal capital, largest and most important tourist destination.

**[Villa Union:](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villa_Uni%C3%B3n,_Sinaloa "Villa Unión, Sinaloa")** Located 25 km from Mazatlán, second most important town of the municipality. It is said that the first settlers belonged to a Spanish family who arrived there in 1576. Among its economic activities are fishing, agriculture, livestock, fruit growing, aquaculture, and brick making.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-10)

**[El Recodo:](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Recodo,_Sinaloa "El Recodo, Sinaloa")** So-called for the square shape of the Rio Presidio at this point. It is the cradle of Don Cruz Lizarraga, founder of the international [Banda El Recodo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banda_El_Recodo "Banda El Recodo"). Its economic activities are livestock, agriculture, fruit growing, tanning, and saddlery.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-11)

**[El Quelite:](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Quelite,_Sinaloa "El Quelite, Sinaloa")** A picturesque and attractive tourist town located 38 km northwest of Mazatlán. The El Quelite River passes through it. Its houses contain the Spanish classical influence predominant in the eighteenth century. Charrería is practiced here, as is the Prehispanic game called Ulama. The main economic activities are: livestock, agriculture, farming and fruit growing.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-12)

**Mármol de Salcido:** This town is 32 km from Mazatlán. It was an important cement and line production center. Its current economic activity is the production of chilies, fodder, and tomatoes; its coast has a large number of pristine beaches.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-13)

**El Roble:** Founded in 1867, it is 32 km from Mazatlán. It became the largest sugar mill in the south of the state. Its main economic activities are agriculture and the production of cheese and honey.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-14)

**Siqueiros:** Originally called Penitas, it then adopted the name of San José de Siqueiros, in honor of the patron saint of the town, and the name of its founder. Founded in 1749, it is located 29 km from Mazatlán on the Presidio River. Among its economic activities are agriculture, livestock, and vegetables.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-15)

**La Noria:** Located 35 km northwest of Mazatlán, its first settlers date from the late sixteenth century. Among its economic activities are livestock, agriculture, and saddlery. It is close to Presa Picachos.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-16) A few miles away is the famous Vinata de Los Osuna, a major producer of blue agave, belonging to the family of the same name.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-17)

**El Habal:** A village located 10 km north of Mazatlán. Its inhabitants are engaged in animal husbandry, farming, and fruit growing.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-18)

Mazatlán in Sinaloa

The town of Mazatlán is located in the southern [Sinaloa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinaloa "Sinaloa"). With a land area of 3,068.5 square kilometres (1,184.8 sq mi) (5.3% of the total area of the state), it is Sinaloa's ninth largest municipality. It is bordered on the north by the municipality of [San Ignacio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Ignacio_Municipality,_Sinaloa "San Ignacio Municipality, Sinaloa") and the state of [Durango](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durango "Durango"), on the south by the town of [El Rosario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Rosario,_Sinaloa "El Rosario, Sinaloa") and the Pacific Ocean, on the east by the town of Concordia, and on the west by the Pacific Ocean.

Its average elevation is 10 metres (33 ft) above sea level.

### Geomorphology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Geomorphology")]

The [orography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orography "Orography") is determined by the ramifications of the [Sierra Madre Occidental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sierra_Madre_Occidental "Sierra Madre Occidental") on the northwestern coastal plain bearing towards the Pacific Ocean, where the hills rise towards Vigia, Punta de Materén, and the Monte chair. This orography, before entering the municipality of San Ignacio, takes the name of Sierra del Metate, whose characteristic is the formation of Peak Metate.

At the edge of Mazatlán and [Concordia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concordia,_Sinaloa "Concordia, Sinaloa") runs the Sierra del Metate and Panuco. In this county, the Sierra Madre Occidental is diverted to penetrate Durango, leaving before some detachments, such as the Sierra de San Juan and the Friars, and constitutes, in of its topography, the following hilly areas:

To the north end of town one can see the Friars extending northwest, with elevations ranging from 150 to 1,900 meters above sea level. In the northwestern portion, [El Quelite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Quelite,_Sinaloa "El Quelite, Sinaloa") branches have elevations of 50–700 meters above sea level. On the south-east and north sides, Arroyo de La Noria and some tributaries of the River El Quelite rise. The town of La Noria is located in this same part of the mountain, extending in a northwesterly direction at 300 and 500 meters above sea level. On its western side, the Zapote Brook begins. The Sierra de San Marcos is located in the north at 50 to 700 meters above sea level. Forming the southeastern and northwestern slopes are Brook Copala and some tributaries of the Presidio River.

### Geology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Geology")]

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/Paseo_en_Yate_Mazatlan.jpg/250px-Paseo_en_Yate_Mazatlan.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Paseo_en_Yate_Mazatlan.jpg)

Yacht tour, Mazatlán, Sinaloa

The geological nature of the municipality, primarily made of sedimentary rock, gives rise to the outcrop of fragments of marine and consolidated rocks, and volcanic and metamorphic rocks. Mazatlán generally consists of tonalite and monsonitas belonging to the Middle Tertiary: rhyodacites, rhyolites and ignimbrites with tuffaceous sediments at the base outcrops; andesitic rocks and felsitic late Early Cretaceous conglomerate, sandstone, tuff, sandy tuff "tobalítica", conglomeratic sandstone, arkose storm origins and late Tertiary rhyolitic tuffs, limestones, shales, sandstones and quartzites of coal, gravel and conglomerates that make alluvial fans and slope deposits; rhyolite and rhyodacite tuffs of the same composition, dacite and Lower Tertiary andecita medium; volcanic and pyroclastic spills of andecitic Cretaceous composition; plutonic rocks of basic composition and basic ultra late Paleozoic, Cretaceous limestones, conglomerates of igneous and metamorphic songs; sediments within the course of rivers and streams and sandy sediments, gravel, silt, and orange.

### Hydrology

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Hydrology")]

El Quelite River, and the Zapote, La Noria, and Los Cocos streams form part of the water resources of the municipality in the southwestern and southeastern slopes; these streams increase its volume considerably during the rainy season.

The current of the El Quelite River recorded a catchment of 835 square kilometers, where it drained annually for an average of 107 million cubic meters with variations ranging from 78 to 163 million cubic meters. This hydrological current passing through the town of Mazatlán touches the towns of El Castillo, Las Juntas, Amapa, Los Naranjos, Milkweed, Modesto Station, and El Recreo. After traveling a distance of 100 kilometers from its source, it discharges into the Pacific Ocean. The El Zapote and Los Cocos streams drain in a southeasterly direction to end at the Presidio River, up to the villages from which they take their names.

On the southeast slope of the Sierra del Quelite is the De La Noria stream, and on the north side of it are some tributaries from the El Quelite River. The La Noria stream drains in a southeasterly direction of the town of the same name, and finally ends in the Presidio River.

El Zapote stream is formed on the western slope of the Sierra de La Noria, and moves in a southwesterly direction. In passing, it touches the towns of Zapote and El Recreo, and empties into the Pacific Ocean.

On the northern slopes of the Sierra del Salto, near the village of the same name in the state of Durango, the Presidio River moves southeastward and makes a journey of 167 kilometers. Its catchment area is 5,614 square kilometers, with an average annual expenditure of 900 million cubic meters, a maximum of 2,225 and a minimum of 550 million cubic meters. Populations on its banks are Los Cocos, El Zapote, El Placer, El Tecomate, Copala, El Recodo, Porras, [Villa Unión](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villa_Uni%C3%B3n,_Sinaloa "Villa Unión, Sinaloa"), Alley Ostial, and Alley Rosa.

### Coast

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Coast")]

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/63/Mazatlan_Viejo_198_%2813089107975%29.jpg/250px-Mazatlan_Viejo_198_%2813089107975%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mazatlan_Viejo_198_(13089107975).jpg)

Old photograph of Mazatlán showing a [breakwater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breakwater_(structure) "Breakwater (structure)")

The coasts of the municipality extend over 80 kilometres (50 mi), and sandy beach sediments are formed in the northwestern flank of the head of the municipality. There is a substance classified as berms, which is a soft sediment formation. The coast consists of gravel and conglomerates that form alluvial fans and slope deposits.

In the southwestern corner, Huizache Lagoon occupies an area of 4,000 hectares (40.0 square miles). It receives the maritime influence through the Ostial estuary and freshwater diversion channel, and receives water from the Presidio River.

The coastline of the municipality is lined with shrimp and small-scale flake fishing vessels.

Cooperatives are distributed in the estuaries of the Escopama, Salinitas, El Veintinueve, and Estero Uriah Huizache lagoon.

Most of the islands of the municipality are formed by ignimbrites, rhyolitic tuffs and tuffaceous sandstones of altered and deformed light color.

Bird Island is located between the extreme equatorial coordinates of 106 ° 28'34 " west longitude and 23 ° 15'25" north latitude; its area is about 0.4 square kilometers, 1.1 kilometers long, and maximum and minimum range of 800–650 meters respectively.

Deer Island is located between 106 ° 27'60 " west longitude and 23 ° 14'03" north latitude; its approximate length is 1.850 meters (6 ft 0.8 in), and its width varies between 250 and 700 meters (820 and 2,300 ft).

[Crestón Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crest%C3%B3n_Island "Crestón Island") is located on the western edge of the outer bay of Mazatlán, and it has a length of 700 meters and a maximum width of 800 meters. To the northwest, about 3 miles away, small islands like "Southern Brother" and "Northern Brother" (the first with 46.3 meters in elevation) and Turtle Rock rise 1.5 meters above sea level at its highest ridge.

Goats Island is similar to Crestón's appearance; it has a height above sea level of a little over 50 meters.

Stone Island is the most important part of the municipal coastline; its size is the largest of all because it has 30 square kilometers, and is approximately 14.5 miles long by 2.5 wide. Despite its name, Stone Island is a peninsula that connects to the continent near the [Mazatlán International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n_International_Airport "Mazatlán International Airport").

### Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Climate")]

Located just south of the [Tropic of Cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropic_of_Cancer "Tropic of Cancer"), Mazatlán has a [tropical savanna climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_savanna_climate "Tropical savanna climate") (_Aw_), bordering a hot [semi-arid climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-arid_climate "Semi-arid climate") (_BSh_), with a marked and rather long dry season and an average annual temperature of 25°C.

During the summer months, with the humidity factor, temperatures usually feel well above what the thermometer shows.

During the period of 1940–1980, the municipality experienced an average annual 748 mm of precipitation, with a maximum of 215.4 mm in 24 hours, and 90.4 mm was observed in one hour. During the same period the average evaporation rate per year was 2146.80 mm; the prevailing winds are in a northwesterly direction at an average speed of 5.0 meters.

### Flora and fauna

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Flora and fauna")]

[Video 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/21/Ballenas_mzt.webm?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original)

Whale watching in Mazatlán

The flora of Mazatlán are tabachines, eucalyptus, laurels, and poplars. Its fauna includes birds like ducks, herons, and pelicans. There are [armadillos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armadillo "Armadillo"), [raccoons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raccoons "Raccoons"), and a variety of marine species such as whales, dolphins, turtles, and fish. White-tailed deer is one of the main animals that characterizes Mazatlán. Today, there are fewer animals and plants than before, due to the way humans have changed the ecosystem.

Mazatlán has several protected areas, one of which is the Protection of Flora and Fauna Area (APFF). CACAXTLA Plateau is located between the towns of Mazatlán and San Ignacio in the central part of the state of [Sinaloa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinaloa "Sinaloa"), and contains a portion of the coastal habitats of the state, and is the largest in Sinaloa. This wealth of habitats favors the presence of 66 species of flora and fauna listed in NOM-059-ECOL-2001 and CITES[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-florayfauna-21) and 47.5% of endemism reported for Sinaloa, plus charismatic and commercially important species. At the same time, the protected area is home to a population of 7,964 inhabitants, whose livelihood depends entirely on the extraction of natural resources in this area. The relationship between nature and society in the APFF Cacaxtla Plateau is the focus of this program.

## Economy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Economy")]

Tourism and fishing are the main industries in Mazatlán. The city houses the main beach resorts, and has the second largest fishing fleet in Mexico. The most processed seafood products in the city are shrimp and tuna. The first Mazatlán hotel with a restaurant inside was named Canton La Fonda, and became operational in 1850. It was owned by a Chinese immigrant, Luen-Sing, which called the establishment the Luen-Sing Hotel. In 1864, there were three hotels and three restaurants in Mazatlán, with more opening in the late nineteenth century. Today, more than twenty miles of beaches are the main attraction, and the city contains a large number of hotels, restaurants, bars, and shops. The city is also home to the [Pacífico brewery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pac%C3%ADfico_(beer) "Pacífico (beer)"), a coffee factory, and two power plants.

## Tourism and culture

### Historic Center

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Historic Center")]

The Historic Center of Mazatlán, among whose former inhabitants are French, German, Chinese, Italian, Spanish and [Americans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Americans "Americans") (many contemporary inhabitants of Mazatlán are descended from these), was named Heritage of the Nation on 12 March 2001. A civil association composed of a group of Mazatlán locals have managed to revive this area, along with the support of various organizations, companies, and government authorities. Among the buildings and areas of high cultural value are the [Cathedral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basilica_Cathedral_of_Mazatl%C3%A1n "Basilica Cathedral of Mazatlán"), [Plazuela República](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plazuela_Rep%C3%BAblica "Plazuela República"), [Plazuela Zaragoza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plazuela_Zaragoza,_Mazatl%C3%A1n "Plazuela Zaragoza, Mazatlán"), [Plazuela Machado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plazuela_Machado "Plazuela Machado"), [Plazuela Hidalgo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plazuela_Hidalgo,_Mazatl%C3%A1n "Plazuela Hidalgo, Mazatlán"), the [Angela Peralta Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teatro_%C3%81ngela_Peralta,_Mazatl%C3%A1n "Teatro Ángela Peralta, Mazatlán"), the old Hotel Iturbide (today the [Municipal Arts Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centro_Municipal_de_las_Artes,_Mazatl%C3%A1n "Centro Municipal de las Artes, Mazatlán")), Mansion of Redo, Melchers House, House of Retes, Corvera Building, Bank of London and Mexico Building, Haas House, [Temple of San José](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Templo_de_San_Jos%C3%A9,_Mazatl%C3%A1n "Templo de San José, Mazatlán"), and various others.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-23)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Culture and art")]

Mazatlán hosts several events annually, the most important being the International Carnival of Mazatlán, which was 114 years old in 2012.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-24) Other important events are the Mazatlán Cultural Festival and the José Limón International Dance Festival,[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-26) celebrated every year in the winter and spring, respectively. There is also the Book Fair and Arts of Mazatlán (Feliart) and Mazatlán Book Fair (FELIMAZ).[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-28)

Another important event is the International Motorcycle Week, which attracts thousands of motorcyclists from around the country as well as from abroad, and is held each year during Easter week.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-29)

In sports, Mazatlán is home to the Pacific International Triathlon held in April, and the Pacific International Marathon, which is held every year in late November and early December, and is attended by athletes from around the world.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-30)

In 2012, Mazatlán was chosen as the host city for the tenth installment of [Premios Oye!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premios_Oye! "Premios Oye!"), prizes awarded by the National Academy of Music in Mexico, and the Volleyball Olympic qualifiers for the Olympic Games in London 2012.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-31)

### Mazatlán Carnival

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Mazatlán Carnival")]

Main article: [Carnaval de Mazatlán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carnaval_de_Mazatl%C3%A1n "Carnaval de Mazatlán")

[Video 6](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3b/Combate_Naval_Mzt.webm?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=index&utm_content=original)

Naval Combat in Mazatlán

This is currently one of the most important carnivals in Mexico, since the first parade on Sunday brings together more than 600,000 people for over three hours in the coastal area of the city on the "Avenida del Mar." A novelty that allows tourists to come from all over the world to witness this festival is called "Burning of humor" where tradition says to burn a character (Monigote) representing someone who people think has done a misdeed, which usually means politicians, presidents, or as in 2013, "influenza" was burned. Both of these have negatively affected the country's image in recent years. This is followed by the famous "Naval Combat," depicting the battle that took place against French vessels seeking to land at the port.

A representative element of this carnival are "Monigotes" that are placed in important areas of the city as decorations. These are large figures made of paper mache and supported by large structures. The central events of the carnival are the crowning of the queen of the carnival, a massive event held with a selection of artists. Two parades are scheduled, one on Sunday and another on Mardi Gras (to close the celebration). Decorated floats line much of the coastal walk, with an estimated several hundred thousand spectators in attendance. These include royal courts, ambassadors from around the country and abroad, special guests such as athletes, TV entertainers, and various show-business personalities, as well as hundreds of Mazatlecos of all ages and social conditions.

The Mazatlán Carnival is distinguished from other carnivals for its distinctive accompaniment by Banda Sinaloa music that has transcended the world through what is today called "la onda grupera." Events includes cultural activities (poetry contests, literature prizes, and shows of enormous artistic quality), with which the party extends to all sectors of the population and covers a range of local and tourist tastes.

[![Image 26](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b8/Mazatlan_El_Faro_2.jpg/250px-Mazatlan_El_Faro_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mazatlan_El_Faro_2.jpg)

Mazatlán Lighthouse (El Faro)

[![Image 27](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/Faro_de_Mazatl%C3%A1n.JPG/250px-Faro_de_Mazatl%C3%A1n.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Faro_de_Mazatl%C3%A1n.JPG)

Mazatlán lighthouse seen up close

The Mazatlán lighthouse, called El Faro Lighthouse,[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-mazatlantoday.net-32) is located at the peak of Cerro del Crestón, at the southern end of the peninsular city of Mazatlán. The lighthouse has the distinction of being settled in what was formerly an island, and has a length of 641 meters by 321 meters and a height of 157 meters, making it the highest natural lighthouse in the Americas, and one of the highest operating lighthouses in the world.

In 1821, the Cortes of Cádiz issued a decree certifying the City of Mazatlán as the first port of height of the Mexican Pacific. This introduced Mazatlán as a viable destination for international trade. The decree, along with the rapid growth of large mining and commercial consortia, led to an intensified level of ship traffic. In those days, it was not uncommon for over 60 ships from Europe and the Far East, loaded with different types of merchandise, to reach the port each year. After several days of travel and trading of supplies, these boats would depart Mazatlán loaded with bars of gold and silver from the rich mines of the region.

While the exponential amount of growth in boat traffic into and out of the port undoubtedly benefited the region, it also presented a problem at night. At that time there was no way to indicate to boats in the dark where the marina was located, or how to enter and dock, making it hard for ships to be accurate, which often led to sailors endangering their boats.

The first use of the Isla de Crestón as a lighted marine signal was in 1828. The light facilities, located on top of an imposing hill, were very modest, consisting of only a small stone structure on which fires, fueled by whale oil and wood, or coconut chips, were lit. The fires were fed wood and coal, allowing them to produce a dim light that could only be seen within walking distance, making it of little help to seafarers, especially in bad weather.

El Faro became the answer to the problem. First lit over the Pacific Ocean in 1879, the lighthouse's original lamp was constructed in Paris. It was made of an oil lamp surrounded by mirrors, and a Fresnel lens to focus the light.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-mazatlantoday.net-32) This allowed El Faro's light to be seen from a much further distance, and thus give better navigation services, leading to approaches made with greater precision.

In 1905, the lamp was converted to hydrogen gas, and was made to be able to revolve in a full circle. The final update of the light source came in 1933, when it was converted to electricity, which is what is still there today. To emit its powerful light, El Faro uses a 1,000 watt bulb, which is focused by a Fresnel lens.

It is now one of the top tourist attractions in the city of Mazatlán, and people can hike up to see it up close. The view from the lighthouse is also a big draw for visitors.

### Banda Sinaloense

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Banda Sinaloense")]

Banda Sinaloense or Tambora is a type of musical ensemble, as well as a traditional and popular musical genre, which was established in the early twenties in the state of Sinaloa, in the northwestern region of Mexico. It originates in the European Fanfare style, however, like many other traditional Mexican ensembles, Banda Sinaloense groups perform a variety of musical forms, and their repertoire covers various traditional styles such as rancheras, corridos, polkas, waltzes, mazurkas, and chotis, all tailored to the sensitivity of the inhabitants of this Mexican region: music as well as romantic ballads such as Cumbia.

[![Image 28](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/46/Band%C2%B4s_Sinaloa.jpg/250px-Band%C2%B4s_Sinaloa.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Band%C2%B4s_Sinaloa.jpg)

Example of a Sinaloa band in the early 1900s

The unique sound of the Sinaloa band is very similar to German and French wind instrument bands, though there are differences in styles between north-central and southern parts of the state. In the north-central area, the musical phrasing is lighter and nuanced, more similar to Western European styles, and in the south, the style has a very strong phrasing and a little less nuanced performance, more influenced by the Bavarian German style. Several researchers, have located the origin of these styles to these regions, especially considering foreign interventions in the state and in Mazatlán early in the century, which was inhabited mostly by German immigrants. However, the Swiss ethnomusicologist Helena Simonett explains that the first Sinaloense bands were formed by people who deserted the military and municipal bands, and went to live in mountain villages, adding credence to the Sinaloa founders with the rhythmic influence of Mayo-Yoreme, which have contributed to its essence. Nevertheless, there is an historic agreement which dates the musical influence before the Mazatlán German trade boom (1870–1890), as it would lead not only to distribution of instruments through marketing, but also required a cultural disclosure that could only happen in a close relationship between the carriers of such traditions and the people of the region, and this circumstance only occurred in Mazatlán. That is why the theory of French and Spanish influence on the German influence in other regions of Sinaloa is reinforced as the development of the music of the Sinaloan drum has records and previous history in distant places in the mountains of Sinaloa where there was no German influence. However, post-war French influence intervention and Spanish cultural remnants are present. There is also evidence of the formation of the first organological Mazatlán clusters as well as other parts of Sinaloa, for example: La [Banda El Recodo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banda_El_Recodo "Banda El Recodo") de Don Cruz Lizarraga in 1938, which had a strong German influence in its playing style, and included stringed instruments, in contrast with La Banda Los Tacuichamona (1888), La Banda Los Sirolas Culiacán (1920) and The Band of Brothers Rubio (1929) Mocorito, which were exclusively wind instruments and percussion akin to the Galo-Ibérico fanfare style.

### Sports

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: Sports")]

Baseball is popular among Mazatlecos. The representative team, called [Venados de Mazatlán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venados_de_Mazatl%C3%A1n "Venados de Mazatlán"), is part of the [Mexican Pacific League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Pacific_League "Mexican Pacific League"). The league's season begins in mid-October and ends in late December. Playoffs are in January of every year, and from the eight teams that make up the league, one becomes the representative of Mexico in the [Caribbean Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Series "Caribbean Series").

In Basketball the representative team, called [Venados de Mazatlán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venados_de_Mazatl%C3%A1n_(basketball) "Venados de Mazatlán (basketball)"), is part of the [CIBACOPA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuito_de_Baloncesto_de_la_Costa_del_Pac%C3%ADfico "Circuito de Baloncesto de la Costa del Pacífico"). The league season is played from the last days of March until the first days of June, while the playoffs begin in mid-June and end the first days of July.

Another sport that has been practiced for over 25 years is [soccer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football"), with major achievements both statewide and nationally. On June 2, 2020, it was announced that [Liga MX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liga_MX "Liga MX") club [Monarcas Morelia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monarcas_Morelia "Monarcas Morelia") would be relocating to a new state of the art football stadium in Mazatlán in time for the league's 2020–21 season,[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-33) with rumors that the team would be renamed either Delfines de Mazatlán (Dolphins of Mazatlán) or [Mazatlán F.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n_F.C. "Mazatlán F.C.")[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-34)

Mazatlán is a major sporting center of the country, with important sporting activities such as the [marathon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathon "Marathon") and [triathlon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Triathlon "Triathlon"), in which not only local but also foreign athletes participate.

One of the initial [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") teams in Mazatlán were the Mazatlán Redskins. They now play [American football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_football "American football"), soccer, and volleyball.

### La Isla de la Piedra

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: La Isla de la Piedra")]

La Isla de la Piedra, called Stone Island was born in 1936.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-35) Stone Island is known throughout Mexico for its long sandy beaches, Mexico's third largest coconut grove followed by the length of the southern beach which seems to disappears in the horizon.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-36) The main source of work for the residents of the island is fishing and transportation, as they bring many tourist and locals to the island from Mazatlán due to its popularity. To get to the island, it is possible to go by ferry, water taxi or drive by the 15 Mexico-Nogales road. Activities on the island include boat excursions, swimming, beach activities, and horseback riding.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-37)

### Mazatlán Aquarium

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Mazatlán Aquarium")]

Since its opening on September 13, 1980, Mazatlán Aquarium has been one of the most complete of its kind in Latin America.

It was divided into two main areas, the aquarium and the botanical garden. The aquarium contained exhibits for 50 different fish species and a museum that had temporary exhibitions and permanent displays that included shells, snails, and materials relating to the marine ecosystem. The botanical garden consisted of 1 hectare which included 75 tree species from around the world, and regional species of Sinaloa.

On May 30, 2023, the Gran Acuario Mazatlán was inaugurated, replacing and expanding the old aquarium that was in its place, it was the largest aquarium in Latin America.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-38)

### Observatorio 1873

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=28 "Edit section: Observatorio 1873")]

Main article: [Observatorio 1873](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Observatorio_1873 "Observatorio 1873")

Observatorio 1873 is a tourism park in Mazatlán. In the middle of the 19th century, it began as a military lookout point for defending Mazatlán against hostile ships and piracy.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-Moreno2024-09-01-39) It was transformed in 1873 into Observatorio Mazatlán, an [observatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Observatory "Observatory") focused on data collection in [meteorology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meteorology "Meteorology") and [seismology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seismology "Seismology").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-Moreno2024-09-01-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-Gonz%C3%A1lez2021-01-30-40) Observatorio 1837 opened for vistors in February 2020.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-Moreno2024-09-01-39)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-Gonz%C3%A1lez2021-03-23-41) It includes an _[agave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agave "Agave")_ garden, a [whale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whale "Whale") museum, a [manor house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manor_house "Manor house") museum, an [aviary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aviary "Aviary"), an [iguana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iguana "Iguana") sanctuary, a [zip line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zip_line "Zip line"), and a rooftop bar and restaurant.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n#cite_note-Moreno2024-09-01-39)

### Gastronomy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=29 "Edit section: Gastronomy")]

[![Image 29](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Mariscosmaza.jpg/250px-Mariscosmaza.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mariscosmaza.jpg)

Local Mazatlán dishes

Main dishes in Mazatlán are heavily influenced by seafood. Food specialties include [ceviches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceviche "Ceviche"), [cocktails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocktails "Cocktails"), zarandeado fish, and [aguachile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aguachile "Aguachile"). Other common and prominent foods are smoked marlin and tuna, [chilorio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilorio "Chilorio"), bearded tamales (made with shrimp), Governor tacos, fish crackers and Sinaloa-style grill-roasted chicken.

[![Image 30](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/93/Gastronom%C3%ADa_Mazatl%C3%A1n.jpg/250px-Gastronom%C3%ADa_Mazatl%C3%A1n.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gastronom%C3%ADa_Mazatl%C3%A1n.jpg)

Dish from an informal restaurant in Mazatlán

There is also a variety of restaurants offering international cuisine such as Japanese, Italian and Chinese. Fast food, vegetarian, snacks, meats, and a variety of taquerias with their own specialty foods are also available.

The local cuisine offers a variety of fresh drinks such as [horchata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horchata "Horchata"), barley, coconut, coconut horchata, Tejuino, wines and a range of beers, of which the best known is the local beer called [Pacífico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pac%C3%ADfico_(beer) "Pacífico (beer)"), which has its factory in the harbor. Another well-known drink in the region is a vanilla-flavored beverage called "tonicol."

Typical sweets include coconut candies, jamoncillos, and other candy made with coconut marshmallows from the region.

## Transportation

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=30 "Edit section: Transportation")]

The [Mazatlán International Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazatl%C3%A1n_International_Airport "Mazatlán International Airport") ([IATA Code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IATA_Code "IATA Code"): MZT) has daily domestic flights and international flights to the United States and Canada.

By land, Mazatlán is connected to the north ([Culiacán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culiac%C3%A1n "Culiacán")) and south ([Tepic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tepic "Tepic")) and to [Guadalajara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guadalajara "Guadalajara") via [highway 15](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Federal_Highway_15 "Mexican Federal Highway 15") and the corresponding tolled [Federal Highway 15D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Federal_Highway_15D "Mexican Federal Highway 15D"). To the east, it is connected to [Durango](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Durango "Durango") by [Highway 40](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Federal_Highway_40 "Mexican Federal Highway 40") and the corresponding [Federal Highway 40D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Federal_Highway_40D "Mexican Federal Highway 40D").

Ferries make the daily journey to [La Paz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Paz,_Baja_California_Sur "La Paz, Baja California Sur"), Baja California Sur, while a varied number of cruise ships visit the port every week from the United States.

### The Malecón of Mazatlán

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=32 "Edit section: The Malecón of Mazatlán")]

The Malecón (boardwalk) of Mazatlán is to be considered one of the longest in the world. Its length is about 8.5 kilometres (5.3 mi) along the Pacific coast. Along the Malecón are high cliffs, monuments, roundabouts, historical buildings, hotels, etc. The Malecón is composed of a series of roadways with designated space for pedestrians. The names of these roads vary depending on the stage or time of their construction. From south to north, the roads that compose the Malecón are as follow:

*   Calz. Joel Montes Camarena: which connects the lighthouse, which used to be an island, to the rest of the city.
*   Paseo del Centenario: starting in the previous street and bordering the west at the lookout hill where cliffs are seen, it was built to commemorate the centennial of the Independence of Mexico.
*   Paseo Olas Altas: the oldest section of the boardwalk, it was originally a dike to prevent flooding problems in the 1830s, then it became an embankment which was used as urban space, and eventually it became a recreational space. It was the first part of the city with street lighting, and includes the south side of icebox hill and lookout hill.
*   Paseo Claussen: It was built for the centennial in 1910. It borders the icebox hill and ends at the bay of Puerto Viejo. It was named in honor of George Claussen, who was in command of the Mazatlán Works Agency and promoted the centennial project.
*   Avenida del Mar: This is the most representative and longest section of the boardwalk; it extends along the bay of Puerto Viejo and comprises just over half of all the boardwalk. The panoramic tour ends at the tip, which initiates the Golden Zone (the primary hotel zone), and the avenue changes names twice and continues for several kilometers parallel to the coastline, yet maintains some distance from the coastal hotels.

## Politics

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=33 "Edit section: Politics")]

See also: [Palacio Municipal de Mazatlán](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palacio_Municipal_de_Mazatl%C3%A1n "Palacio Municipal de Mazatlán")

In the municipality of Mazatlán, two electoral preferences exist. While the inhabitants of the receiverships, police stations, and other villages in the municipality continue voting traditionally for the [Institutional Revolutionary Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institutional_Revolutionary_Party "Institutional Revolutionary Party") (PRI), this phenomenon is changing within the city.

Mazatlán has traditionally been governed by municipal leaders from the ruling [Institutional Revolutionary Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institutional_Revolutionary_Party "Institutional Revolutionary Party"). During the municipal elections of 1989, Humberto Rice García (1990–1992) won the municipal presidency as a candidate for the [National Action Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Action_Party_(Mexico) "National Action Party (Mexico)") (PAN). However, the [Institutional Revolutionary Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institutional_Revolutionary_Party "Institutional Revolutionary Party") regained the municipality during the elections of 1992, when Martin Gavica Garduño (1993–1995) won the leadership. Alejandro Camacho Mendoza reclaimed the municipality for his party, PAN, for the 1996–1998 period, and Alejandro Higuera Osuna held it for the 1999–2001 term.

In the 2002–2004 elections, both the National Action Party and the [Institutional Revolutionary Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institutional_Revolutionary_Party "Institutional Revolutionary Party") (PRI) were defeated by the [Labour Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_Party_(Mexico) "Labor Party (Mexico)") candidate, Jorge Alberto Rodriguez Pasos. However, a few months after taking the oath of mayor, Rodriguez Pasos was deposed by the State Congress after being charged for domestic violence, in which his own wife accused him. His place was taken by Gerardo Ramirez Rosete, from the same party. Shortly thereafter, in a move seen as a ruse of the PRI state government, he was replaced by Ricardo Ramírez González, a member of the Institutional Revolutionary Party.

In the 2005–2007 elections, Alejandro Higuera Osuna from PAN won the municipal presidency and held it until June 2007, when he resigned to contest the election for local deputy; on the 12th of that month, he was replaced by Isaac Lopez Arregui.

In the 2008–2010 elections, the Institutional Revolutionary Party regained the town with its candidate Jorge Abel Lopez Sanchez.

Since April 2010, the town of Mazatlán has been ruled by both the [Institutional Revolutionary Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Institutional_Revolutionary_Party "Institutional Revolutionary Party") (PRI) and the [National Action Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Action_Party_(Mexico) "National Action Party (Mexico)"), since the last mayoral election was won by PRI member Jorge Abel Lopez Sanchez, who defeated a former PAN and Petetista government (PT). That was the last time that Mazatlán has had a PRI government.

In July 2010, in the election for Governor, Local, and Municipal presidents' Deputies, the first loss occurred for the PRI governor of [Sinaloa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinaloa "Sinaloa"). [Mario López Valdez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_L%C3%B3pez_Valdez "Mario López Valdez"), former Sinaloa Senator and member of the PRI, was defeated. This ended the PRI hegemony in the state of Sinaloa. Another important event was the third choice Alejandro Higuera Osuna from PAN, who won the municipal presidency of Mazatlán. In addition, the PAN won a historic vote statewide.

## Educational institutions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mazatl%C3%A1n&action=edit&section=34 "Edit section: Educational institutions")]

French explorer Duflot de Mofras notes that by the 1840s, foreign traders based in Mazatlán impelled the opening of the first public school in the city. Still, in 1872, there were only two primary schools. In 1873, the Liceo Rosales, which over time would become the [Autonomous University of Sinaloa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_University_of_Sinaloa "Autonomous University of Sinaloa"), was founded.

Mazatlán has several preschools, elementary, middle, high schools, and universities of both public and private institutions. The [Autonomous University of Sinaloa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomous_University_of_Sinaloa "Autonomous University of Sinaloa") is the largest public university in the city. Other public universities or institutions for higher education include the [University of the West](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universidad_Aut%C3%B3noma_de_Occidente_(Mexico) "Universidad Autónoma de Occidente (Mexico)") and the Polytechnic University of Sinaloa. The remaining universities and institutions of higher education in Mazatlán belong to the private sector and they are the following: Mazatlán Institute of Technology, Nautical School of Mazatlán, [TecMilenio University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TecMilenio_University "TecMilenio University"), [Autonomous University of Durango](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universidad_Aut%C3%B3noma_de_Durango "Universidad Autónoma de Durango"), and the Sinaloa Superior Institute of Technology.

The [National Autonomous University of Mexico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Autonomous_University_of_Mexico "National Autonomous University of Mexico"), [UNAM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNAM "UNAM"), has a presence in the city with an academic unit specializing in marine sciences and the Center for Food Research and Development.

**Waterbury** is a city in the U.S. state of [Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut "Connecticut"). Waterbury had a population of 114,403 as of the [2020 Census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-USCensus2020-3) The city is 33 miles (53 km) southwest of [Hartford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hartford,_Connecticut "Hartford, Connecticut") and 77 miles (124 km) northeast of [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City"). Waterbury is the largest city in the [Naugatuck Valley Planning Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naugatuck_Valley_Planning_Region,_Connecticut "Naugatuck Valley Planning Region, Connecticut") and second-largest city in [New Haven County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Haven_County,_Connecticut "New Haven County, Connecticut").

Throughout the first half of the 20th century, Waterbury had large industrial interests and was the leading center in the United States for the manufacture of [brassware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brass "Brass") (including castings and finishings), as reflected in the nickname the "Brass City" and the city's motto, _Quid Aere Perennius?_ ("What Is More Lasting Than Brass?"). It was also noted for the manufacture of watches and clocks ([Timex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timex_Group_USA "Timex Group USA")).

The city is alongside [Interstate 84](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_84_(Pennsylvania%E2%80%93Massachusetts) "Interstate 84 (Pennsylvania–Massachusetts)") (Yankee Expressway) and [Route 8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_Route_8 "Connecticut Route 8") and has a [Metro-North](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro-North "Metro-North")[railroad station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury_station_(Metro-North) "Waterbury station (Metro-North)") with connections to [Grand Central Terminal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Central_Terminal "Grand Central Terminal"). Waterbury is also home to [Post University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post_University "Post University") and the regional campuses of the [University of Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Connecticut "University of Connecticut"), [University of Bridgeport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Bridgeport "University of Bridgeport"), and [Western Connecticut State University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_Connecticut_State_University "Western Connecticut State University"), as well as [Naugatuck Valley Community College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naugatuck_Valley_Community_College "Naugatuck Valley Community College").

## History

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a9/PostcardWaterburyCTAGWestOptometristSoMainSt1905.jpg/250px-PostcardWaterburyCTAGWestOptometristSoMainSt1905.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:PostcardWaterburyCTAGWestOptometristSoMainSt1905.jpg)

South Main Street, c.1910

The land was originally inhabited by [the Algonquin bands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States"). According to [Samuel Orcutt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Orcutt "Samuel Orcutt")'s history, some Puritan residents of nearby Farmington "found it expedient to purchase the same lands from different tribes, without attempting to decide between their rival claims."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-Orcutt1-7) The original settlement of Waterbury in 1674 was in the area now known as the [Town Plot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Town_Plot_Hill "Town Plot Hill") section. In 1675, the turbulence of [King Philip's War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Philip's_War "King Philip's War") caused the new settlement to be vacated until the resumption of peace in 1677. A new permanent location was found across the river to the east along the Mad River. The original [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algonquin_people "Algonquin people") inhabitants called the area "Matetacoke" meaning "the interval lands."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-8) Thus, the settlement's name was [Anglicized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglicised "Anglicised") to "Mattatuck" in 1673. When the settlement was admitted as the 28th [town](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_town "New England town") in the [Connecticut Colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connecticut_Colony "Connecticut Colony") in 1686,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-9) the name was changed to Waterbury in reference to the numerous streams that emptied into the [Naugatuck River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naugatuck_River "Naugatuck River") from the hills on either side of the valley. At that time, it included all or parts of what later became the towns of [Watertown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watertown,_Connecticut "Watertown, Connecticut"), [Plymouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plymouth,_Connecticut "Plymouth, Connecticut"), [Wolcott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolcott,_Connecticut "Wolcott, Connecticut"), [Prospect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prospect,_Connecticut "Prospect, Connecticut"), [Naugatuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naugatuck,_Connecticut "Naugatuck, Connecticut"), [Thomaston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomaston,_Connecticut "Thomaston, Connecticut"), and [Middlebury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middlebury,_Connecticut "Middlebury, Connecticut").

Growth was slow during Waterbury's first hundred years. The lack of [arable land](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arable_land "Arable land") due to the constant flooding of the [Naugatuck River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naugatuck_River "Naugatuck River") in particular, discouraged many potential settlers. Furthermore, the residents suffered through a great flood in 1691[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-10) and an outbreak of disease in 1712. After a century, Waterbury's population numbered just 5,000.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-11)

Waterbury emerged as an early American industrial power in the 19th century when the city began to manufacture [brass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brass "Brass"), harnessing the waters of the [Mad River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mad_River_(Connecticut) "Mad River (Connecticut)") and [Naugatuck River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naugatuck_River "Naugatuck River") to power the early factories.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-WaterburyObserver1-13) The new brass industry attracted many immigrant laborers from all over the world, leading to an influx of diverse nationalities.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-14) Waterbury was incorporated as a city in 1853 and, as the "Brass Capital of the World", it gained a reputation for the quality and durability of its goods. Brass and copper supplied by Waterbury were used in [Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nevada "Nevada")'s [Boulder Dam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boulder_Dam "Boulder Dam") among myriad applications across the United States.

A famous Waterbury product of the late-19th century was [Robert H. Ingersoll's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingersoll_Watch_Company "Ingersoll Watch Company") one-dollar [pocket watch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pocket_watch "Pocket watch"), five million of which were sold. After this, the clock industry became as important as Waterbury's brass industry. Evidence of these industries can still be seen in Waterbury, as numerous clock towers and old brass factories have become landmarks of the city.

Waterbury produced silverware starting in 1858 by Rogers & Brother, and in 1886 by Rogers & Hamilton.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-Hogan-15) In 1893, Rogers & Brother exhibited wares at the [World's Columbian Exposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World's_Columbian_Exposition "World's Columbian Exposition") in Chicago.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-16) In 1898, both companies became part of the [International Silver Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Silver_Company "International Silver Company"), headquartered in nearby Meriden.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-Hogan-15) Production continued at the Rogers & Brother site until 1938.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-Hogan-15) Designs of the two companies are in the collections of the [Mattatuck Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mattatuck_Museum "Mattatuck Museum") in Waterbury, the [Brooklyn Museum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brooklyn_Museum "Brooklyn Museum") in New York, the [Yale University Art Gallery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_University_Art_Gallery "Yale University Art Gallery") in New Haven, and in many historical societies and museums across the United States.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-18)

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c8/WaterburyEastMain1954.jpg/250px-WaterburyEastMain1954.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:WaterburyEastMain1954.jpg)

East Main Street, 1954

In June 1920, [labor unrest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labor_unrest "Labor unrest") occurred, with striking workers fighting with police on the street. Over 30 were arrested, mostly [Lithuanians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuanian_Americans "Lithuanian Americans"), [Russians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russians_in_America "Russians in America"), [Poles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polish_Americans "Polish Americans"), and [Italians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_Americans "Italian Americans"). The strikers numbered some 15,000,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-19) with most being employed at Scovill, Chase Rolling Mill, and Chase Metal Works. One [striker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strike_action "Strike action") was shot to death by police.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-20)

At its peak during [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), 10,000 people worked at the Scovill Manufacturing Co, later sold to Century Brass. The city's metal manufacturing mills (Scovill Manufacturing, Anaconda American Brass, and [Chase Brass & Copper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chase_Brass_and_Copper_Company "Chase Brass and Copper Company") were the largest) occupied more than 2 million square feet (180,000 m 2) and more than 90 buildings.

On May 24, 1962, the north side of the city was devastated by a [high-end F3 tornado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tornado_outbreak_sequence_of_May_14%E2%80%93June_1,_1962#Bunker_Hill%E2%80%93Fairmount%E2%80%93Waterville%E2%80%93Wolcott%E2%80%93Southington,_Connecticut "Tornado outbreak sequence of May 14–June 1, 1962") that caused widespread damage, destroyed numerous neighborhoods, and left one dead and 50 injured. Damage from the storm was estimated to be at least $5 million.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-StormData-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-Hillcrest1-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-Hillcrest2-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-Hillcrest3-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-Hillcrest4-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-Hillcrest5-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-Hillcrest6-27)

### Historic events

*   Waterbury Land Company was formed in 1807, for the purpose of settling a Connecticut Western Reserve Township named Columbia in Lorain County, Ohio. The draft allotment was purchased for $21,600.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-28)
*   Waterbury's [Fr. Michael J. McGivney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_J._McGivney "Michael J. McGivney") founded the [Knights of Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knights_of_Columbus "Knights of Columbus") in [New Haven, Connecticut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Haven,_Connecticut "New Haven, Connecticut"), on February 2, 1882.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-29) Though the first councils were in Connecticut, the Order spread throughout the United States.
*   Established in 1894, St. Joseph's Church holds the distinction of being the first [Lithuanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuanians "Lithuanians") worshiping community in Connecticut and second oldest in the country.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-30)
*   The first [Unico Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unico_National "Unico National") was founded in Waterbury in 1922 by Dr. Anthony P. Vastola. It grew to 8,000 members and 150 regional groups. The membership is composed of business and professional people of [Italian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italians "Italians") lineage or those who are married to an [Italian-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian-American "Italian-American"). The clubs sponsor educational, cultural and civic programs.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-31)
*   Sacred Heart was the first Catholic high school in Connecticut, September 6, 1922.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-32)
*   One of the first full-length sound motion pictures was made in the 1920s at the studios of the Bristol Co. at Platts Mills by Professor [William Henry Bristol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Henry_Bristol "William Henry Bristol"), who experimented for years with sound pictures.
*   The [Waterbury Clock Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timex_Group_USA "Timex Group USA") produced the [Mickey Mouse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mickey_Mouse "Mickey Mouse") watch[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-33) in 1933 under the [Ingersoll brand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ingersoll_Watch_Company "Ingersoll Watch Company"). The watch was so popular that over 11,000 were sold the first day, and it saved the company from bankruptcy.
*   W1XBS in Waterbury was one of four radio stations in the country that began experimental high fidelity broadcasting in 1934. The station broadcast at 1530 [kHz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KHz "KHz"), and joined the CBS Radio Network on December 1, 1938. They moved to 1590 kHz in 1941, in accordance with the [North American Regional Broadcasting Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_American_Regional_Broadcasting_Agreement "North American Regional Broadcasting Agreement"). The station's broadcasting license was cancelled in 1998 to allow New York's [WWRL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWRL "WWRL") to be upgraded after that station purchased it; at the time it had been known as [WQQW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WQQW_(Connecticut) "WQQW (Connecticut)").
*   Victor Zembruski started his _Polish Eagles_ show on Waterbury radio station [WATR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WATR "WATR") in 1934. As of 2010[[update]](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Waterbury,_Connecticut&action=edit) called _The Zembruski Family Polka Hour_, it is one of the oldest continuously broadcast shows on American radio.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-34)
*   The Chase Dispensary, a medical clinic for employees of the Chase Brass & Copper Co., opened one of the first [birth control](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_control "Birth control") clinics in the country in 1938.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-35)

## Geography

According to the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau"), the city has a total area of 29.0 square miles (75.0 km 2), of which 28.5 square miles (73.9 km 2) is land and 0.42 square miles (1.1 km 2), or 1.46%, is water.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-36)

Waterbury lies in the [humid continental climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humid_continental_climate "Humid continental climate") zone, and normally sees cold, snowy winters and warm, humid summers.

### Neighborhoods

Waterbury's neighborhoods are shaped by the history and geography of the city.

Ethnic communities distinguish the city's 25 neighborhoods. Clusters of shops at the street corners created villages within the city. For many people, home, work and community life were contained within their neighborhood. [Hispanic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hispanic_(U.S._Census) "Hispanic (U.S. Census)") or [Latino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latino_(U.S._Census) "Latino (U.S. Census)") people of any race were 31.2% of the population.

Waterbury has a large [Italian-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian-American "Italian-American") population with 21.46% of its residents claiming Italian heritage.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-43) The Italian influence is especially strong in the Town Plot, Brooklyn, and North End neighborhoods.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-44) Additionally, the city is home to thriving [Albanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albanians "Albanians"), [Cape Verdean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Verde "Cape Verde"), [Brazilian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazil "Brazil"), [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_people "Portuguese people"), and [Lithuanian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuanians "Lithuanians") communities. Waterbury also has a large [Irish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_people "Irish people") community, especially in the Washington Hill section which is home to the city's annual St. Patrick Day's Parade, which, oddly enough, is rarely held on St. Patrick's Day itself. At the beginning of the 21st century, Waterbury had a growing [Orthodox Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orthodox_Jewish "Orthodox Jewish") population.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-45) Waterbury had a significant Jewish population beginning in the late 1800s, initially as a result of [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_Americans "German Americans") immigration. The first [synagogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synagogue "Synagogue") in Waterbury opened in 1872.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-46) In the early 20th century, almost 9,000 [Jews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Jews "American Jews") immigrated from Eastern Europe, with many fleeing persecution. The Orthodox Jewish community has experienced a renaissance since 2000 due to efforts by educators and developers to create an affordable alternative to the high cost of living in established Orthodox communities in New York and New Jersey. This renaissance began with the founding of the [Yeshiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeshiva "Yeshiva") K'tana of Waterbury in 2000; as of 2014, this full-service elementary and middle school has nearly 400 students. Other educational institutions are the Yeshiva Gedolah of Waterbury, which includes a _[mesivta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesivta "Mesivta")_ high school and _[beit medrash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beth\_midrash "Beth midrash")_ (undergraduate) program for approximately 230 students, a [Bais Yaakov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bais_Yaakov "Bais Yaakov") school for girls, and a _[kolel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kolel "Kolel")_. As of the end of 2014, the Waterbury Orthodox community numbers 180 families and includes a _[mikveh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikveh "Mikveh")_, _[eruv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eruv "Eruv")_, and community services such as [Hatzalah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Hatzalah "United Hatzalah") and [Chaverim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chaverim_(volunteers) "Chaverim (volunteers)").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-47)

There were 42,622 households, out of which 31.2% had children under the age of 18 living with them, 34.7% were married couples living together, 28.4% had a single householder with no husband present, and 36.9% were non-families. 31.4% of all households were made up of individuals, and 12.1% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.46 and the average family size was 3.11.

In the city, the population was spread out, with 25.6% under the age of 18, 10.1% from 18 to 24, 27.4% from 25 to 44, 24.3% from 45 to 64, and 12.6% who were 65 years of age or older. The median age was 35.2 years. For every 100 females, there were 89.9 males. For every 100 females age 18 and over, there were 85.8 males.

According to the 2014 5-year American Community Survey (conducted 2010–2014, data released December 3, 2015), the median income for a household in the city was $41,136, compared to $69,899 statewide. In Waterbury, 24.2% of the population, or 26,122 residents of the city, lived below the poverty line, compared to 10.5% statewide. In Waterbury, 36.8% of the child population age 0–17, or 9,984 children in the city, lived below the poverty line, compared to 14% statewide.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterbury,_Connecticut?printable=yes#cite_note-48)
