In 1903, Saint Patrick's Day became an official public holiday in Ireland due to the [Bank Holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank_Holiday "Bank Holiday") (Ireland) Act 1903, an [Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Act_of_parliament "Act of parliament") of the [Parliament of the United Kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_the_United_Kingdom "Parliament of the United Kingdom") introduced by [James O'Mara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_O'Mara "James O'Mara"), an MP from the [Irish Parliamentary Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Parliamentary_Party "Irish Parliamentary Party") (IPP).[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-omara1-64)

The first Saint Patrick's Day parade in Ireland was held in [Waterford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterford "Waterford") in 1903, hundreds of years after the first parade in North America. The week of Saint Patrick's Day 1903 had been declared Irish Language Week by the [Gaelic League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaelic_League "Gaelic League") and in Waterford they opted to have a procession on Sunday 15 March. The procession comprised the Mayor and members of Waterford Corporation, the Trades Hall, the various trade unions and bands who included the 'Barrack St Band' and the '[Thomas Francis Meagher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Francis_Meagher "Thomas Francis Meagher") Band'.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-65) The parade began at the premises of the Gaelic League in George's St and finished in the Peoples Park, where the public were addressed by the Mayor and other dignitaries.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-munster_express-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-67) On Tuesday 17 March, most Waterford businesses—including public houses—were closed and marching bands paraded as they had two days previously.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-68)

On Saint Patrick's Day 1916, the [Irish Volunteers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Volunteers "Irish Volunteers")—an Irish nationalist paramilitary organisation—held parades throughout Ireland. The authorities recorded 38 St Patrick's Day parades, involving 6,000 marchers, almost half of whom were reported to be armed.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-FOOTNOTECroninAdair2002105-69) The following month, the Irish Volunteers launched the [Easter Rising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Rising "Easter Rising") against British rule. This marked the beginning of the [Irish revolutionary period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_revolutionary_period "Irish revolutionary period") and led to the [Irish War of Independence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_War_of_Independence "Irish War of Independence") and [Civil War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Civil_War "Irish Civil War"). During this time, Saint Patrick's Day celebrations in Ireland were muted, although the day was sometimes chosen to hold large political rallies.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-FOOTNOTECroninAdair2002108-70)

The celebrations remained low-key after the creation of the [Irish Free State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Free_State "Irish Free State") in 1922; the only state-organized observance was a military procession and [trooping of the colours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trooping_the_colours "Trooping the colours"), and an Irish-language [mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mass_(Catholic_Church) "Mass (Catholic Church)") attended by government ministers.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-FOOTNOTECroninAdair2002134-71) In 1927, the Irish Free State government [banned the selling of alcohol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prohibition "Prohibition") on St Patrick's Day, although it remained legal in [Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland"). The ban was not repealed until 1961.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-FOOTNOTECroninAdair2002135%E2%80%93136-72)

The first official, state-sponsored Saint Patrick's Day parade in [Dublin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dublin "Dublin") took place in 1931.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-73) Public St Patrick's Day festivities in Ireland have been cancelled three times, all for public health reasons.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-75) In 2001, celebrations were postponed to May due to the [foot-and-mouth outbreak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2001_United_Kingdom_foot-and-mouth_outbreak "2001 United Kingdom foot-and-mouth outbreak"),[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-77)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-78) while in 2020 and 2021 they were cancelled outright due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-79)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-80)[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-84)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-85)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/94/St_Patricks_Day_Inter_Church_Procession%2C_Downpatrick%2C_March_2010_%2803%29.JPG/250px-St_Patricks_Day_Inter_Church_Procession%2C_Downpatrick%2C_March_2010_%2803%29.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:St_Patricks_Day_Inter_Church_Procession,_Downpatrick,_March_2010_(03).JPG)

A Saint Patrick's Day [Christian procession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_procession "Christian procession") in [Downpatrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downpatrick "Downpatrick"), where Saint Patrick is said to be buried

In [Ulster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulster "Ulster"), especially within [Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland") and [County Donegal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Donegal "County Donegal") (particularly East Donegal), the celebration of Saint Patrick's Day was affected by sectarian divisions.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-FOOTNOTECroninAdair2002175%E2%80%93177-86) Up until the late twentieth century, a majority of the population in Ulster, the northern [province](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provinces_of_Ireland "Provinces of Ireland") in Ireland, were [Protestant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulster_Protestants "Ulster Protestants")[Ulster unionists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unionism_in_Ireland "Unionism in Ireland") who saw themselves primarily as British, while a substantial minority were Catholic Irish nationalists who saw themselves primarily as Irish. Although it was a public holiday, Northern Ireland's [Unionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulster_Unionist_Party "Ulster Unionist Party") government did not officially observe St Patrick's Day.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-FOOTNOTECroninAdair2002175%E2%80%93177-86) During the conflict in Northern Ireland known as [the Troubles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Troubles "The Troubles") (late 1960s–late 1990s), public St Patrick's Day celebrations were rare and tended to be associated with the Catholic community.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-FOOTNOTECroninAdair2002175%E2%80%93177-86) In 1976, [loyalists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulster_loyalism "Ulster loyalism")[detonated a car bomb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillcrest_Bar_bombing "Hillcrest Bar bombing") outside a pub crowded with Catholics celebrating St Patrick's Day in [Dungannon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dungannon "Dungannon") in the south-east of [County Tyrone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Tyrone "County Tyrone"); four civilians were killed and many injured. However, some Protestant unionists attempted to 're-claim' the festival, and in 1985 the [Orange Order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orange_Order "Orange Order") held its own Saint Patrick's Day parade.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-FOOTNOTECroninAdair2002175%E2%80%93177-86) Since the end of the conflict in 1998 there have been cross-community St Patrick's Day parades in towns throughout Northern Ireland, which have attracted thousands of spectators.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-FOOTNOTECroninAdair2002175%E2%80%93177-86) In Belfast, [Belfast City Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belfast_City_Hall "Belfast City Hall") flies the [St Patrick's Saltire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Patrick's_Saltire "St Patrick's Saltire") alongside the Union Jack on St Patrick's Day.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-87)

In the mid-1990s the government of the [Republic of Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Ireland "Republic of Ireland") began a campaign to use Saint Patrick's Day to showcase Ireland and its culture.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-hist-88) The government set up a group called [St. Patrick's Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Festival "St. Patrick's Festival"), with the aims of creating a world-class national festival and "to project, internationally, an accurate image of Ireland as a creative, professional and sophisticated country with wide appeal".[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-festival-89) The first Saint Patrick's Festival was held on 17 March 1996. In 1997, it became a three-day event, and by 2006, the festival was five days long. More than 675,000 people attended the 2009 parade, and that year's festival saw almost 1 million visitors, who took part in festivities that included concerts, outdoor theatre performances, and fireworks.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-90) From 2006 to 2012 the [Skyfest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skyfest "Skyfest") formed the centrepiece of the Saint Patrick's Festival.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-92)

The week around Saint Patrick's Day is _[Seachtain na Gaeilge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seachtain\_na\_Gaeilge "Seachtain na Gaeilge")_ ("Irish Language Week"), when more [Irish language](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_language "Irish language") events are held and there is more effort to use the language.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-93)

Christian leaders in Ireland have expressed concern about the secularisation of Saint Patrick's Day. In _The Word_ magazine's March 2007 issue, Fr [Vincent Twomey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vincent_Twomey "Vincent Twomey") wrote, "It is time to reclaim St Patrick's Day as a church festival". He questioned the need for "mindless alcohol-fuelled revelry" and concluded that "it is time to bring the piety and the fun together".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-94)

One of the biggest celebrations outside the cities is in [Downpatrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downpatrick "Downpatrick"), [County Down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Down "County Down"), where Saint Patrick is said to be buried. The shortest Saint Patrick's Day parade in the world formerly took place in [Dripsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dripsey "Dripsey"), [County Cork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Cork "County Cork"). The parade lasted just 23.4 metres and traveled between the village's two pubs. The tradition began in 1999, but ended after five years when one of the pubs closed.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-95) The current shortest Saint Paddy's Day parade has been held in Little Compton, [Rhode Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhode_Island "Rhode Island"), since 2022. The parade lasts only 89 feet. The title is disputed by Hot Springs, [Arkansas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arkansas "Arkansas"), which has hosted the shortest St. Patrick's Day parade since 2004, measuring at 98 feet.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-96)

#### England

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d6/St_Patrick%27s_Day_-_Trafalgar_Square_March_2006.jpg/250px-St_Patrick%27s_Day_-_Trafalgar_Square_March_2006.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:St_Patrick's_Day_-_Trafalgar_Square_March_2006.jpg)

Saint Patrick's Day celebration at [Trafalgar Square](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trafalgar_Square "Trafalgar Square") in London, 2006

In England, the Royal Colonel or [Colonel-in-chief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colonel-in-chief "Colonel-in-chief") traditionally present bowls of shamrock to members of the [Irish Guards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Guards "Irish Guards"), a regiment in the [British Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Army "British Army"), following [Queen Alexandra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Alexandra "Queen Alexandra") introducing the tradition in 1901.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-97) Since 2012, [Catherine, Princess of Wales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine,_Princess_of_Wales "Catherine, Princess of Wales") has presented the bowls of shamrock to the Irish Guards. While female royals are often tasked with presenting the bowls of shamrock, male royals have also undertaken the role, such as [King George VI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_George_VI "King George VI") in 1950 to mark the 50th anniversary of the formation of the Irish Guards, and in 2016 the [Duke of Cambridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William,_Prince_of_Wales "William, Prince of Wales") in place of his wife.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-98)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-99) Fresh Shamrocks are presented to the Irish Guards, regardless of where they are stationed, and are flown in from Ireland.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-100)

While some Saint Patrick's Day celebrations could be conducted openly in Britain pre 1960s, this would change following the commencement by the IRA's bombing campaign on [mainland Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Britain "Great Britain") and as a consequence this resulted in a suspicion of all things Irish and those who supported them which led to people of Irish descent wearing a sprig of shamrock on Saint Patrick's day in private or attending specific events.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-Pages_180%E2%80%93183-101) Today, after many years following the [Good Friday Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Friday_Agreement "Good Friday Agreement"), people of Irish descent openly wear a sprig of shamrock to celebrate their Irishness.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-Pages_180%E2%80%93183-101)

Christian denominations in Great Britain observing his [feast day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feast_day "Feast day") include the [Church of England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_England "Church of England") and the Roman Catholic Church.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-Irish_and_non-Irish_celebrants-102)

[Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham "Birmingham") holds the largest Saint Patrick's Day parade in Britain with a city centre parade[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-103) over a two-mile (3 km) route through the city centre. The organisers describe it as the third biggest parade in the world after Dublin and New York.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-104)

London, since 2002, has had an annual Saint Patrick's Day parade which takes place on weekends around the 17th, usually in Trafalgar Square. In 2008, the water in the Trafalgar Square fountains was dyed green. In 2020, the parade was cancelled due to the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic").[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-105)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-106)

[Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool "Liverpool") has the highest proportion of residents with Irish ancestry of any English city.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-107) This has led to a long-standing celebration on Saint Patrick's Day in terms of music, cultural events and the parade.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-108)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-109)

[Manchester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester "Manchester") hosts a two-week Irish festival in the weeks prior to Saint Patrick's Day. The festival includes an Irish Market based at the city's town hall which flies the Irish tricolour opposite the Union Flag, a large parade as well as a large number of cultural and learning events throughout the two-week period.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-110)

The Scottish town of [Coatbridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coatbridge "Coatbridge"), where the majority of the town's population are of Irish descent,[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-ScotGov-Immigration-111)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-CoatbridgeFestival-112) also has [a Saint Patrick's Day Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day_festival_Coatbridge "St. Patrick's Day festival Coatbridge") which includes celebrations and parades in the town centre.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-CoatbridgeFestival-112)[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-113)

[Glasgow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glasgow "Glasgow") has a considerably large Irish population; due, for the most part, to the Irish immigration during the 19th century. This immigration was the main cause in raising the population of Glasgow by over 100,000 people.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-114) Due to this large Irish population, there are many Irish-themed pubs and Irish interest groups who hold yearly celebrations on Saint Patrick's day in Glasgow. Glasgow has held a yearly Saint Patrick's Day parade and festival since 2007.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-115)

#### Malta

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saint_Patrick%27s_Day&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Malta")]

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/Porte_des_Bombes_on_St_Patrick%27s_Night.jpg/250px-Porte_des_Bombes_on_St_Patrick%27s_Night.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Porte_des_Bombes_on_St_Patrick's_Night.jpg)

[Porte des Bombes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porte_des_Bombes "Porte des Bombes") illuminated in green on Saint Patrick's Day of 2014

The first Saint Patrick's Day celebrations in Malta took place in the early 20th century by soldiers of the [Royal Dublin Fusiliers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Dublin_Fusiliers "Royal Dublin Fusiliers") who were stationed in [Floriana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floriana "Floriana"). Celebrations were held in the Balzunetta area of the town, which contained a number of bars and was located close to the barracks. The Irish diaspora in Malta continued to celebrate the feast annually.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-maltaindependent2018-03-18-116)

Today, Saint Patrick's Day is mainly celebrated in Spinola Bay and [Paceville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paceville "Paceville") areas of [St Julian's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Julian's "St Julian's"),[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-117) although other celebrations still occur at Floriana[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-maltaindependent2018-03-18-116) and other locations.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-118)[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-119) Thousands of Maltese attend the celebrations, "which are more associated with drinking beer than traditional Irish culture."[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-120)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-121)

#### Russia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saint_Patrick%27s_Day&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Russia")]

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/St_Patrick%27s_Day_2012_in_Moscow.jpg/250px-St_Patrick%27s_Day_2012_in_Moscow.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:St_Patrick's_Day_2012_in_Moscow.jpg)

[Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow") hosts an annual Saint Patrick's Day festival

The first Saint Patrick's Day parade in Russia took place in 1992.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-122) Since 1999, there has been a yearly "Saint Patrick's Day" festival in Moscow and other Russian cities.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-123) The official part of the Moscow parade is a military-style parade and is held in collaboration with the Moscow government and the Irish embassy in Moscow. The unofficial parade is held by volunteers and resembles a carnival. In 2014, Moscow Irish Week was celebrated from 12 to 23 March, which includes Saint Patrick's Day on 17 March. Over 70 events celebrating Irish culture in Moscow, St Petersburg, Yekaterinburg, Voronezh, and Volgograd were sponsored by the Irish Embassy, the Moscow City Government, and other organisations.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-124)

In 2017, the [Russian Orthodox Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Orthodox_Church "Russian Orthodox Church") added the feast day of Saint Patrick to [its liturgical calendar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_liturgical_calendar "Eastern Orthodox liturgical calendar"), to be celebrated on 30 March[[O.S.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Style_and_New_Style_dates "Old Style and New Style dates") 17 March].[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-125)

[Madrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madrid "Madrid"),[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-126)[Barcelona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barcelona "Barcelona"),[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-127)[A Coruña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Coru%C3%B1a "A Coruña") and [Benidorm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benidorm "Benidorm") are the biggest cities where great celebrations take place in Spain, but some other smaller cities have started to host Saint Patrick's Day in recent years, such as [El Espinar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Espinar "El Espinar"),[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-128)[Caldas de Reyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caldas_de_Reyes "Caldas de Reyes"), [Pontevedra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontevedra "Pontevedra"), [Salamanca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salamanca "Salamanca"), [Elda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elda "Elda"), [Valladolid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valladolid "Valladolid")[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-129) and [Maspalomas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maspalomas "Maspalomas").

#### Other European countries

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saint_Patrick%27s_Day&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Other European countries")]

[Sarajevo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarajevo "Sarajevo"), the capital city of [Bosnia and Herzegovina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bosnia_and_Herzegovina "Bosnia and Herzegovina") has an Irish expatriate community.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-130)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-131) The community established the [Sarajevo Irish Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarajevo_Irish_Festival "Sarajevo Irish Festival") in 2015, which is held for three days around and including Saint Patrick's Day. The festival organizes an annual parade, hosts Irish theatre companies, screens Irish films and organizes concerts of Irish folk musicians. The festival has hosted numerous Irish artists, filmmakers, theatre directors and musicians such as [Conor Horgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conor_Horgan "Conor Horgan"), Ailis Ni Riain, [Dermot Dunne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dermot_Dunne "Dermot Dunne"), [Mick Moloney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mick_Moloney "Mick Moloney"), [Chloë Agnew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chlo%C3%AB_Agnew "Chloë Agnew") and others.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-132)[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-133)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-134)

Although it is not a national holiday in [Lithuania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lithuania "Lithuania"), the [Vilnia River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vilnia_River "Vilnia River") is dyed green every year on the Saint Patrick's Day in the capital [Vilnius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vilnius "Vilnius").[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-135)

[Norway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norway "Norway") has had a Saint Patrick's Day parade in Oslo since 2000, first organized by Irish expatriates living in Norway, and partially coordinated with the Irish embassy in Oslo.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-136)

While Saint Patrick's Day in [Switzerland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Switzerland "Switzerland") is commonly celebrated on 17 March with festivities similar to those in neighbouring central European countries, it is not unusual for Swiss students to organise celebrations in their own living spaces on Saint Patrick's Eve. Most popular are usually those in Zurich's [Kreis 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aussersihl "Aussersihl"). Traditionally, guests also contribute with beverages and dress in green.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-137)

In [Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germany "Germany") since 1996 the city of [Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Munich "Munich") holds a parade on the weekend before the 17th of March, which has turned into one of the biggest St. Patrck's Day celebrations in continental Europe. In 2026, 30 years after the first parade, around 70 groups comprising together of 1,500 participants marched in the parade and attracted 45,000 spectators.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-138)

### Americas

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saint_Patrick%27s_Day&action=edit&section=15 "Edit section: Americas")]

#### Canada

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saint_Patrick%27s_Day&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Canada")]

Saint Patrick's Day is a government holiday in [Newfoundland and Labrador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newfoundland_and_Labrador "Newfoundland and Labrador").[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-139) The island Newfoundland has strong historic and cultural ties to Ireland and is cited as the most Irish place outside of Ireland.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-140) Approximately 20% of Newfoundland's population consists of [Irish Newfoundlanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Newfoundlanders "Irish Newfoundlanders").

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c5/St._Patrick%27s_Day_Montreal_2007.jpg/250px-St._Patrick%27s_Day_Montreal_2007.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:St._Patrick's_Day_Montreal_2007.jpg)

Montreal hosts one of the longest-running and largest Saint Patrick's Day parades in North America

One of the longest-running and largest Saint Patrick's Day ([French](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_language "French language"): _le jour de la Saint-Patrick_) parades in North America occurs each year in [Montreal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montreal "Montreal"),[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-141) whose [city flag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flag_of_Montreal "Flag of Montreal") includes a [shamrock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shamrock "Shamrock") in its lower-right quadrant. The yearly celebration has been organised by the United Irish Societies of Montreal since 1929. The parade has been held yearly without interruption since 1824. Saint Patrick's Day itself, however, has been celebrated in Montreal since as far back as 1759 by Irish soldiers in the Montreal Garrison following the British conquest of New France.

In [Saint John, New Brunswick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_John,_New_Brunswick "Saint John, New Brunswick") Saint Patrick's Day is celebrated as a week-long celebration. Shortly after the JP Collins Celtic Festival is an Irish festival celebrating Saint John's Irish heritage. The festival is named for a young Irish doctor James Patrick Collins who worked on [Partridge Island (Saint John County)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partridge_Island_(Saint_John_County) "Partridge Island (Saint John County)") quarantine station tending to sick Irish immigrants before he died there himself.

In [Manitoba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manitoba "Manitoba"), the Irish Association of Manitoba runs a yearly three-day festival of music and culture based around Saint Patrick's Day.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-142)

In 2004, the CelticFest Vancouver Society organised its first yearly festival in downtown [Vancouver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver "Vancouver") to celebrate the [Celtic Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_Nations "Celtic Nations") and their cultures. This event, which includes a parade, occurs each year during the weekend nearest Saint Patrick's Day.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-143)

In [Quebec City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec_City "Quebec City"), there was a parade from 1837 to 1926. The [Quebec City St-Patrick Parade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quebec_City_St-Patrick_Parade "Quebec City St-Patrick Parade") returned in 2010 after more than 84 years. For the occasion, a portion of the [New York Police Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City_Police_Department "New York City Police Department") Pipes and Drums were present as special guests.

There has been a parade held in [Toronto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto "Toronto") since at least 1863.[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-144)

The [Toronto Maple Leafs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_Maple_Leafs "Toronto Maple Leafs") hockey team was known as the [Toronto St. Patricks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_St._Patricks "Toronto St. Patricks") from 1919 to 1927, and wore green jerseys. In 1999, when the Maple Leafs played on Saint Patrick's Day, they wore green St Patrick's retro uniforms.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Some groups, notably [Guinness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness "Guinness"), have lobbied to make Saint Patrick's Day a national holiday.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-145)

In March 2009, the [Calgary Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calgary_Tower "Calgary Tower") changed its top exterior lights to new green CFL bulbs just in time for Saint Patrick's Day. Part of an environmental non-profit organisation's campaign (Project Porchlight), the green represented environmental concerns. Approximately 210 lights were changed in time for Saint Patrick's Day, and resembled a [Leprechaun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leprechaun "Leprechaun")'s hat. After a week, white CFLs took their place. The change was estimated to save the Calgary Tower some $12,000 and reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 104 tonnes.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-146)

Since 2019, the City of [Waterloo, Ontario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterloo,_Ontario "Waterloo, Ontario") has had to contend with an ever-growing massive street party that has coincided with the Saint Patrick's Day celebrations. In 2023, police could be seen putting fences up on Ezra Avenue to discourage partiers to participate in the unauthorized event that has cost the city as much as $750,000 a year for police, paramedics, and municipal services.[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-147)

#### United States

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saint_Patrick%27s_Day&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: United States")]

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/ChicagoStPatricksDay2015.jpg/250px-ChicagoStPatricksDay2015.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ChicagoStPatricksDay2015.jpg)

The [Chicago River dyed green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_River#Saint_Patrick's_Day "Chicago River")[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-148)

Main article: [Saint Patrick's Day in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Patrick's_Day_in_the_United_States "Saint Patrick's Day in the United States")

Saint Patrick's Day, while not a legal holiday in the United States, is nonetheless widely recognised and observed throughout the country as a celebration of Irish and [Irish-American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish-American "Irish-American") culture. Celebrations include prominent displays of the colour green, religious observances, numerous parades, and copious consumption of alcohol.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-Irish_Culture_3-11) The holiday has been celebrated in what is now the U.S. since 1600, with the first parade occurring in 1601.[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-149)

It is customary for the Irish [Taoiseach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taoiseach "Taoiseach") (Irish Prime Minister) to meet with the [President of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") on or around Saint Patrick's Day.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-irishtimes.com-150)[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-151) Traditionally, the Taoiseach presents the US president a [Waterford Crystal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterford_Crystal "Waterford Crystal") bowl filled with shamrocks.[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-irishexaminer.com-152) This tradition began in 1952 when the Irish Ambassador to the US, [John Hearne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hearne_(lawyer) "John Hearne (lawyer)"), sent a box of shamrocks to President [Harry S. Truman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_S._Truman "Harry S. Truman"). From then, it became a yearly custom for the Irish ambassador to send Saint Patrick's Day shamrocks to an official in the US President's administration, although on some occasions the shamrocks were given personally by the Irish Taoiseach or Irish President to the US president in Washington.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-irishtimes.com-150)[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-irishexaminer.com-152) After the meeting between Taoiseach [Albert Reynolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Reynolds "Albert Reynolds") and President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") in 1994, the presenting of the shamrocks became a yearly custom.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-irishtimes.com-150)[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-153)

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/77/D%C3%ADa_de_San_Patricio_Buenos_Aires_2.jpg/250px-D%C3%ADa_de_San_Patricio_Buenos_Aires_2.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:D%C3%ADa_de_San_Patricio_Buenos_Aires_2.jpg)

Celebrations in [Buenos Aires](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buenos_Aires "Buenos Aires") centre on Reconquista street

In Buenos Aires, a party is held in the downtown street of Reconquista, where there are several Irish pubs;[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-155)[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-156) in 2006, there were 50,000 people in this street and the pubs nearby.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-157) Neither the Catholic Church nor the [Irish community](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_settlement_in_Argentina "Irish settlement in Argentina"), the fifth largest in the world outside Ireland,[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-158) take part in the organisation of the parties.

#### Montserrat

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saint_Patrick%27s_Day&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Montserrat")]

The island of [Montserrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montserrat "Montserrat") is known as the "Emerald Island of the [Caribbean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caribbean_Sea "Caribbean Sea")" because of its founding by [Irish refugees from Saint Kitts and Nevis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_immigration_to_Saint_Kitts_and_Nevis "Irish immigration to Saint Kitts and Nevis"). Montserrat is one of three places where Saint Patrick's Day is a public holiday, along with Ireland and the Canadian province of Newfoundland and Labrador. ### Oceania

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saint_Patrick%27s_Day&action=edit&section=21 "Edit section: Oceania")]

#### Australia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saint_Patrick%27s_Day&action=edit&section=22 "Edit section: Australia")]

[![Image 21](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ee/St_Patrick%27s_Parade_Brisbane-13_%288562155117%29.jpg/250px-St_Patrick%27s_Parade_Brisbane-13_%288562155117%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:St_Patrick's_Parade_Brisbane-13_(8562155117).jpg)

Saint Patrick's Parade in Brisbane

Saint Patrick's Day is not a public holiday in Australia, although it is celebrated each year across the country's states and territories.[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-160)[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-161)[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-162) Festivals and parades are often held on weekends around 17 March in cities such as [Sydney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sydney "Sydney"),[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-163)[Brisbane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brisbane "Brisbane"),[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-164)[Adelaide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide "Adelaide"),[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-165) and [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne").[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-166) On occasion, festivals and parades are cancelled. For instance, Melbourne's 2006 and 2007 Saint Patrick's Day festivals and parades were cancelled due to sporting events ([Commonwealth Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commonwealth_Games "Commonwealth Games") and [Australian Grand Prix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australian_Grand_Prix "Australian Grand Prix")) being booked on and around the planned Saint Patrick's Day festivals and parades in the city.[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-167) In Sydney the parade and family day was cancelled in 2016 due to financial problems.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-168)[[169]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-169) However, Brisbane's Saint Patrick's Day parade, which was cancelled at the outbreak of [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") and wasn't revived until 1990,[[170]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-170) was not called off in 2020 as precaution for the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), in contrast to many other Saint Patrick's Day parades around the world.[[171]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-171)

The first mention of Saint Patrick's Day being celebrated in Australia was in 1795, when Irish convicts and administrators, Catholic and Protestant, in the [penal colony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penal_colony "Penal colony") came together to celebrate the day as a national holiday, despite a ban against assemblies being in place at the time.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-O'Farrell-172) This unified day of Irish nationalist observance would soon dissipate over time, with celebrations on Saint Patrick's Day becoming divisive between religions and social classes, representative more of Australianness than of Irishness and held intermittingly throughout the years.[[172]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-O'Farrell-172)[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-173)[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-174) Historian [Patrick O'Farrell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patrick_O'Farrell "Patrick O'Farrell") credits the [1916 Easter Rising](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Easter_Rising "Easter Rising") in [Dublin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dublin "Dublin") and [Archbishop Daniel Mannix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archbishop_Daniel_Mannix "Archbishop Daniel Mannix") of [Melbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melbourne "Melbourne") for re-igniting St Patrick's Day celebrations in Australia and reviving the sense of Irishness amongst those with Irish #### New Zealand

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saint_Patrick%27s_Day&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: New Zealand")]

From 1878 to 1955, Saint Patrick's Day was recognised as a public holiday in New Zealand, together with [St George's Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_George's_Day "St George's Day") (England) and [St Andrew's Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Andrew's_Day "St Andrew's Day") (Scotland).[[182]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-182)[[183]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-183)[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-184)[Auckland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auckland "Auckland") attracted many Irish migrants in the 1850s and 1860s, and it was here where some of the earliest Saint Patrick's Day celebrations took place, which often entailed the hosting of community picnics.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-Bueltmann-185) However, this rapidly evolved from the late 1860s onwards to include holding parades with pipe bands and marching children wearing green, sporting events, concerts, balls and other social events, where people displayed their Irishness with pride.[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-Bueltmann-185) While Saint Patrick's Day is no longer recognised as a public holiday, it continues to be celebrated across New Zealand with festivals and parades at weekends on or around 17 March.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-186)[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-187)

In the [university city](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/College_town "College town") of [Dunedin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dunedin "Dunedin"), Saint Patrick's Day (commonly referred to as "St Paddy's") is widely regarded as one of the largest social events of the year. Among the student population, the day is associated with informal drinking traditions such as "six before six" (consuming six alcoholic drinks before 6:00 am), "wine before nine" (consuming a bottle of wine before 9:00 am), and "goon before noon" (consuming a cask of wine before 12:00 pm).[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-188)

### Asia

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saint_Patrick%27s_Day&action=edit&section=24 "Edit section: Asia")]

[![Image 22](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/aa/Saint_Patricks_Day_in_Motomachi_Yokohama.jpg/250px-Saint_Patricks_Day_in_Motomachi_Yokohama.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Saint_Patricks_Day_in_Motomachi_Yokohama.jpg)

Saint Patrick's Day in [Motomachi, Yokohama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motomachi,_Yokohama "Motomachi, Yokohama")

Saint Patrick's parades are now held in many locations across Japan.[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-url2013_St_Patricks_Day_Parades_in_Japan-189) The first parade, in Tokyo, was organised by The Irish Network Japan (INJ) in 1992.

The Irish Association of Korea has celebrated Saint Patrick's Day since 1976 in [Seoul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seoul "Seoul"), the capital city of [Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korea "South Korea") and [Busan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Busan "Busan"), second largest city in Korea. The plaxe of the parade and festivals are [Itaewon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itaewon "Itaewon") of Seoul and [Seomyeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seo-myeon,_Busan "Seo-myeon, Busan") of Busan. It is sponsored by Embassy of Ireland in Korea.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-190)

In [Malaysia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysia "Malaysia"), the St Patrick's Society of Selangor, founded in 1925, organises a yearly St Patrick's Ball, described as the biggest Saint Patrick's Day celebration in Asia. [Guinness Anchor Berhad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness_Anchor_Berhad "Guinness Anchor Berhad") also organises 36 parties across the country in places like the [Klang Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klang_Valley "Klang Valley"), [Penang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penang "Penang"), [Johor Bahru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johor_Bahru "Johor Bahru"), Malacca, [Ipoh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ipoh "Ipoh"), [Kuantan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuantan "Kuantan"), [Kota Kinabalu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kota_Kinabalu "Kota Kinabalu"), [Miri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miri,_Malaysia "Miri, Malaysia") and [Kuching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuching "Kuching").

### UN Peacekeeping missions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saint_Patrick%27s_Day&action=edit&section=25 "Edit section: UN Peacekeeping missions")]

Irish [United Nations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations "United Nations") (UN) peacekeepers outside Ireland also celebrate Saint Patrick's Day. For example, in 2021, the [United Nations Disengagement Observer Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Disengagement_Observer_Force "United Nations Disengagement Observer Force")'s Irish contingent led a parade in Syria where members received shamrocks and 35 personnel were presented with the [UN Peacekeeping Medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Nations_Peacekeeping_Medal?action=edit&redlink=1 "United Nations Peacekeeping Medal (page does not exist)").[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-191)

### International Space Station

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saint_Patrick%27s_Day&action=edit&section=26 "Edit section: International Space Station")]

[![Image 23](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Chris_Hadfield_in_the_Space_Station_on_Saint_Patrick%27s_Day.jpg/250px-Chris_Hadfield_in_the_Space_Station_on_Saint_Patrick%27s_Day.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chris_Hadfield_in_the_Space_Station_on_Saint_Patrick's_Day.jpg)

Astronaut [Chris Hadfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Hadfield "Chris Hadfield") wearing green in the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") on Saint Patrick's Day, 2013

Astronauts on board the [International Space Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Space_Station "International Space Station") have celebrated the festival in different ways. Irish-American [Catherine Coleman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_Coleman "Catherine Coleman") played a hundred-year-old flute belonging to [Matt Molloy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Molloy "Matt Molloy") and a [tin whistle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tin_whistle "Tin whistle") belonging to [Paddy Moloney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddy_Moloney "Paddy Moloney"), both members of the Irish music group [The Chieftains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Chieftains "The Chieftains"), while floating weightless in the space station on Saint Patrick's Day in 2011.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-192)[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-193)[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-194) Her performance was later included in a track called "The Chieftains in Orbit" on the group's 2012 album, _[Voice of Ages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voice\_of\_Ages "Voice of Ages")_.[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-195)

[Chris Hadfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Hadfield "Chris Hadfield") took photographs of Ireland from Earth orbit, and a picture of himself wearing green clothing in the space station, and posted them online on Saint Patrick's Day in 2013. He also posted online a recording of himself singing "[Danny Boy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Boy "Danny Boy")" in space.[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-196)[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-197)

## Criticism

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saint_Patrick%27s_Day&action=edit&section=27 "Edit section: Criticism")]

Saint Patrick's Day celebrations have been criticised, particularly for their association with [public drunkenness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_drunkenness "Public drunkenness") and [disorderly conduct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disorderly_conduct "Disorderly conduct"). Some argue that the festivities have become too [commercialised](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commercialism "Commercialism") and tacky,[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-FOOTNOTECroninAdair2002240-198)[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-199) and have strayed from their original purpose of honouring Saint Patrick and Irish heritage.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-200)[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-201)[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-FOOTNOTECroninAdair2002240-198) Irish American journalist [Niall O'Dowd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Niall_O'Dowd "Niall O'Dowd") has criticised attempts to recast Saint Patrick's Day as a celebration of [multiculturalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiculturalism "Multiculturalism") rather than a celebration of Irishness.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-202)

[![Image 24](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e2/Man_in_Leprechaun_Outfit_on_St_Patrick%27s_Day.jpg/250px-Man_in_Leprechaun_Outfit_on_St_Patrick%27s_Day.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Man_in_Leprechaun_Outfit_on_St_Patrick's_Day.jpg)

Man in a [leprechaun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leprechaun "Leprechaun") outfit on Saint Patrick's Day

Saint Patrick's Day celebrations have also been criticised for fostering demeaning stereotypes of Ireland and [Irish people](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_people "Irish people").[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-FOOTNOTECroninAdair2002240-198) An example is the wearing of '[leprechaun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leprechaun "Leprechaun") outfits',[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-203) which are based on derogatory 19th century caricatures of the Irish.[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-204) In the run up to Saint Patrick's Day 2014, the [Ancient Order of Hibernians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Order_of_Hibernians "Ancient Order of Hibernians") successfully campaigned to stop major American retailers from selling novelty merchandise that promoted negative Irish stereotypes.[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-205)

Saint Patrick's Day celebrations outside Ireland have been described by critics as displays of "[Plastic Paddyness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plastic_Paddy "Plastic Paddy")"; where foreigners [appropriate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_appropriation "Cultural appropriation") and misrepresent [Irish culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_culture "Irish culture"), claim Irish identity, and enact Irish stereotypes.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-206)

[LGBTQ groups in the US](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBTQ_rights_in_the_United_States "LGBTQ rights in the United States") were long banned from marching in Saint Patrick's Day parades in [New York City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") and [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston"). In 1995, the [Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States")'s landmark decision in _[Hurley v. Irish-American Gay, Lesbian, and Bisexual Group of Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurley\_v.\_Irish-American\_Gay,\_Lesbian,\_and\_Bisexual\_Group\_of\_Boston "Hurley v. Irish-American Gay, Lesbian, and Bisexual Group of Boston")_ affirmed event organizers' rights to determine the messages that their events conveyed, effectively permitting the exclusion of LGBTQ groups. The bans on LGBTQ group participation in New York City and Boston were lifted in 2014 and 2015, respectively.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-207)[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-208) However, LGBTQ groups still experience barriers to participation[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-209) and have organized alternative, inclusive events such as [St. Pat's for All](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Pat's_for_All "St. Pat's for All") in [Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queens "Queens").

**Saint Patrick's Day**, or the **Feast of Saint Patrick** ([Irish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_language "Irish language"): _Lá Fhéile Pádraig_, [lit.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Literal_translation "Literal translation")'the Day of the Festival of Patrick'), is a religious and cultural [holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holiday "Holiday") held on 17 March, the traditional death date of [Saint Patrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Patrick "Saint Patrick") (c.385– c.461), the foremost [patron saint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patron_saint "Patron saint") of [Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ireland "Ireland").

Saint Patrick's Day was made an official Christian [feast day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feast_day "Feast day") in the early 17th century and is observed by the [Catholic Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church"), the [Anglican Communion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anglican_Communion "Anglican Communion") (especially the [Church of Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_of_Ireland "Church of Ireland")),[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-7) the [Eastern Orthodox Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Orthodox_Church "Eastern Orthodox Church"), and the [Lutheran Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lutheranism "Lutheranism"). The day commemorates Saint Patrick and the arrival of [Christianity in Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity_in_Ireland "Christianity in Ireland"), and, by extension, celebrates the [heritage and culture of the Irish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culture_of_Ireland "Culture of Ireland") in general.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-RitschelMichallon2022-5)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-Irish_Culture_1-8) Celebrations generally involve public parades and festivals, [céilithe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C%C3%A9ilithe "Céilithe"), and the wearing of green attire or [shamrocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shamrock "Shamrock").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-Irish_Culture_2-9) Christians who belong to liturgical denominations also attend [church services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Church_service "Church service").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-Irish_Culture_1-8)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-Irish_Culture_5-10) Historically, the [Lenten](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenten "Lenten") restrictions [on fasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christian_fasting "Christian fasting") and [drinking alcohol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity_and_alcohol "Christianity and alcohol") were lifted for the day, which has encouraged the holiday's tradition of revelry.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-Irish_Culture_1-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-Irish_Culture_2-9)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-Irish_Culture_3-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-Irish_Culture_4-12)

Saint Patrick's Day is a [public holiday](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_holiday "Public holiday") in the [Republic of Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Ireland "Republic of Ireland"),[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-13)[Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland"),[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-14) the Canadian province of [Newfoundland and Labrador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newfoundland_and_Labrador "Newfoundland and Labrador") (for provincial government employees), and the British Overseas Territory of [Montserrat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montserrat "Montserrat"). It is also widely celebrated in places with a large [Irish diaspora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_diaspora "Irish diaspora") community, such as [Great Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Britain "Great Britain"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-15)[Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canada "Canada"), the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States"), [Australia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Australia "Australia"), [New Zealand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Zealand "New Zealand"), and [South Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Africa "South Africa").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-16) Saint Patrick's Day is celebrated in more countries than any other [national festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Day "National Day").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-FOOTNOTECroninAdair2002242-17) Modern celebrations have been greatly influenced by those of the Irish diaspora, particularly those that developed in North America. However, there has been criticism of Saint Patrick's Day celebrations for having become too commercialised, for their connections to [drinking culture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drinking_culture "Drinking culture"), and for fostering negative stereotypes of the Irish people.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-18)

## Saint Patrick

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saint_Patrick%27s_Day&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Saint Patrick")]

Main article: [Saint Patrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Patrick "Saint Patrick")

Saint Patrick was a 5th-century Christian missionary and bishop in Ireland. Much of what is known about Saint Patrick comes from the _Declaration_, which was allegedly written by Patrick himself. It is believed that he was born in [Roman Britain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_Britain "Roman Britain") in the fourth century, into a wealthy [Romano-British](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romano-British_culture "Romano-British culture") family. His father was a Christian [deacon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deacon "Deacon") and his grandfather a [priest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priest "Priest"). According to the _Declaration_, at the age of sixteen, he was kidnapped by Irish raiders and taken as a slave to [Gaelic Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaelic_Ireland "Gaelic Ireland").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-19) It says that he spent six years there working as a shepherd and that during this time he [found God](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_conversion "Religious conversion"). The _Declaration_ says that God told Patrick to flee to the coast, where a ship would be waiting to take him home. After making his way home, Patrick went on to become a priest.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Patrick's_Day#cite_note-20)

According to tradition, Patrick returned to Ireland to convert the [pagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celtic_polytheism "Celtic polytheism") Irish to Christianity. The _Declaration_ says that he spent many years evangelising in the northern half of Ireland and converted thousands.

Tradition holds that he died on 17 March and was buried at [Downpatrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downpatrick "Downpatrick"). Over the following centuries, many legends grew up around Patrick and he became Ireland's foremost saint.

## Celebration and traditions

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Saint_Patrick%27s_Day&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Celebration and traditions")]

According to legend, Saint Patrick used the three-leaved [shamrock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shamrock "Shamrock") to explain the [Holy Trinity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Trinity "Holy Trinity") to [Irish pagans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Celtic_religion "Ancient Celtic religion").
