**Wladimir Klitschko**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-3) (born 25 March 1976) is a Ukrainian former [professional boxer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_boxer "Professional boxer") who competed from 1996 to 2017. He held multiple [heavyweight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavyweight "Heavyweight") world championships between 2000 and 2015, including [unified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unified_champion "Unified champion")[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-4) titles between 2008 and 2015. During this time he also held the [International Boxing Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Boxing_Organization "International Boxing Organization") (IBO) and _[Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Ring\_(magazine) "The Ring (magazine)")_ magazine titles. Klitschko is considered by some to be one of the greatest heavyweight champions ever.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-5)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-6)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-7)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-8) He was known for his exceptional [knockout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knockout "Knockout") power, using a strong [jab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jab "Jab"); [straight right hand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_(boxing) "Cross (boxing)"); and [left hook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hook_(boxing) "Hook (boxing)"), quick hand speed, formidable physical strength (which he often employed when [clinching](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinch_fighting "Clinch fighting") opponents), and his athletic [footwork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Footwork_(martial_arts) "Footwork (martial arts)") and mobility – unusual for boxers of his size.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-9)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-10)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-11)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-12)

As an [amateur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amateur_boxing "Amateur boxing"), Klitschko represented Ukraine at the [1996 Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Olympics "1996 Olympics"), winning a gold medal in the [super-heavyweight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super-heavyweight "Super-heavyweight") division and ending his amateur run with 134 wins and 6 losses. After turning professional later that year, he defeated [Chris Byrd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Byrd "Chris Byrd") in 2000 to win the [World Boxing Organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Boxing_Organization "World Boxing Organization") (WBO) heavyweight title. Klitschko's first reign as champion ended in an upset knockout loss to [Corrie Sanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrie_Sanders "Corrie Sanders") in 2003, which was followed by another upset knockout loss to [Lamon Brewster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamon_Brewster "Lamon Brewster") in 2004. It was during this time that Klitschko hired [Emanuel Steward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emanuel_Steward "Emanuel Steward") as his trainer, which began an eight-year partnership that lasted until Steward's death in 2012. In particular, Steward was credited with Klitschko's transition from an aggressive puncher to a more defensively-oriented boxer, much as he had done with [Lennox Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lennox_Lewis "Lennox Lewis") from 1995 to 2003.

From 2004 to 2015, Wladimir and his brother [Vitali Klitschko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitali_Klitschko "Vitali Klitschko") (himself a multiple-time world champion) dominated heavyweight boxing, a period typically known as the "[Klitschko Era](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klitschko_brothers "Klitschko brothers")" of the division.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-13)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-14) In 2006, Wladimir regained a portion of the world heavyweight championship after defeating Byrd in a rematch to win the [International Boxing Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Boxing_Federation "International Boxing Federation") (IBF) and IBO titles. He won his second WBO title by defeating [Sultan Ibragimov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sultan_Ibragimov "Sultan Ibragimov") in 2008. Following his defeat of [Ruslan Chagaev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruslan_Chagaev "Ruslan Chagaev") in 2009, Klitschko was awarded the _Ring_ title, and lastly he won the [World Boxing Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Boxing_Association "World Boxing Association") (WBA) title ([Unified version](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WBA_(Unified) "WBA (Unified)"), later [Super version](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WBA_(Super) "WBA (Super)")) from [David Haye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Haye "David Haye") in 2011.

During Klitschko's reign as world heavyweight champion, his fights would reportedly generate up to 500 million viewers worldwide.[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-note1-23) Klitschko holds all-time records for the [longest time spent as world heavyweight champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_heavyweight_boxing_championship_records_and_statistics#Longest_title_reigns "World heavyweight boxing championship records and statistics") at 4,382 days and [most fighters beaten for the world heavyweight championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_heavyweight_boxing_championship_records_and_statistics#Most_opponents_beaten_in_title_fights "World heavyweight boxing championship records and statistics"), at 23.[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-32) He also holds records for the [most wins and title defences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undisputed_championship_(boxing)#Unified_championship "Undisputed championship (boxing)") of the unified championship[[note 1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-nw1-33) in professional boxing history. In 2011, both Wladimir and Vitali entered the [Guinness World Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness_World_Records "Guinness World Records") book as brothers with most world heavyweight title fight wins (30 at the time; 40 as of 2020).[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-guinness-world-records-most-hw-title-fight-wins-between-brothers-34)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-35)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-36) Klitschko was inducted into the International Boxing Hall of Fame Class of 2021, having been elected in his first year of eligibility.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-ibhof-class-2021-1-37)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-ibhof-class-2021-2-38)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wladimir_Klitschko&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Klitschko was born on 25 March 1976 in Semipalatinsk, [Kazakh SSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazakh_Soviet_Socialist_Republic "Kazakh Soviet Socialist Republic"), Soviet Union ([Semey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semey "Semey"), Kazakhstan).[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-boxrec-39)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-40)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-41) He is the son of Nadiia Ulianivna Klychko (née Bulyno) and Volodymyr Rodionovych Klychko (1947–2011), a [Soviet Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Air_Force "Soviet Air Force") major general and a [military attaché](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_attach%C3%A9 "Military attaché") of [USSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USSR "USSR") in [East Germany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Germany "East Germany"). He is the younger brother of former [WBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Boxing_Council "World Boxing Council"), WBO, and Ring magazine heavyweight champion [Vitali Klitschko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitali_Klitschko "Vitali Klitschko"), the incumbent [Mayor of Kyiv](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayor_of_Kyiv "Mayor of Kyiv").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-42) Klitschko's paternal grandmother was [Jewish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashkenazi_Jews "Ashkenazi Jews").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-43)

The Klitschko brothers lived as children in Czechoslovakia from 1980 to 1985, where their father was stationed with the [Soviet Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Group_of_Forces "Central Group of Forces"). They attended a school designated for children of Soviet soldiers in the town of [Mimoň](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mimo%C5%88 "Mimoň") in Northern Bohemia.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-44)

The Klitschko family lived in [Pripyat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pripyat "Pripyat"), [Ukrainian SSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukrainian_Soviet_Socialist_Republic "Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic") from 1985 to 1986, when the town was evacuated following the [Chernobyl nuclear disaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chernobyl_disaster "Chernobyl disaster"). The father was one of the commanders in charge of cleaning up the effects of the disaster in 1986 and was afterward diagnosed with cancer.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-45) He later served as a military attache at the embassy of Ukraine in Germany.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-46)

Both Wladimir and Vitali hold PhDs[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-47)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-48) in sports science,[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-LA_Times_14_October_2015-49) with Wladimir's dissertation discussing how much training to give to young athletes between 14 and 19 based on the development of their bodies.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-50) As a reference to their PhDs, Wladimir is announced as "Dr. Steelhammer", a nickname similar to his brother, Vitali, who goes by "Dr. Ironfist".

## Amateur career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wladimir_Klitschko&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Amateur career")]

Klitschko started training in [amateur boxing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amateur_boxing "Amateur boxing") with Brovary Olympic Reserve School in the late 1980s. In the early 1990s, Klitschko was coached in Poland's [Gwardia Warszawa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gwardia_Warsaw "Gwardia Warsaw") boxing club, where, according to [Jerzy Kulej](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerzy_Kulej "Jerzy Kulej"), "He and his brother used to demolish our boys."[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-51) In 1993, he won the Junior European Championships as a [heavyweight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavyweight "Heavyweight"). In 1994, he received 2nd place at the Junior World Championships in [Istanbul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Istanbul "Istanbul"), Turkey, losing to Cuban [Michel López Núñez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michel_L%C3%B3pez_N%C3%BA%C3%B1ez "Michel López Núñez") in the finals.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-52) In 1995, he won the gold medal at the Military Championships in [Ariccia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ariccia "Ariccia"), Italy, defeating [Luan Krasniqi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luan_Krasniqi "Luan Krasniqi"), to whom he had lost in the third round of the World Championships in Berlin, Germany earlier that year. In 1996, he captured 2nd place as a Super Heavyweight at the European Championships in [Vejle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vejle "Vejle"), Denmark losing to [Alexei Lezin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexei_Lezin "Alexei Lezin") on points (1–6) in the finals. He defeated Lezin later that year on points (4–1) in the semi-finals at the [1996 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics "1996 Summer Olympics") in [Atlanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta "Atlanta").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-53) Klitschko had an amateur record of 134 wins (65 KO) and 6 losses. Of his six amateur losses, two were by [walkover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amateur_boxing#Reesults "Amateur boxing") (equivalent to a no-contest in a professional context), three were by points (to Michel López, Alexei Lezin, and Luan Krasniqi, all of whom he defeated in rematches), and one was by RSCI.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-54) The latter result happened at the 14th Copenhagen Cup - Copenhagen, Denmark - November 1993, when his bout with [Don Diego Poeder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Diego_Poeder "Don Diego Poeder") was stopped in the first round due to a cut.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-55)

He first achieved world attention at the [1996 Summer Olympics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics "1996 Summer Olympics") in [Atlanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlanta "Atlanta"), Georgia. He defeated [Paea Wolfgramm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paea_Wolfgramm "Paea Wolfgramm") to win the [Super-Heavyweight gold medal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_medalists_in_boxing "Olympic medalists in boxing").

## Professional career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wladimir_Klitschko&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Professional career")]

> "Wladimir hits very hard, harder than (Mike) Tyson. At one point, they ran twelve 800-meter [roughly a half mile] sprints, each under 3 minutes, with a minute rest between each one. I timed every one and every one was under 3 minutes. I never saw a heavyweight do anything even close to that. They work their asses off. To be able to do that, two 250-pound guys – whew. They're two of the best athletes I've ever trained."

—[Freddie Roach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freddie_Roach_(boxing) "Freddie Roach (boxing)"), who trained both the Klitschko brothers and [Mike Tyson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Tyson "Mike Tyson"), on the athleticism of the brothers.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-57)

### Early career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wladimir_Klitschko&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Early career")]

Klitschko turned professional with Universum Box-Promotion in Hamburg under the tutelage of [Fritz Sdunek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fritz_Sdunek "Fritz Sdunek"), often being featured on fight cards alongside his elder brother Vitali. After building an undefeated record of 24–0 with 21 KOs, he suffered his first loss to 24–13–1 [Ross Puritty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_Puritty "Ross Puritty"), in what was Klitschko's first and only professional fight in Ukraine. Puritty forced Klitschko, who had at that time not gone beyond eight rounds, to punch himself out. Klitschko began to be overwhelmed in the tenth round and went down twice but was allowed to continue. At the start of the eleventh round, with Puritty continuing to land hard punches, Klitschko's trainer, Fritz Sdunek, entered the ring and stopped the fight.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-58) Three years later, Klitschko's brother Vitali stopped Puritty in the eleventh round himself. On 18 March 2000, Klitschko fought [Paea Wolfgramm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paea_Wolfgramm "Paea Wolfgramm"), whom he fought previously in the 1996 super-heavyweight Olympic finals. In their professional rematch, Klitschko knocked Wolfgramm out in the first round.

### Klitschko vs. Byrd, Jefferson, Shufford

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wladimir_Klitschko&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Klitschko vs. Byrd, Jefferson, Shufford")]

Main article: [Chris Byrd vs. Wladimir Klitschko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Byrd_vs._Wladimir_Klitschko "Chris Byrd vs. Wladimir Klitschko")

Wladimir Klitschko got his chance to fight for the world heavyweight championship on 14 October 2000 against [WBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Boxing_Organization "World Boxing Organization") champion [Chris Byrd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Byrd "Chris Byrd"). Byrd, considered one of the most avoided fighters in the heavyweight division at the time,[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-invincible-byrd-59)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-what-i-like-about-byrd-60) won the title six months earlier on 1 April from Wladimir's brother [Vitali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitali_Klitschko "Vitali Klitschko") (who had a perfect record of 27 fights, 27 wins, 27 KOs coming into the fight),[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-invincible-byrd-59)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-byrd-vs-vitali-61) being a late replacement for [Donovan Ruddock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donovan_Ruddock "Donovan Ruddock"). In that fight, Byrd was trailing on the scorecards (83–88, 83–88, & 82–89) but was declared the winner after Vitali retired on his stool between 9th and 10th rounds due to shoulder injury.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-invincible-byrd-59) Byrd's title defence against Wladimir was scheduled to take place at [Kölnarena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K%C3%B6lnarena "Kölnarena") in [Cologne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cologne "Cologne") and was billed as "Revenge Of The Brother".[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-eyeonthering-62) In a fight that was aired on [pay-per-view](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pay-per-view "Pay-per-view") in the United Kingdom,[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-63) Wladimir won the WBO world heavyweight title from Byrd by a wide [unanimous decision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unanimous_decision "Unanimous decision") (UD) with scores of 120–106, 119–107, and 118–108, flooring his opponent twice.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-64)

Klitschko's first defence of the WBO title came on 24 March 2001 against [Derrick Jefferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derrick_Jefferson "Derrick Jefferson"). Jefferson, regarded as a big and athletic [brawler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_styles_and_technique#Slugger "Boxing styles and technique") and a fan-friendly attraction,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-jefferson-harris-65) was coming into the bout with a record of 23 wins in 26 bouts, with 19 of those wins coming inside the distance (18 of them inside the first three rounds, 11 of them - in the first round).[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-66)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-jefferson-record-67) Jefferson was mostly known for the sixth-round [knockout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knockout "Knockout") (KO) of [Maurice Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Harris_(boxer) "Maurice Harris (boxer)"), which was named [_The Ring_ Knockout of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ring_magazine_Knockout_of_the_Year "The Ring magazine Knockout of the Year") in 1999. He was 4–2 in the last six fights, losing by [technical knockout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Technical_knockout "Technical knockout") (TKO) to [David Izon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Izon "David Izon"), in a fight he was winning on the scorecards but punched himself out,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-68) and [Oleg Maskaev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oleg_Maskaev "Oleg Maskaev") in round four after breaking an ankle during the first knockdown in the first round.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-69)

For the bout, Jefferson weighed in at 260.25 lbs, the heaviest in his professional career and 20 pounds heavier than in his previous bout.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-jefferson-record-67) The additional weight appeared to be muscle.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-jefferson-l-70) The fight lasted only two rounds. In the first round, Klitschko knocked Jefferson down with a short left hook. After the first round Jefferson's left eye was swollen.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-jefferson-l-70)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-annihilates-jefferson-71) Klitschko knocked him down twice more in round two, once with a straight right hand and again with another left hook, with the fight being stopped after the last knockdown, declaring Klitschko the winner by TKO in the second round. Klitschko earned $1 million for the fight.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-annihilates-jefferson-71)

Klitschko's next title defence was scheduled less than five months later on 4 August 2001. The fight took place at the [Mandalay Bay Events Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandalay_Bay_Events_Center "Mandalay Bay Events Center") in [Paradise, Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradise,_Nevada "Paradise, Nevada") against hometown fighter, [Charles Shufford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Shufford "Charles Shufford"). At the time, Shufford had a 17–1 record, coming off of wins against [Jimmy Thunder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Thunder "Jimmy Thunder") and [Lamon Brewster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamon_Brewster "Lamon Brewster").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-shufford-72) Shufford weighed in at 234 lbs., 17 pounds lighter than in his previous bout.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-shufford-record-73) Shufford, having played [George Foreman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Foreman "George Foreman") opposite [Will Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Smith "Will Smith") in the movie [_Ali_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_(2001_film) "Ali (2001 film)"), entered the ring with Smith by his side.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-shufford-smith-74) Klitschko knocked Shufford down three times, once in round two, once in round three (both times with a straight right hand) and in round six with a left hook, with referee stopping the bout after the third knockdown. According to punch stats, Klitschko landed 58 of 262 punches (22%) and Shufford connected on 16 of 190 (8%).[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-shufford-stats-75)

### Klitschko vs. Botha, Mercer, McCline

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wladimir_Klitschko&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Klitschko vs. Botha, Mercer, McCline")]

Main articles: [Wladimir Klitschko vs. Ray Mercer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko_vs._Ray_Mercer "Wladimir Klitschko vs. Ray Mercer") and [Wladimir Klitschko vs. Jameel McCline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko_vs._Jameel_McCline "Wladimir Klitschko vs. Jameel McCline")

Klitschko returned to Germany for the next defence of his WBO title against [Francois Botha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francois_Botha "Francois Botha"). The fight took place at [Hanns-Martin-Schleyer-Halle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanns-Martin-Schleyer-Halle "Hanns-Martin-Schleyer-Halle") in [Stuttgart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stuttgart "Stuttgart"), the same venue where Botha had fought [Axel Schulz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axel_Schulz "Axel Schulz") for the [IBF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IBF "IBF") title six years earlier, in the most watched boxing match in [German TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_TV "German TV") history.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-botha-schulz-76)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-botha-schulz-de-77) According to Botha's coach [Abel Sanchez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abel_Sanchez "Abel Sanchez"), Botha was in the best shape of his career.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-botha-klitschko-east-side-78) The South African contender was game in the opening rounds, trying to catch Klitschko with the right hook, but Klitschko was successfully keeping him at the end of his jab.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-botha-klitschko-east-side-78) In the eighth round, Klitschko caught him with a counter right hand and then hit Botha with several shots, knocking him down with a left hook. Botha got up, but was unsteady on his feet and had both eyes swollen, proceeding the referee to stop the bout.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-botha-klitschko-east-side-78)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-botha-l-79)

Klitschko had his next title defence scheduled three months later, on 29 June 2002 at [Etess Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Etess_Arena "Etess Arena") in [Atlantic City, New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atlantic_City,_New_Jersey "Atlantic City, New Jersey"), against former WBO heavyweight titleholder [Ray Mercer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Mercer "Ray Mercer"). It was the first time in his professional career that Klitschko fought an [Olympic Gold medalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Olympic_medalists_in_boxing "List of Olympic medalists in boxing"). 41-year-old Mercer, having fought [Lennox Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lennox_Lewis_vs._Ray_Mercer "Lennox Lewis vs. Ray Mercer") and [Evander Holyfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evander_Holyfield "Evander Holyfield") throughout his career, was expected to be a tough challenge for Klitschko that would give him and [Lennox Lewis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lennox_Lewis "Lennox Lewis"), the [WBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Boxing_Council "World Boxing Council") and [_The Ring_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ring_(magazine) "The Ring (magazine)") champion, a second common opponent (along with Francois Botha) and a bout comparable to [Lewis vs. Tyson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lennox_Lewis_vs._Mike_Tyson "Lennox Lewis vs. Mike Tyson").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-mercer-80)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-legacy-81) During the build-up to the bout, Mercer referred to Klitschko as "Russian [Tommy Morrison](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Mercer_vs._Tommy_Morrison "Ray Mercer vs. Tommy Morrison")".[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-legacy-81) Since his comeback in 2001, Mercer had won four fights over journeymen, three of them inside two rounds, prior to the Klitschko bout.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-mercer-boxrec-82)

Klitschko dominated Mercer throughout the entire bout, stopping Mercer in the sixth round. At 2:48 of the first round, Klitschko dropped Mercer with a left hook, becoming only the second man to drop Mercer.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-mercer-80) Throughout the fight, Klitschko was frequently landing combinations of stiff left jabs, left hooks, and straight right hands. By the fifth round, Mercer's face was swollen and his right eye was cut.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-mercer-80) In the sixth, Klitschko unleashed a barrage of punches, prompting the referee to stop the bout. Klitschko became the first fighter to defeat Mercer inside the distance.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-mercer-80) According to [CompuBox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CompuBox "CompuBox") statistics, Klitschko landed 193 total punches out of 429 thrown (104 power punches out of 167), while Mercer landed 54 shots out of 124 (only 5 power punches landed out of 10 thrown).[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-mercer-80)

Klitschko returned to Mandalay Bay Event Center for his sixth defence on 7 December 2002 against [Jameel McCline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jameel_McCline "Jameel McCline"). McCline, having made his professional boxing debut in 1995, became an established contender after defeating [Michael Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Grant_(boxer) "Michael Grant (boxer)"), knocking him down with the first punch thrown and ultimately stopping him in 43 seconds.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-mccline-record-83)[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-84) Prior to fighting Klitschko, McCline had defeated two more heavyweight contenders, [Lance Whitaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lance_Whitaker "Lance Whitaker") and [Shannon Briggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannon_Briggs "Shannon Briggs"), by wide unanimous decisions.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-mccline-record-83) Being 6 ft 6 in tall with an 82 in reach, McCline was of similar height and longer reach than Klitschko,[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-85) while also being 22 lbs heavier.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-mccline-record-83) Many opinion polls gave Klitschko a 60–40 advantage over McCline.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-wlad-vs-mccline-86) The fight was the main event of the card that also featured [Floyd Mayweather Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Floyd_Mayweather_Jr. "Floyd Mayweather Jr.") defending the WBC lightweight title against [Jose Luis Castillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jose_Luis_Castillo "Jose Luis Castillo").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-mccline-event-87)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-mccline-88)

The fight turned out to be tentative, with Klitschko winning almost every round using his jab and superior footwork. At the end of the tenth round, Klitschko staggered McCline with a barrage of left hooks and overhand rights, and ultimately knocked him down with a left-right combination.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-wlad-vs-mccline-86) Before the start of the eleventh round, McCline's corner threw in the towel, giving Klitschko his 36th career win by stoppage.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-wlad-vs-mccline-86) At the time of the stoppage, the scorecards were 98–91, 99–90 (twice), all in favour of the champion.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-wlad-vs-mccline-86) CompuBox stats showed that Klitschko landed 181 of his 433 punches thrown (42%), and McCline landed 61 of 307 (20%).[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-mccline-88)

The following week after Klitschko's win over McCline, Chris Byrd, whom Klitschko defeated for the WBO world title, beat Evander Holyfield to become IBF world champion.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-byrd-vs-holyfield-89)

### Klitschko vs. Sanders, Brewster

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wladimir_Klitschko&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Klitschko vs. Sanders, Brewster")]

Main articles: [Wladimir Klitschko vs. Corrie Sanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko_vs._Corrie_Sanders "Wladimir Klitschko vs. Corrie Sanders") and [Wladimir Klitschko vs. Lamon Brewster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko_vs._Lamon_Brewster "Wladimir Klitschko vs. Lamon Brewster")

[![Image 25](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/40/Wladimir_Klitschko.jpg/250px-Wladimir_Klitschko.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wladimir_Klitschko.jpg)

Klitschko in 2004

After failing to reach agreements with [Kirk Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kirk_Johnson "Kirk Johnson"), [Fres Oquendo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fres_Oquendo "Fres Oquendo"), [Lou Savarese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lou_Savarese "Lou Savarese") and [Danny Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Williams_(boxer) "Danny Williams (boxer)"), Universum ultimately signed a 4-fight contract with [Corrie Sanders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corrie_Sanders "Corrie Sanders"), who was ranked No.9 contender by WBO at the time. According to the agreement, Sanders' first fight was going to be for the WBO world heavyweight title. The fight was scheduled to take place on 8 March 2003 in [Hanover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanover "Hanover"), Germany. Klitschko later admitted that he came to the fight unmotivated and was already thinking about the vacation he was going to enjoy after the fight.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-90) Klitschko suffered an upset TKO loss to Sanders. With thirty seconds left in the opening round, Wladimir threw a jab but Sanders countered with a big left hook, prompting Klitschko to enter a clinch. While in the clinch, Sanders landed another left hook that sent Klitschko to the canvas. Klitschko got up but was dropped again almost immediately. The following round, Sanders continued his assault on a visibly hurt Klitschko, dropping him twice more at the beginning of the round. The referee waived it off after the fourth knockdown. The fight was named Upset of the Year by [The Ring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Ring_(magazine) "The Ring (magazine)") for 2003.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-91)

After winning two minor bouts in Germany and enlisting the services of boxing trainer [Emanuel Steward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emanuel_Steward "Emanuel Steward"), Klitschko again fought for the vacant WBO title on 10 April 2004, in [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas "Las Vegas"), against Lamon Brewster. Klitschko dominated Brewster through the course of the first four rounds, sending him to the canvas in the fourth;[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-strannyi-boi-klitschko-92) however, things turned around in the fifth when Klitschko began tiring and Brewster's punches began backing him up. Not defending himself and leaning into ropes for support, Klitschko took a standing eight count. On unsteady legs, Klitschko fell to the canvas after the bell and the referee stopped the fight for his safety.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-93) When talking about the fight, Emmanuel Steward said: "Wladimir was in incredible shape. I've never seen anything like this in my career. I know what it looks like when a boxer is getting hurt from punches. There was definitely something else that caused problems for Wladimir".[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-brewster-perelomnyi-boi-94)

Shortly after the fight Klitschko was rushed into hospital. An examination showed Klitschko's blood sugar level almost two times higher than the permissible norm. According to members of Klitschko's team, the doctor told them that Klitschko had been "inches away" from falling into a [diabetic coma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diabetic_coma "Diabetic coma"), and that with blood sugar level that high, Klitschko would have been incapable of handling a single proper training session.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-vitali-raskryl-podrobnosti-otravleniya-wladimira-95)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-kak-otravili-klitschko-96)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-2000-ua-97)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-3-porazheniya-klitschko-98) After returning from the examination to the hotel, he fell ill with nausea, followed by physical weakness.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-The_Ring_no._6-99)

Judd Bernstein, the lawyer representing Klitschko, suggested that he was a victim of an ongoing fight fixing in Las Vegas (which also included fraudulent medical reports), which was investigated by FBI at the time.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-100)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-The_Irish_Times-101) Bernstein pointed out that in the last 48 hours before the beginning of the fight, the betting odds in favour of Klitschko rapidly dropped from 11-to-1 to 3,5-to-1 suggesting somebody knew that Brewster had an unfair advantage in the fight. [Dr Margaret Goodman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Goodman "Margaret Goodman"), the chairwoman of the Nevada State Athletic Commission's medical advisory board and Nevada's chief ringside physician was in the ring and attending to Klitschko seconds after the referee stopped the fight. Her initial diagnosis of a Grade 3 concussion was confirmed at the hospital after further tests. Goodman was sceptical of the theory that Klitschko had been drugged.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-The_Irish_Times-101)

After the fight, Wladimir's cutman Joe Souza was fired. During the fight, Souza used vaseline on Wladimir's face but also body, which had never been done in any of Klitschko's previous fights. As a replacement, the team hired [Jacob "Stitch" Duran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacob_Duran "Jacob Duran").[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-vitali-raskryl-podrobnosti-otravleniya-wladimira-95)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-delo-ob-otravlenii-klitschko-102)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-2000-ua-97)

### Klitschko vs. Williamson, Castillo, Peter

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wladimir_Klitschko&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Klitschko vs. Williamson, Castillo, Peter")]

Main article: [Wladimir Klitschko vs. Samuel Peter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko_vs._Samuel_Peter "Wladimir Klitschko vs. Samuel Peter")

Following his loss to Brewster, Klitschko began his journey back towards the top of the heavyweight division. First, he faced hard-hitting [DaVarryl Williamson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DaVarryl_Williamson "DaVarryl Williamson").[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-williamson-103) The fight took place at [Caesars Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caesars_Palace "Caesars Palace") in [Las Vegas, Nevada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas,_Nevada "Las Vegas, Nevada").[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-williamson-record-104) Williamson dropped Klitschko forty seconds into the second round, but was outboxed throughout the rest of the bout.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-williamson-103) An accidental head butt in the closing seconds of the fifth round caused Klitschko bleeding from a cut above his right eye. Due to the cut, the fight was prematurely stopped, with Klitschko being declared the winner by technical decision. Two of the judges scored the fight identically 49–46 in favour of Klitschko, while the third judge had Williamson winning 48–47.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-williamson-klitschko-105)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-williamson-klitschko-w-106)

After defeating [Eliseo Castillo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliseo_Castillo "Eliseo Castillo") by fourth-round TKO, Klitschko signed to fight [Samuel Peter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samuel_Peter "Samuel Peter") in an IBF and WBO eliminator. Coming into the bout, Klitschko was viewed by many as the underdog[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-peter-1-107) against the 7-to-5 favourite Peter who had won all of his 24 fights, with 21 of them having ended inside the distance. At the time, Samuel Peter was considered one of the brightest prospects in the heavyweight division. Distinguished boxing coaches [Angelo Dundee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angelo_Dundee "Angelo Dundee") and [Teddy Atlas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teddy_Atlas "Teddy Atlas") expected Peter to win.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-gendlin-108)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-peter-1-bout-109) Wladimir's team, including his brother Vitali, were worried about Wladimir, and were against this fight to happen. Wladimir, however, insisted on fighting Peter, claiming that beating a feared, hard-hitting fighter like Samuel Peter would help him to regain his stock and become mandatory challenger for two heavyweight belts.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-110)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-111)

The first four rounds were tentative, with Klitschko working behind the jab, not allowing Peter to close the distance. At the end of the third, Peter staggered Klitschko with a powerful left hook. He hurt Klitschko again in the fifth with another left hook, sending Klitschko to the canvas with the [rabbit punch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabbit_punch "Rabbit punch"). The referee counted it as the knockdown. Peter immediately went for the attack after Klitschko got up, dropping him again with the rabbit punch. The referee scored it as the second knockdown.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-book_golden_klitschko_brothers-112) Klitschko regained composure and outboxed Peter through sixth to ninth rounds, with Peter frequently trying to hit Klitschko with the rabbit punch whenever escaping from a clinch.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-book_golden_klitschko_brothers-112)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-peter-l-113) Near the end of the tenth round Peter staggered Wladimir with a hard right hand, eventually sending Klitschko to the canvas with another right when Wladimir was backing away. In the 11th and 12th rounds, Klitschko was trying to keep Peter at the distance using straight punches. Peter caught him with a left hook in the last round, but was unable to capitalise on it. Instead, Klitschko caught him with a hard counter left hook of his own, staggering Peter for the first time in the fight.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-book_golden_klitschko_brothers-112)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-peter-l-113) Eventually the bout went the distance, with Klitschko winning the fight by clear unanimous decision (UD). All the judges scored the bout identically 114–111.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-vs-peter-1-bout-109)[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-114)

### Klitschko vs. Byrd II, Brock, Austin

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wladimir_Klitschko&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Klitschko vs. Byrd II, Brock, Austin")]

Main articles: [Chris Byrd vs. Wladimir Klitschko II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Byrd_vs._Wladimir_Klitschko_II "Chris Byrd vs. Wladimir Klitschko II"), [Wladimir Klitschko vs. Calvin Brock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko_vs._Calvin_Brock "Wladimir Klitschko vs. Calvin Brock"), and [Wladimir Klitschko vs. Ray Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko_vs._Ray_Austin "Wladimir Klitschko vs. Ray Austin")

On 22 April 2006, in [Mannheim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mannheim "Mannheim"), Germany, Klitschko faced Chris Byrd for a second time, this time for the IBF heavyweight title. At the time of the bout, Byrd was ranked as the best heavyweight by _The Ring_, while Klitschko was ranked eighth.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-115) Coming into the fight, Klitschko was viewed as the favourite. Many observers expected Klitschko to dominate Byrd similarly to their first bout.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-116)

> _April 22nd, 2006 may be one of the most momentous dates in the history of boxing. On that day, Wladimir Klitschko of Ukraine will most likely easily defeat Chris Byrd of the United States for Byrd's IBF heavyweight title. If that result occurs, it may mark the dawning of a new era in boxing. Three of the four major titlists will be from Eastern Europe. Like the flood waters of [Hurricane Katrina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane\_Katrina "Hurricane Katrina") that swept away much of New Orleans, a rising tidal wave of Eastern European fighters threatens to sweep away American supremacy in the heavyweight division, putting an end to an era that began with the reign of [John L. Sullivan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John\_L.\_Sullivan "John L. Sullivan") — 124 years ago._

_(John Hively, boxingscene.com[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir\_Klitschko#cite\_note-117))_

Klitschko defeated Byrd by TKO in the seventh round, becoming a two-time heavyweight world champion in the process. Klitschko dominated the fight using his jab and superior reach, knocking Byrd down twice, once in round five and once in round seven. Byrd beat the count after the second knockdown, but his face was battered and bloody, and the fight was waved off.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-118) At the time of the stoppage, judge Roy Francis had the challenger winning every round, while two other judges, Steve Epstein and Robert Hoyle, gave Klitschko all but one round.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-119)

In his first title defence, Klitschko agreed to face then-undefeated heavyweight contender [Calvin Brock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvin_Brock "Calvin Brock"). With a record of 29–0, 22 KOs, Brock was considered one of the most promising and demanded American heavyweight prospects at the time. In an ESPN interview in July 2005, [Mike Tyson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Tyson "Mike Tyson") named him and Samuel Peter as his favourite fighters from the new crop of heavyweights.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-brock-build-up-1-120)[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-brock-espn-29-0-121)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-tyson-interview-espn-122) In the build-up, Brock expressed confidence in his abilities: "I can adopt to every style. He's big like Jameel McCline, but a better fighter. I will beat him and become the heavyweight champion of the world. Klitschko has a good jab, but they also said [Timur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timur_Ibragimov "Timur Ibragimov")'s best weapon was his jab. I have a good jab myself. I can adapt to anybody's style, anybody's strength and turn their weapon against them." He also dismissed claims that the division lacks strong competition: "The heavyweight division is stacked with a bunch of talent. It's not weak, definitely not weak. The division is pretty strong and that's why the title keeps changing hands."[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-brock-build-up-1-120)[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-brock-build-up-2-123)

The fight took place on 11 November 2006 at [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden "Madison Square Garden").[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-124) In the opening rounds, Brock's economical but effective movement made Klitschko reluctant to throw punches, with Wladimir not being able to fully establish his rhythm.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-brock-espn-125) In between the third and fourth rounds, Klitschko's trainer [Emmanuel Steward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Steward "Emmanuel Steward") urged Wladimir to press the action. Klitschko started fighting more aggressively, hurting Brock several times with the right cross. In the fifth round, Brock opened a cut under Klitschko's left eye that started bleeding heavily in the sixth. In the seventh round, Wladimir caught Brock with a counter right hand before sending him to the canvas with another straight right.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-brock-espn-125)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-brock-l-126) Brock was able to get up but was unsteady on his feet, prompting the referee to stop the bout.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-brock-espn-125)[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-brock-l-126)

Klitschko then faced mandatory challenger [Ray Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Austin_(boxer) "Ray Austin (boxer)") on 10 March 2007, at the [SAP Arena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAP_Arena "SAP Arena") in Mannheim, Germany. 36-year-old Austin was mostly known for draws against [Sultan Ibragimov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sultan_Ibragimov "Sultan Ibragimov"), [Larry Donald](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Donald "Larry Donald") and [Lance Whitaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lance_Whitaker "Lance Whitaker"). In preparation for the fight, Austin was trained by a prominent coach Stacey McKinley.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-127) Klitschko won by a second-round KO with four consecutive left hooks to Austin's head. Klitschko did not throw a single right hand in that fight.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-128)

### Klitschko vs. Brewster II, Ibragimov, Thompson

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Wladimir_Klitschko&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Klitschko vs. Brewster II, Ibragimov, Thompson")]

Main articles: [Wladimir Klitschko vs. Lamon Brewster II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko_vs._Lamon_Brewster_II "Wladimir Klitschko vs. Lamon Brewster II"), [Wladimir Klitschko vs. Sultan Ibragimov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko_vs._Sultan_Ibragimov "Wladimir Klitschko vs. Sultan Ibragimov"), and [Wladimir Klitschko vs. Tony Thompson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko_vs._Tony_Thompson "Wladimir Klitschko vs. Tony Thompson")

Klitschko then avenged one of his previous losses as he defeated Lamon Brewster on 7 July 2007, in Cologne, Germany. Brewster's [corner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornermen "Cornermen") asked the referee to stop the fight at the end of the sixth round. It was later revealed that Klitschko fought most of the fight with a broken middle finger on his left hand.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-129)

By the end of October 2007, Wladimir Klitschko started negotiations with then-WBO world heavyweight champion [Sultan Ibragimov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sultan_Ibragimov "Sultan Ibragimov") about the unification showdown in the near future. This would be the first heavyweight unification fight since 13 November 1999 when WBC champion [Lennox Lewis defeated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lennox_Lewis_vs._Evander_Holyfield_II "Lennox Lewis vs. Evander Holyfield II") then-WBA and IBF champion [Evander Holyfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evander_Holyfield "Evander Holyfield").[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-130)[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-131) On 20 November, Klitschko and Ibragimov officially signed the contract for their unification clash to take place on 23 February 2008 at [Madison Square Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madison_Square_Garden "Madison Square Garden").[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-132) Two days later in Moscow, a first pre-fight press-conference was held.[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-133) Klitschko began his preparations for the fight on 18 December. His training camp was located between [Santa Monica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santa_Monica "Santa Monica"), Los Angeles and [Palm Beach, Florida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palm_Beach,_Florida "Palm Beach, Florida").[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-134) Ibragimov began his preparations for the bout on 25 December. Among Ibragimov's sparring partners were Klitschko's former opponent [Jameel McCline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jameel_McCline "Jameel McCline") and Swedish heavyweight prospect [Attila Levin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Attila_Levin "Attila Levin").[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-135)[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-136)

In the pre-fight prediction, a vast majority of Ukrainian, Russian and American observers expected Klitschko to win by either stoppage or unanimous decision. Out of six journalists of the Ukrainian magazine _Ring_, five predicted Klitschko to stop Ibragimov, with only one expecting Klitschko to win by decision. 24 of 26 members of _boxingscene.com_ expected Klitschko to come out as the winner – 18 of them predicted the win to come by way of KO/TKO, one expert predicted decision, while the remaining five were unsure about either possibility. The remaining two experts predicted Ibragimov to win by decision. 10 of the 12 members of _ringsidereport.com_ picked Klitschko to win, with eight of them expecting the victory to come by way of KO/TKO. The remaining two picked Ibragimov to win by stoppage.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-137) In the build-up to the fight, Klitschko's trainer [Emmanuel Steward](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmanuel_Steward "Emmanuel Steward") said that Sultan Ibragimov was going to be Wladimir's toughest opponent to date, praising Ibragimov for his hand speed and mobility, while Klitschko complimented Ibragimov on his accomplishments: "Sultan Ibragimov is a boxer that hasn't lost in any of his 23 fights, with the sole draw being against [Ray Austin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Austin_(boxer) "Ray Austin (boxer)"). His amateur career can be described as fantastic, and the fact that he's the heavyweight champion of the world speaks volumes about his professional career as well. I think he's a strong and dangerous opponent that should not be underestimated. His last two fights against [Shannon Briggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shannon_Briggs "Shannon Briggs") and [Evander Holyfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evander_Holyfield "Evander Holyfield") proved that."[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-138) Ibragimov's trainer [Jeff Mayweather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Mayweather "Jeff Mayweather") was confident that Ibragimov would be able to establish his rhythm and "press Klitschko to the corner".[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-139) The pre-fight build-up was marked with controversy after Ibragimov's manager Boris Grinberg insulted Klitschko during one of the interviews: "Sultan Ibragimov knocks out this Ukraine gay, motherf***er!". Grinberg later apologised to Klitschko.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-140) The day before the bout, Klitschko weighed in at 238 pounds (108 kg), the lightest since 1999,[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-klitschko-record-141) while Ibragimov's weight was 219 pounds (99 kg), his lightest since 2005.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-ibragimov-record-142)

From the opening bell, both fighters fought tentatively, avoiding risks. Klitschko retreated onto [the outside](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boxing_styles_and_technique "Boxing styles and technique"), fighting at a distance and remaining unreachable for Ibragimov who tried to establish his right jab but had his right hand constantly pushed down by Klitschko. By the end of the opening round, Klitschko became more active with his jab, while Ibragimov unsuccessfully tried to catch Wladimir with a series of right and left hooks. By the third round, Klitschko took control of the center of the ring, keeping Ibragimov at the end of his left jab and occasionally throwing right jabs as well.[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-143) In the fifth round, Klitschko caught Ibragimov with a straight right hand, however Ibragimov appeared to be unhurt. Most of Ibragimov's attempts to close distance ended with Klitschko tying him up. In the second half of the fight, the situation did not change, with Klitschko keeping Ibragimov at distance with straight shots, while Ibragimov was only able to occasionally catch Klitschko with single shots to the body. Ibragimov's corner was almost silent from the sixth round onwards, unable to give their man any meaningful advice.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-144) Klitschko's dominance became even more visible after he caught Ibragimov with a straight right in round nine, almost knocking him down. He caught Ibragimov again with a counter left hook at the end of the eleventh. The twelfth round saw Ibragimov unsuccessfully trying to catch Klitschko with overhand shots. Ultimately, the fight went the distance, with Klitschko being declared the winner by unanimous decision. The judges scored the bout 119–110, 117–111 and 118–110.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-ibragimov-klitschko-gendlin-145)[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-ibragimov-klitschko-belenkyi-146)[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-ibragimov-klitschko-belenkyi2-147) Klitschko reportedly earned $9 million for the fight.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-sportarena.com-148)[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-sport.24tv.ua-149) He donated $500,000 of his earnings to the Bronx's Laureus Sport for Good Foundation.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-150)

The fight was heavily criticised by observers and prominent boxing public figures.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-ibragimov-klitschko-espn-151)[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-ibragimov-klitschko-guardian-152) Boxing promoter [Bob Arum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Arum "Bob Arum") called the fight "an absolute shame",[[148]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-153) while Dan Goossen described it as "awful".[[149]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-154) Boxing journalist Phil Santos pointed out that Klitschko fought for the majority of the fight "only with his left hand", proving once again that he "is the best heavyweight in the world right now". Santos also noted that such cautious, safety-first style was not going to help Klitschko to increase his popularity in the United States.[[150]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-155) Some observers were more apologetic of Klitschko's performance: "It's really irritating that so many people, people that know very little about boxing, say that Klitschko's dominance means stagnation for the heavyweight division. described Thompson as "one of the most difficult fights we will have".[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-thomspon-klitschko-eurosport-162)[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wladimir_Klitschko#cite_note-thomspon-klitschko-espn-163) **Semey** ([/s ɪ ˈ m eɪ,s ɛ-/](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/English "Help:IPA/English"); [Kazakh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazakh_language "Kazakh language"): Семей / Semei[[sʲɪˈmʲej]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Kazakh "Help:IPA/Kazakh")([listen](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/7/73/Kk-semey.ogg/Kk-semey.ogg.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kk-semey.ogg "File:Kk-semey.ogg")), formerly known as **Semipalatinsk** ([Russian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language "Russian language"): Семипалатинск[[sʲɪmʲɪpɐˈɫatʲɪnsk]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Russian "Help:IPA/Russian")) until 2007 and as **Alash-Qala** ([Kazakh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazakh_language "Kazakh language"): Алаш-қала / Alaş-qala[[ɑˌɫɑʃ‿qɑˈɫɑ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Kazakh "Help:IPA/Kazakh")) from 1917 to 1920, is a city in north-eastern [Kazakhstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazakhstan "Kazakhstan"), in the Kazakh part of [Siberia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siberia "Siberia"). When [Abai Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abai_Region "Abai Region") was created in 2022, Semey became its administrative centre. It lies along the [Irtysh River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irtysh_River "Irtysh River") near the border with [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russia "Russia"), 1,000 kilometers (620 mi) north of [Almaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaty "Almaty") and 700 kilometers (430 mi) southeast of the Russian city of [Omsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omsk "Omsk"). Its population is 312,764 (stat.gov.kz).

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Semey&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first Russian settlement in the area dates from 1718, when [Russia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsardom_of_Russia "Tsardom of Russia") built a fort beside the river [Irtysh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irtysh_River "Irtysh River"), near the ruins of an ancient [Buddhist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhist "Buddhist") monastery, where seven buildings could be seen. The fort (and later the city) was named _Semipalatinsk_ ([Russian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_language "Russian language") for "Seven-Chambered City") after the monastery. The fort suffered frequent flooding caused by snowmelt swelling the Irtysh.

In 1778 the fort was relocated 18 kilometres (11 mi) upstream to less flood-prone ground.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] A small city developed around the fort, and largely served the river trade between the nomadic peoples of [Central Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Asia "Central Asia") and the growing [Russian Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_Empire "Russian Empire"). The construction of the [Turkestan-Siberia Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkestan-Siberia_Railway "Turkestan-Siberia Railway") in the early 20th century added to the city's importance, making it a major point of transit between Central Asia and Siberia. On 19 May 1854, Semipalatinsk was designated as the capital of the [Semipalatinsk Oblast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipalatinsk_Oblast,_Russia "Semipalatinsk Oblast, Russia") within the Russian Empire.

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/71/Kazakh_intelligentsia_%281918%29.jpg/250px-Kazakh_intelligentsia_%281918%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Kazakh_intelligentsia_(1918).jpg)

Kazakh intelligentsia and members of the [Alash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alash_(party) "Alash (party)") party in Alash-Qala, 1918

The city was one of the main centers for the publication of books by the Kazakh [intelligentsia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligentsia "Intelligentsia").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipalatinsk#cite_note-2) Between 1917 and 1920, the city operated as the capital of the largely unrecognized [Alash Autonomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alash_Autonomy "Alash Autonomy"), a state (1917–1920) established after the outbreak of the [October Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/October_Revolution "October Revolution") in Russia. The city was called **Alash-qala** during the Alash Autonomy years. [Red Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Army "Red Army") forces loyal to [Petrograd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petrograd "Petrograd") took control of the area in 1920. It was the center of the [Semipalatinsk Governorate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipalatinsk_Governorate?action=edit&redlink=1 "Semipalatinsk Governorate (page does not exist)")[[ru](https://ru.wikipedia.org/wiki/%D0%A1%D0%B5%D0%BC%D0%B8%D0%BF%D0%B0%D0%BB%D0%B0%D1%82%D0%B8%D0%BD%D1%81%D0%BA%D0%B0%D1%8F%20%D0%B3%D1%83%D0%B1%D0%B5%D1%80%D0%BD%D0%B8%D1%8F "ru:Семипалатинская губерния")] until 17 January 1928, then of the [East Kazakhstan Oblast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Kazakhstan_Oblast "East Kazakhstan Oblast") between 17 January 1928 and 14 October 1939 and finally of the [Semipalatinsk Oblast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipalatinsk_Oblast,_Kazakhstan "Semipalatinsk Oblast, Kazakhstan") between 1939 and 1997.

During [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), in connection with the formation of the Polish [Anders' Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anders'_Army "Anders' Army"), a Polish diplomatic post was located in the city from October 1941 to July 1942.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipalatinsk#cite_note-3)

In 1949 the [Soviet atomic bomb programme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_atomic_bomb_project "Soviet atomic bomb project") selected a site on the [steppe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steppe "Steppe")180 km (110 mi) west of the city as the location for its weapons testing. For decades, [Kurchatov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kurchatov,_Kazakhstan "Kurchatov, Kazakhstan") (the secret city at the heart of the test range named for [Igor Kurchatov](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Kurchatov "Igor Kurchatov"), father of the Soviet atomic bomb) was home to many of the brightest stars of Soviet weapons science. The [Soviet Union](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soviet_Union "Soviet Union") operated the [Semipalatinsk Test Site](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipalatinsk_Test_Site "Semipalatinsk Test Site") (STS) from the first explosion in 1949 until 1989; 456 nuclear tests, including 340 underground and 116 atmospheric tests, took place there.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipalatinsk#cite_note-4)

Some land around Semey has suffered environmental and health effects from the time of its atomic prosperity: nuclear fallout from the atmospheric tests and uncontrolled exposure of the workers, some of whom lived in the area close to the testsite, have resulted in high rates of [cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancer "Cancer"), childhood [leukemia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leukemia "Leukemia"), and [birth defects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth_defect "Birth defect") among the residents of neighbouring villages.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipalatinsk#cite_note-5)

Modern Semey, a bustling university town, has a population exceeding 350,000. Because of its proximity to the Kazakh border with the Russian Federation, and the large scientific community attached to the STS labs and the university, which includes many Russians, Semey is said to have a more Russian character than other cities in Kazakhstan.

[Semipalatinsk Oblast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipalatinsk_Oblast,_Kazakhstan "Semipalatinsk Oblast, Kazakhstan") merged with the larger [East Kazakhstan Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Kazakhstan_Region "East Kazakhstan Region"), whose capital city is [Oskemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oskemen "Oskemen"), on 23 May 1997.

The [Semey Bridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semey_Bridge "Semey Bridge"), a suspension bridge across the Irtish River, connects the two major parts of Semey. It has a main span of 750 metres (2,460 ft) and a total length of 1,086 metres (3,563 ft).[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipalatinsk#cite_note-6) Construction began in 1998 and the bridge opened to traffic in November 2000.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipalatinsk#cite_note-7)

NASA satellite photo of Semey

In 2007 the Semipalatinsk City Council voted unanimously in favour of changing the name of the city to _Semey_. The Chairman said that existing name had negative associations because of the extensive atomic testing there.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipalatinsk#cite_note-8)

In March 2022, Semey was selected by [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Kazakhstan "President of Kazakhstan")[Tokayev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kassym-Jomart_Tokayev "Kassym-Jomart Tokayev") as the prospective capital of the new [Abai Region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abai_Region "Abai Region"). This came into force on 8 June 2022 when Abai Region became an official [Region of Kazakhstan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Regions_of_Kazakhstan "Regions of Kazakhstan").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipalatinsk#cite_note-9)

On October 12 2025, the city held its first [mayoral election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Semey_akim_election "2025 Semey akim election").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipalatinsk#cite_note-10)

## Climate

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Semey&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Climate")]

Semey has a cold [semi-arid climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-arid_climate "Semi-arid climate"), with warm summers and very cold winters. Precipitation is low for the whole year, except for July which has an average of 50 millimetres (2.0 in) compared to less than 30 millimetres (1.2 in) in other months. Snow is common, though light, in winter. The lowest temperature on record is −48.6°C (−55.5°F), recorded in November 1910, and the highest temperature is 42.5°C (108.5°F), recorded in August 2002.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipalatinsk#cite_note-pogoda-11)

Semey is situated at the [Turkestan–Siberia Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turkestan%E2%80%93Siberia_Railway "Turkestan–Siberia Railway") and offers connections to [Almaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Almaty "Almaty") (former [Alma-Ata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alma-Ata "Alma-Ata")), [Barnaul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnaul "Barnaul"), and [Novosibirsk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Novosibirsk "Novosibirsk"), among others.

Dostoevsky Literary Memorial Museum

The city has a museum to commemorate [Abay Qunanbayuli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abay_Qunanbayuli "Abay Qunanbayuli").

Both a museum and a street are named after Dostoyevsky. The Museum of F. M. Dostoevsky in Semey was opened on 7 May 1971. It was established by the Resolution of the Council of Ministers of the [Kazakh SSR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kazakh_SSR "Kazakh SSR") N 261. Of the seven museums devoted to Dostoevsky, this is the only one located outside Russia.
