**Peter Joseph Polaco** (born October 16, 1973) is an American [professional wrestler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestler "Professional wrestler"). He is best known for his appearances with [Extreme Championship Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extreme_Championship_Wrestling "Extreme Championship Wrestling") (ECW) and the [World Wrestling Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wrestling_Federation "World Wrestling Federation") (WWF) under the [ring name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_name "Ring name")**Justin Credible**.

Debuting in 1992, Polaco first came to prominence in 1994 when he debuted in the WWF as **Aldo Montoya**.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-owwIP-5) After leaving the WWF in 1997, he joined ECW and adopted the ring name "Justin Credible". He formed the [Impact Players](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_Players "Impact Players")[tag team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tag_team "Tag team") with [Lance Storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lance_Storm "Lance Storm") in 1999 and the duo won the [ECW World Tag Team Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECW_World_Tag_Team_Championship "ECW World Tag Team Championship") twice in 2000.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-impactplayers-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecwtag-7) Later that year, he won the ECW World Heavyweight Championship at [CyberSlam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CyberSlam_(2000) "CyberSlam (2000)") and held it for five months.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecwchampionship-8) He remained in the title contention until ECW folded in 2001 and competed in the last match of ECW. He then returned to WWF as a member of X-Factor and later [The Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Alliance_(professional_wrestling) "The Alliance (professional wrestling)") during the [Invasion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Invasion_(professional_wrestling) "The Invasion (professional wrestling)")[angle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Angle "Glossary of professional wrestling terms").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-xfactor-9) He later won the [Hardcore Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE_Hardcore_Championship "WWE Hardcore Championship")[eight times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_WWE_Hardcore_Champions "List of WWE Hardcore Champions") before departing in 2003.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-wwehardcore-10) He briefly returned to the renamed WWE in 2006 as part of the revived [ECW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECW_(WWE_brand) "ECW (WWE brand)")[brand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE_Brand_Extension "WWE Brand Extension").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-owwIP-5)

## Professional wrestling career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Credible&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Professional wrestling career")]

### Early career (1992–1994)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Credible&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Early career (1992–1994)")]

Polaco traveled to [Calgary, Alberta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calgary,_Alberta "Calgary, Alberta") in 1992 to train at the Hart Brothers Training Camp, nominally run by [Keith Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keith_Hart_(wrestler) "Keith Hart (wrestler)"). He was mainly trained by his future [tag team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tag_team "Tag team") partner, [Lance Storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lance_Storm "Lance Storm"), and [Chris Jericho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Jericho "Chris Jericho"), who both graduated the program the year before. After wrestling unpaid as **P. J. Walker**, and setting up the rings there for a time, he began working for [New England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England "New England")–based [wrestling promotions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling_promotion "Professional wrestling promotion"). [_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 1994, he also [worked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Work "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") a few matches as an enhancement talent in [World Championship Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Championship_Wrestling "World Championship Wrestling") (WCW).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-11)

### World Wrestling Federation (1993, 1994–1997)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Credible&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: World Wrestling Federation (1993, 1994–1997)")]

He began wrestling for the [World Wrestling Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wrestling_Federation "World Wrestling Federation") (WWF) as an [enhancement talent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Job_(professional_wrestling) "Job (professional wrestling)").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-OWOW-12) His first match was a loss to [Lex Luger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lex_Luger "Lex Luger") on the March 1, 1993, episode of _[Monday Night Raw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Raw "WWE Raw")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-wwf93-13) He continued to wrestle sporadically in the WWF throughout 1993 and 1994 losing to [Yokozuna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yokozuna_(wrestler) "Yokozuna (wrestler)"), [Bam Bam Bigelow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bam_Bam_Bigelow "Bam Bam Bigelow"), [Mr. Perfect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curt_Hennig "Curt Hennig"), [Diesel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Nash "Kevin Nash"), [Jeff Jarrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Jarrett "Jeff Jarrett"), [Owen Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owen_Hart "Owen Hart"), [Undertaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Undertaker_(wrestler) "Undertaker (wrestler)") and [Nikolai Volkoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikolai_Volkoff "Nikolai Volkoff"). He even scored an upset victory against [Irwin R. Schyster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Rotunda "Mike Rotunda") on the September 20, 1993, episode of _Raw_, after a distraction by [Razor Ramon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Hall "Scott Hall").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-wwf93-13)

In November 1994, Polaco was hired by [Pat Patterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Patterson_(wrestler) "Pat Patterson (wrestler)") to a full-time contract in the WWF. His [Portuguese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugal "Portugal") ancestry inspired the WWF to give him the soccer player [character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Gimmick "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") of **Aldo Montoya**. However the idea changed to the "[Portuguese Man O' War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_Man_O'_War "Portuguese Man O' War")" character since he didn't like soccer.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-14) He made his televised debut as a [fan favorite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face_(professional_wrestling) "Face (professional wrestling)") on the November 14 episode of _[Monday Night Raw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE\_Raw "WWE Raw")_, where he picked up a victory over [The Brooklyn Brawler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Lombardi "Steve Lombardi").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-15) He was once offered to be a part of the [Million Dollar Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Million_Dollar_Corporation "The Million Dollar Corporation") by [Ted DiBiase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_DiBiase "Ted DiBiase"). He refused and told him to "shove his money in his ear". His mask drew criticism by fellow wrestlers, who called it a "jockstrap". Polaco befriended [The Kliq](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Kliq "The Kliq"), an influential group of upper card wrestlers, after [Razor Ramon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scott_Hall "Scott Hall") offered to mentor him. Polaco made his [pay-per-view](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pay-per-view "Pay-per-view") debut at the [1995 Royal Rumble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Rumble_(1995) "Royal Rumble (1995)") as a participant in the [Royal Rumble match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Rumble#Match "Royal Rumble"). He lasted 13 minutes until he was eliminated by eventual winner [Shawn Michaels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shawn_Michaels "Shawn Michaels").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-16) Montoya suffered his first televised loss against [Mantaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mantaur "Mantaur") on the January 29 episode of _[Action Zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWF\_Action\_Zone "WWF Action Zone")_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-17) On the April 8 episode of _[Superstars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWF\_Superstars\_of\_Wrestling "WWF Superstars of Wrestling")_, Polaco defeated the [Intercontinental Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE_Intercontinental_Championship "WWE Intercontinental Championship")[Jeff Jarrett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeff_Jarrett "Jeff Jarrett") in a non-title match, which earned him a title shot against Jarrett for the Intercontinental Championship on the April 22 episode of _Superstars_, where Jarrett retained the title.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-18) Montoya appeared at the [In Your House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_Your_House "In Your House") pay-per-view, where he attempted to prevent Jarrett and [The Roadie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Road_Dogg "Road Dogg") from attacking Razor Ramon after a [handicap match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling_match_types#Handicap_match "Professional wrestling match types").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-19)

He made only one pay-per-view appearance in 1996 at the [Royal Rumble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Rumble_(1996) "Royal Rumble (1996)"), where he participated in the [Royal Rumble match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Rumble#Match "Royal Rumble"), where he lasted only two minutes until he was eliminated by [Tatanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tatanka_(wrestler) "Tatanka (wrestler)").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-20) His only highlight of the year was an upset victory against [Jerry Lawler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Lawler "Jerry Lawler") on the July 27 episode of _Superstars_, which he gained by [pinning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pin_(professional_wrestling) "Pin (professional wrestling)") Lawler with [Jake Roberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Roberts "Jake Roberts")' _[DDT](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DDT\_(professional\_wrestling) "DDT (professional wrestling)")_ finishing move. He lost to Lawler in a rematch on the August 5 episode of _Monday Night Raw_. After the match, Lawler poured [Jim Beam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Beam "Jim Beam") whiskey down his throat.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-21)

Throughout this time, Montoya became more of a lower card wrestler and even asked for his release in June 1997 when he was only being [booked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Book "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") twice a month.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-22) The WWF initially declined and sent him to a developmental promotion [United States Wrestling Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Wrestling_Association "United States Wrestling Association") in [Memphis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Memphis,_Tennessee "Memphis, Tennessee") to hone his skills, where he remained for seven weeks. He was then released on the condition that he could not work for rival promotion [World Championship Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Championship_Wrestling "World Championship Wrestling"), which was then luring wrestlers away from the WWF with the promise of larger salaries. Polaco was instead sent to [Extreme Championship Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extreme_Championship_Wrestling "Extreme Championship Wrestling") as part of a talent exchange between WWF and ECW.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-OWOW-12)

### Extreme Championship Wrestling (1997–2001)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Credible&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Extreme Championship Wrestling (1997–2001)")]

#### Undefeated streak and various feuds (1997–1999)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Credible&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Undefeated streak and various feuds (1997–1999)")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/29/Justin_Credible_in_ECW.jpg/250px-Justin_Credible_in_ECW.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Justin_Credible_in_ECW.jpg)

Polaco at an ECW event in 1998

Polaco joined ECW under the guidance of [booker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Book "Glossary of professional wrestling terms")[Paul Heyman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Heyman "Paul Heyman"), who promised to make him a star. He debuted in ECW as "PG-187" in a loss to [Chris Candido](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Candido "Chris Candido") on August 21, 1997.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-23) He later resumed his "PJ Walker" name. At [As Good as It Gets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECW_As_Good_as_It_Gets "ECW As Good as It Gets"), his [character](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Gimmick "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") was repackaged as he shaved his head and switched to a [grunge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grunge "Grunge") style of dress, and adopted a cocky, sneering, egomaniacal attitude. He was introduced by [Jason Knight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Knight_(wrestler) "Jason Knight (wrestler)"), who named him "Justin Credible" ("Just Incredible").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecw97-24) Credible defeated [Jerry Lynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Lynn "Jerry Lynn") by debuting a new [finisher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Finisher "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") called _[That's Incredible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piledriver\_(professional\_wrestling)#Kneeling\_reverse\_piledriver "Piledriver (professional wrestling)")_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecw97-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-25) He began an undefeated streak which included a notable win over [The Great Sasuke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Great_Sasuke "The Great Sasuke") on the October 24 episode of _[Hardcore TV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECW\_Hardcore\_TV "ECW Hardcore TV")_.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecw97-24) Credible suffered his first loss in ECW against [Mikey Whipwreck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikey_Whipwreck "Mikey Whipwreck") in his pay-per-view debut at [November to Remember](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_to_Remember_(1997) "November to Remember (1997)").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-26) Credible continued his [rivalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feud_(professional_wrestling) "Feud (professional wrestling)") with Whipwreck, beating him in televised rematches on _Hardcore TV_,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-OWOW-12) while losing again at [Better Than Ever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECW_Better_Than_Ever "ECW Better Than Ever").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-27)

Credible quickly became a rising [villain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heel_(professional_wrestling) "Heel (professional wrestling)") in the company and adopted [Nicole Bass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicole_Bass "Nicole Bass") as his bodyguard. He began his next major feud with the company's veteran [Tommy Dreamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Dreamer "Tommy Dreamer") in 1998.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecw98-28) Credible defeated Dreamer in a [first blood match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling_match_types#First_Blood_match "Professional wrestling match types") at February's [CyberSlam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CyberSlam_(1998) "CyberSlam (1998)") pay-per-view[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-29) but lost to him in a match at [Living Dangerously](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Living_Dangerously_(1998) "Living Dangerously (1998)").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-30) Polaco was attacked by his returning nemesis Mikey Whipwreck after the match.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecw98-28) The two resumed their rivalry as Credible defeated Whipwreck at [Wrestlepalooza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrestlepalooza_(1998) "Wrestlepalooza (1998)").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-31) During this time, Credible began a high-profile feud with Jerry Lynn as he lost to Lynn at [It Ain't Seinfeld](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It_Ain't_Seinfeld "It Ain't Seinfeld").[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-32) Credible defeated Lynn in a [two out of three falls match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling_match_types#Series_variations "Professional wrestling match types") at [A Matter of Respect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Matter_of_Respect_(1998) "A Matter of Respect (1998)")[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-33) and in a [standard one-on-one match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling_match_types#Singles_match "Professional wrestling match types") at the [Heat Wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_Wave_(1998) "Heat Wave (1998)") pay-per-view on August 2.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-34)

In the fall of 1998, Credible renewed his feud with Tommy Dreamer. He joined forces with [Jack Victory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jack_Victory "Jack Victory") and [Rod Price](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rod_Price_(wrestler) "Rod Price (wrestler)") against Dreamer and [The Gangstanators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Gangstanators "The Gangstanators") ([John Kronus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kronus "John Kronus") and [New Jack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jack "New Jack")) in a [Philly Street Fight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcore_wrestling "Hardcore wrestling") at the [UltraClash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UltraClash_(1998) "UltraClash (1998)") event, where his team lost.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-35) Polaco and Victory lost to Dreamer and [Jake Roberts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jake_Roberts "Jake Roberts") in a [tag team match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling_tag_team_match_types "Professional wrestling tag team match types") at the company's premier pay-per-view event [November to Remember](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_to_Remember_(1998) "November to Remember (1998)").[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-36) However, he defeated Dreamer in the first-ever [Stairway to Hell match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ladder_match "Ladder match") at the [Guilty as Charged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guilty_as_Charged_(1999) "Guilty as Charged (1999)") pay-per-view on January 10, 1999, thanks to interference by [Terry Funk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terry_Funk "Terry Funk").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecw99-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-38)

#### Impact Players (1999–2000)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Credible&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Impact Players (1999–2000)")]

Main article: [The Impact Players](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Impact_Players "The Impact Players")

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2b/Justin_Credible_in_December_1999.jpg/250px-Justin_Credible_in_December_1999.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Justin_Credible_in_December_1999.jpg)

Credible at an ECW show in December 1999

In the midst of his [rivalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feud_(professional_wrestling) "Feud (professional wrestling)") with [Tommy Dreamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Dreamer "Tommy Dreamer"), Polaco aligned himself with his mentor [Lance Storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lance_Storm "Lance Storm") after the duo lost a [three-way dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling_match_types#Basic_elimination_matches "Professional wrestling match types") against Dreamer at [House Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Party_(1999) "House Party (1999)").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-39) Storm and Credible continued to feud with Dreamer until the duo formed a [tag team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tag_team "Tag team") at [Crossing the Line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ECW_supercards_and_pay-per-view_events#1999 "List of ECW supercards and pay-per-view events") called [The Impact Players](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Impact_Players "The Impact Players"). They proclaimed themselves to be "New Franchise" after [Shane Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Douglas "Shane Douglas") teased his retirement but Douglas instead chose Dreamer as his successor.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-impactplayers-6)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecw99-37) Impact Players were defeated by Dreamer and Douglas at [Living Dangerously](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Living_Dangerously_(1999) "Living Dangerously (1999)") on March 21.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-40) Credible lost a match to Douglas at [CyberSlam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CyberSlam_(1999) "CyberSlam (1999)").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-41) The feud with Dreamer and Douglas ended when Douglas left the company in mid-1999.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecw99-37) Following Douglas' departure, Credible faced [Sid Vicious](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sid_Eudy "Sid Eudy") in a match at May's [Hardcore Heaven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcore_Heaven_(1999) "Hardcore Heaven (1999)"), which ended in a no contest.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-42)

Impact Players began dominating the [roster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Extreme_Championship_Wrestling_alumni "List of Extreme Championship Wrestling alumni") in singles and tag team competition and quickly earned main event status by feuding with the company's top wrestlers. They defeated [Jerry Lynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Lynn "Jerry Lynn") and [Sabu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabu_(wrestler) "Sabu (wrestler)") at the [Hostile City Showdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hostile_City_Showdown#1999 "Hostile City Showdown") event in June[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-43) while lost to Lynn and [Rob Van Dam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Van_Dam "Rob Van Dam") in the main event of [Heat Wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECW_Heat_Wave#1999 "ECW Heat Wave") pay-per-view on July 18.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-44) Polaco then embarked on a feud with Sabu, which culminated in a match between the two at September's [Anarchy Rulz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anarchy_Rulz_(1999) "Anarchy Rulz (1999)") pay-per-view, which Polaco won.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-45) Impact Players' next feud was with [The Sandman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman_(wrestler) "The Sandman (wrestler)") and the [ECW World Tag Team Champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECW_World_Tag_Team_Championship "ECW World Tag Team Championship") Tommy Dreamer and [Raven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raven_(wrestler) "Raven (wrestler)"). At [November to Remember](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_to_Remember_(1999) "November to Remember (1999)"), Impact Players teamed with [Rhino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhyno "Rhyno") against Sandman, Raven and Dreamer in a losing effort.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-46)

Impact Players continued their rivalry with Raven and Dreamer as they began pursuing the ECW World Tag Team Championship. On the January 7, 2000, episode of _ECW on TNN_, Credible defeated Dreamer in the second Stairway to Hell match.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecw99-37) Impact Players were [booked](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Book "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") to win the titles from Raven and Dreamer at [Guilty as Charged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guilty_as_Charged_(2000) "Guilty as Charged (2000)") on January 9, 2000.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecwtag-7)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-47) A month later, Impact Players [dropped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Drop "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") the titles to Dreamer and [Masato Tanaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masato_Tanaka "Masato Tanaka") on the March 3 episode of _[ECW on TNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECW\_on\_TNN "ECW on TNN")_.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecw2000-48) Shortly after, [Mike Awesome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Awesome "Mike Awesome") and Raven won the titles from Dreamer and Tanaka. At [Living Dangerously](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Living_Dangerously_(2000) "Living Dangerously (2000)"), Impact Players defeated both teams in a three-way dance to regain the World Tag Team Championship.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecwtag-7)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-49)

#### World Heavyweight Champion (2000–2001)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Credible&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: World Heavyweight Champion (2000–2001)")]

[![Image 7](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/49/Justin_Credible_in_August_2000_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Justin_Credible_in_August_2000_(cropped).jpg)

Justin Credible in August 2000 at [Midtown Massacre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midtown_Massacre "Midtown Massacre")

Polaco received the biggest [push](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Push "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") of his career at the [CyberSlam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CyberSlam_(2000) "CyberSlam (2000)") event on April 22, when he and [Jason](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Knight_(wrestler) "Jason Knight (wrestler)") attacked rival [Tommy Dreamer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Dreamer "Tommy Dreamer") and [Raven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raven_(wrestler) "Raven (wrestler)") after Dreamer defeated [Taz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tazz "Tazz") to win the [ECW World Heavyweight Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECW_World_Heavyweight_Championship "ECW World Heavyweight Championship"). He threw down his [ECW World Tag Team Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECW_World_Tag_Team_Championship "ECW World Tag Team Championship") belt and challenged Dreamer to defend the title against him on the spot to which Dreamer agreed. Polaco defeated Dreamer to win the title after Dreamer's [valet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manager_(professional_wrestling) "Manager (professional wrestling)")[Francine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francine_Fournier "Francine Fournier")[turned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Turn "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") on Dreamer.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecwchampionship-8)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecw2000-48)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-50) From this point, Francine became Credible's valet. Credible became a loyal ally of [The Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Network_(professional_wrestling) "The Network (professional wrestling)") and the top wrestler of the group. Upon winning the World Heavyweight Championship, Credible vacated his half of the World Tag Team Championship and berated his mentor and tag team partner [Lance Storm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lance_Storm "Lance Storm"), leading to a [rivalry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feud_(professional_wrestling) "Feud (professional wrestling)") between the two. At the [Hardcore Heaven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcore_Heaven_(2000) "Hardcore Heaven (2000)") pay-per-view, Credible was scheduled to defend the title against Dreamer and Storm in a [three-way dance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling_match_types#Basic_elimination_matches "Professional wrestling match types") but he refused to defend the title against anyone except Storm and threatened to throw the World Heavyweight Championship. Credible defended the title against Storm in a [singles match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling_match_types#Singles_match "Professional wrestling match types"), during which he injured Storm's valet [Dawn Marie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dawn_Marie "Dawn Marie") with a _[That's Incredible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piledriver\_(professional\_wrestling)#Kneeling\_reverse\_piledriver "Piledriver (professional wrestling)")_. Credible retained the title and was assaulted by Dreamer after the match.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecw2000-48)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-51) Credible successfully defended the title against Dreamer in the third [Stairway to Hell match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ladder_match "Ladder match") between the duo at [Heat Wave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heat_Wave_(2000) "Heat Wave (2000)").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-52)

Credible represented The Network with [Rhino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhyno "Rhyno") in a tournament for the vacant World Tag Team Championship in September. They defeated [The Sandman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman_(wrestler) "The Sandman (wrestler)") and [Chilly Willy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chilly_Willy_(wrestler) "Chilly Willy (wrestler)") in the first round before losing to Dreamer and [Jerry Lynn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Lynn "Jerry Lynn") in the quarterfinals. Credible defended his World Heavyweight Championship against Network's [Steve Corino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Corino "Steve Corino") on the September 15 _[ECW on TNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECW\_on\_TNN "ECW on TNN")_, during which Corino brought Dawn Marie as his valet, who had been injured by Credible at Hardcore Heaven. Credible managed to retain the title but it stirred up problems between Credible and Corino. Credible successfully defended the title against Corino and Jerry Lynn in an elimination match on the September 29 episode of _ECW on TNN_,[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecw2000-48) before losing the title to Lynn at [Anarchy Rulz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anarchy_Rulz_(2000) "Anarchy Rulz (2000)") on October 1 after being hit with his own move _That's Incredible_,[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecw2000-48)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-53) ending his five-month reign at [162 days](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ECW_World_Heavyweight_Champions "List of ECW World Heavyweight Champions").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecwchampionship-8)

Credible competed against Lynn, Corino and The Sandman for the title in a [Double Jeopardy match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professional_wrestling_match_types#Double_Jeopardy_match "Professional wrestling match types"), the following month at [November to Remember](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/November_to_Remember_(2000) "November to Remember (2000)"). Corino and Credible eliminated Sandman and Lynn respectively and then Corino defeated Credible to win the title.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-54) Credible faced Corino and Lynn in a three-way dance for the title at [Massacre on 34th Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massacre_on_34th_Street "Massacre on 34th Street"), where Corino retained the title.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-55) He received another opportunity for the title against Corino and Sandman in a [Tables, Ladders, Chairs and Canes match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tables,_Ladders_and_Chairs_match "Tables, Ladders and Chairs match") at the company's final pay-per-view [Guilty as Charged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guilty_as_Charged_(2001) "Guilty as Charged (2001)"), where Sandman won the title.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-56) He competed against Sandman in the final match in the history of ECW on January 13, 2001, which he won but offered a rematch, which he lost to Sandman.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-ecw2000-48)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-57)

### Return to World Wrestling Federation / World Wrestling Entertainment (2001–2003)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Credible&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Return to World Wrestling Federation / World Wrestling Entertainment (2001–2003)")]

Main article: [The Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Alliance_(professional_wrestling) "The Alliance (professional wrestling)")

With ECW facing imminent [bankruptcy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bankruptcy "Bankruptcy") and Paul Heyman becoming unable to pay the roster, Polaco returned to the WWF as Justin Credible in February 2001, immediately forming an alliance with [X-Pac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-Pac "X-Pac") and assisting him in his pursuit of the [WWF Intercontinental Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWF_Intercontinental_Championship "WWF Intercontinental Championship"). The duo eventually formed a [stable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glossary_of_professional_wrestling_terms#Stable "Glossary of professional wrestling terms") with [Albert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matt_Bloom "Matt Bloom") known as X-Factor. X-Pac and Credible tried several times to win the [WWF Tag Team Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWF_Tag_Team_Championship "WWF Tag Team Championship"), but were unsuccessful. The team split when Credible aligned himself with [Paul Heyman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Heyman "Paul Heyman")'s band of ECW insurgents and helped form [The Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Alliance_(professional_wrestling) "The Alliance (professional wrestling)") with [World Championship Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Championship_Wrestling "World Championship Wrestling") (WCW). Credible remained on the company's "B" shows, forming a team with [Raven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raven_(wrestler) "Raven (wrestler)"), until Team Alliance lost at [Survivor Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Survivor_Series_(2001) "Survivor Series (2001)").

Credible was fired along with the rest of the Alliance roster (in kayfabe) by [Vince McMahon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vince_McMahon "Vince McMahon") until [Ric Flair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ric_Flair "Ric Flair") was able to save his job and get him [drafted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2002_WWF_draft_lottery "2002 WWF draft lottery") over to the [Raw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raw_(WWE_brand) "Raw (WWE brand)")[brand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE_Brand_Extension "WWE Brand Extension") in March 2002. On the Raw brand, Credible wrestled mostly on _[Sunday Night Heat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunday\_Night\_Heat "Sunday Night Heat")_ and lost many singles matches he was in, but managed to become an eight-time [WWE Hardcore Champion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WWE_Hardcore_Champion "WWE Hardcore Champion"). His last match on _Raw_ was a [squash match](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squash_(professional_wrestling) "Squash (professional wrestling)") in which he was defeated by [Batista](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_Batista "Dave Batista"). Polaco was released on January 20, 2003, with his final televised WWE appearance being a loss to [Test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Test_(wrestler) "Test (wrestler)") on the December 8, 2002, episode of _Heat_.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-58)

### Independent circuit (2003–2006)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Credible&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Independent circuit (2003–2006)")]

Polaco wrestled for numerous [independent promotions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_circuit "Independent circuit"). He has appeared several times for [Ring of Honor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ring_of_Honor "Ring of Honor"), where he was a member of [The Carnage Crew](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Carnage_Crew "The Carnage Crew"), and for [Xtreme Pro Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xtreme_Pro_Wrestling "Xtreme Pro Wrestling"), where he feuded with [Shane Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shane_Douglas "Shane Douglas").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-PowerSlam109-59) He appeared with [Total Nonstop Action Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total_Nonstop_Action_Wrestling "Total Nonstop Action Wrestling") (TNA), forming a stable with several other ex-ECW wrestlers and reviving his feud with Jerry Lynn.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-PowerSlam109-59) He was also briefly a member of the [Xtreme Horsemen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xtreme_Horsemen "Xtreme Horsemen") in [Major League Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Major_League_Wrestling "Major League Wrestling") with [C. W. Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._W._Anderson "C. W. Anderson"), [Steve Corino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Corino "Steve Corino"), and [Simon Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pat_Kenney "Pat Kenney"), who were briefly managed by [J. J. Dillon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._J._Dillon "J. J. Dillon"). In June 2005, Polaco appeared in all _[Hardcore Homecoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcore\_Homecoming "Hardcore Homecoming")_ event. He was defeated by Jerry Lynn at June 10, by Sandman at September 15 and by Lynn again at September 18. He defeated Lynn at the final Hardcore Homecoming event in a Steel Cage match. Also, he interfered at [ECW One Night Stand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECW_One_Night_Stand_(2005) "ECW One Night Stand (2005)") match between his mentor Lance Storm and Chris Jericho, attacking Jericho with a kendo stick.

On November 13, 2005, Polaco, wrestling as P.J. Polaco, was announced as the "mystery opponent" for Raven on the TNA pay-per view, [Genesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genesis_(2005) "Genesis (2005)"). Polaco lost the match after Raven hit a DDT.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-60)

Credible signed a contract with the MTV "[Wrestling Society X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrestling_Society_X "Wrestling Society X")" stating that if MTV decided to turn the "one time special" into a full season, he would complete the season and would be un-able to compete anywhere else for that time period. He was released from his contract on June 5, 2006. Polaco was in the main event of the first Wrestling Society X Show, the WSX Rumble. He was the first person in the match and the last one eliminated. [_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Second return to World Wrestling Entertainment (2006)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Credible&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Second return to World Wrestling Entertainment (2006)")]

Polaco was rehired by [World Wrestling Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wrestling_Entertainment "World Wrestling Entertainment") in June 2006. He returned to WWE television at the June 7 _WWE vs. ECW Head to Head_ event as a member of the [ECW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECW_(WWE_brand) "ECW (WWE brand)") brand of WWE, taking part in a 20-man [battle royal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_royal_(professional_wrestling) "Battle royal (professional wrestling)").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-61) He made several appearances on _[ECW on Sci Fi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ECW\_on\_Sci\_Fi "ECW on Sci Fi")_ before being released from his WWE contract on September 28, 2006. During his brief WWE run he won two matches, both by disqualification defeating [Balls Mahoney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Balls_Mahoney "Balls Mahoney") and [Sabu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabu_(wrestler) "Sabu (wrestler)"). He also lost to [CM Punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CM_Punk "CM Punk") in Punk's ECW debut match.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-62)

### Return to the independent circuit (2006–present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Credible&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Return to the independent circuit (2006–present)")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Justin_Credible_%28Peter_Polaco%29_in_June_2007_%28cropped%29.JPG/250px-Justin_Credible_%28Peter_Polaco%29_in_June_2007_%28cropped%29.JPG?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Justin_Credible_(Peter_Polaco)_in_June_2007_(cropped).JPG)

Credible in 2007

Polaco returned to the independent circuit in 2006 using the name "Justin Time". He wrestled for the Pro Wrestling Syndicate promotion, along with fellow original ECW wrestlers [Sabu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sabu_(wrestler) "Sabu (wrestler)"), [Danny Doring](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Doring "Danny Doring") and [Julio Dinero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julio_Dinero "Julio Dinero"), as well as making appearances for the [Insane Clown Posse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insane_Clown_Posse "Insane Clown Posse") owned [Juggalo Championship Wrestling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juggalo_Championship_Wrestling "Juggalo Championship Wrestling"). On March 29, 2009, he became the Big Time Wrestling Champion, defeating "Hurricane" John Walters with Ric Flair as special guest referee, but Credible was stripped of the title in August of the same year. [_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Justin is also the topic of an upcoming documentary The Price of Fame which also includes [Ted DiBiase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_DiBiase "Ted DiBiase") and [Sean Waltman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Waltman "Sean Waltman"). He was inducted into the [New England Pro Wrestling Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_England_Pro_Wrestling_Hall_of_Fame "New England Pro Wrestling Hall of Fame") on July 12, 2009. On August 8, 2010, Polaco returned to TNA to take part in the ECW-themed pay-per-view [Hardcore Justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcore_Justice_(2010) "Hardcore Justice (2010)") where he performed as P.J. Polaco due to the WWE owning the rights to the Justin Credible name; Polaco was defeated by [Stevie Richards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Richards "Stevie Richards"). Afterwards, he was assaulted by former rival [The Sandman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sandman_(wrestler) "The Sandman (wrestler)") with a Singapore cane.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-63) On January 14, 2012, Credible returned to the former ECW Arena, when he was defeated by Sabu at an [Evolve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolve_(professional_wrestling) "Evolve (professional wrestling)") event in the venue's final professional wrestling match.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-64)

On April 28, 2012, Polaco was scheduled to wrestle on Shane Douglas' Extreme Reunion show, but was removed from the card, as well as the building after being found "slumped over, passed out asleep" in a chair. While he begged management to be let back on the show, they denied his request and kicked him out a second time.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] On August 8, 2012, [Chikara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chikara_(professional_wrestling) "Chikara (professional wrestling)") announced that Polaco, returning to his Aldo Montoya character, would be making his debut for the promotion in the following month's [2012 King of Trios tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_of_Trios#2012 "King of Trios"), where he would team with the [1-2-3 Kid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Waltman "Sean Waltman") and [Tatanka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tatanka_(wrestler) "Tatanka (wrestler)") as "Team WWF".[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-65) In their first round match on September 14, Team WWF was defeated by The Extreme Trio (Jerry Lynn, Tommy Dreamer and [Too Cold Scorpio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2_Cold_Scorpio "2 Cold Scorpio")).[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-66)[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-67)

Polaco retired on November 20, 2015, after facing long-time rival Tommy Dreamer at a Pro Wrestling Syndicate event.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-68) Credible came out of retirement and faced Matt Tremont in a winning effort at CZW show in August 2016.

In March 2017, he returned to wrestling, and teamed with The Sandman &[New Jack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jack "New Jack") in a winning effort at an ECPW show.

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Justin_Credible&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Polaco is of Portuguese ancestry. His parents emigrated to the United States from Portugal three years before he was born. He speaks Portuguese fluently. Polaco and his wife Jill Marie Polaco (née Jurecki) were married on June 4, 1997. They have three sons: Nicholas (born April 2000), Christian, and Jasper.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-69)

In 2018, Polaco was arrested three times between August and December for violating a protection order.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-70)

Polaco and writer/wrestler [Kenny Casanova](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenny_Casanova "Kenny Casanova") released the book _Just a Dream to... Justin Credible!_ in November 2021. It chronicled the personal life and wrestling career of Polaco up to that point.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-71)

In March 2025, [Maven Huffman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maven_Huffman "Maven Huffman"), fellow ex-WWE wrestler, conversed with Polaco as a follow-up to a significant number of accusations of Polaco failing to send merchandise to fans after receiving payment and no-showing independent shows, or showing up in a condition unsuited to perform. While Polaco refuted or denied various claims made, he would concede that there were some instances in which, "...by the time I buy food [with the money sent] I don't have the money to send it [the merchandise] ... I wasn't ready to do that, I wasn't equipped to do that".[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Credible#cite_note-73)
